latest.title: SMART RETAILING IN INTERNET COMMERCE: AN AI-ENABLED CUSTOMER-CENTRIC SERVICE FRAMEWORK
latest.venue: EPH - International Journal of Business & Management Science
latest.abstract: This conceptual paper examines AI-enabled smart retailing as a customer-facing service transformation in Internet commerce rather than as a narrow technological or operational innovation. Drawing on a selective, theory-driven synthesis of services marketing, smart retailing, AI-enabled marketing, customer experience, service-dominant logic, human–AI interaction, and responsible-AI research, it develops a three-layer framework linking AI-enabled service capabilities, customer-experience mechanisms, and Internet-commerce outcomes. The framework identifies three capability groups—algorithmic personalisation and decision support, AI-mediated service interaction, and predictive service intelligence—and four evaluative mechanisms: decision value, interaction quality, transaction confidence, and algorithmic legitimacy. These mechanisms shape customer satisfaction, engagement, service-recovery effectiveness, platform trust, relationship quality, continuance intention, value co-creation, and inclusive service value. Human–AI governance, including privacy protection, transparency, fairness, customer control, human review, and digital accessibility, is treated as a boundary condition that determines whether AI-enabled services are perceived as trustworthy and customer-centred or as intrusive, opaque, unfair, and exclusionary. The paper contributes to Internet-commerce research by repositioning AI as a service-enabling capability and by explaining how customer evaluations translate AI applications into commercial and relational outcomes. It also proposes a focused research agenda for empirical testing across e-commerce websites, mobile applications, online marketplaces, social-commerce platforms, and omnichannel systems.

latest.title: The relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust: brand credibility, emotional attachment, and perceived quality effects
latest.abstract: Introduction The purpose of this research was to explore the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Specifically, we developed a conceptual model which proposes that brand credibility has a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust, and that perceived quality and emotional attachment have mediating effects on brand trust. Methods We tested the conceptual model by conducting a 2 × 2 (low versus high brand ethicality and low versus high brand credibility) between-subjects experiment, with brand trust as the dependent variable. Data ( N = 208) were collected at a large university in Bangladesh, and were analysed using PLS-SEM. Results Results of the experiment suggest that brand ethicality has a direct effect on brand trust. Brand ethicality also enhances emotional attachment and perceived quality, which, in turn, lead to increased brand trust. Brand credibility, however, does not have a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Discussion Drawing on signalling theory, the findings provide causal evidence that brand ethicality builds brand trust through two parallel pathways: an affective pathway via emotional attachment and a cognitive pathway via perceived quality. Contrary to expectations, brand credibility did not act as a boundary condition, suggesting that brand ethicality and brand credibility may be better understood as sequential antecedents of brand trust rather than as interacting constructs. For practice, marketers ought to increase brand ethicality to increase brand trust, both directly and via emotional attachment and perceived quality.

latest.title: Self-pleasure vs conformity: understanding Chinese Gen Z consumption behaviors in the smart electronics market
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explain how Chinese Generation Z consumers construct preferences by moving between conformity and self-pleasure across a digitally mediated smart-appliance journey. Design/methodology/approach An abductive qualitative design combines 48 in-depth interviews (16 each for smart kitchen appliances, floor-mopping robots and smart toilets) with consumer journey mapping. Self-determination theory, conformity theory, social comparison theory and constructive consumer choice guide cross-case interpretation. Findings Retrospective accounts suggest a transition consistent with comparison-mediated internalization. Social cues first reduce uncertainty; social comparison can then convert visible choices into personally relevant benchmarks. Research and use build competence and perceived fit, allowing autonomy and experiential satisfaction to become more influential. Post-purchase sharing satisfies relatedness and renews social influence. Two category attributes shape the path: decision risk/technical complexity and social visibility/identity expressiveness. Practical implications Brands should use credible social proof for discovery, comparison support for evaluation, reliable experiences for use and context-appropriate advocacy mechanisms after purchase. Originality/value The study distinguishes the roles of conformity, social comparison and self-determination within a process model and identifies category conditions associated with differences in reported movement from external referencing to self-endorsed choice.

latest.title: Promotion-rule Complexity and Checkout Abandonment in E-commerce Sales Events: The Mediating Role of Consumer Confusion
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: With the rise of big e-commerce sales events, multiple layers of promotions exist, such as platform coupons, store coupons, stacking, membership discounts and category discounts, which make the checkout process more complex. Promotional mechanisms can help to make the product more attractive, but can also diminish price transparency and add to cognitive load. This research examines the relationship between promotion-rule complexity and consumer checkout abandonment tendency and the role of consumer confusion in this relationship. A mixed-method approach was adopted to analyze a publicly available dataset of 12,330 online shopping sessions, and a survey based on a set of scenarios with 218 valid responses. The findings show that the complexity of the promotion rule has a significant effect on consumer confusion, which consequently results in a higher checkout abandonment tendency. Promotion-rule complexity is positively related to checkout abandonment through consumer confusion. The results contribute to the promotion literature by focusing on the last mile of the promotion process and have implications for e-commerce platforms that aim to minimise the friction involved in decisions by creating simpler rules and more transparent pricing.

latest.title: Digital Word of Mouth and Brand Trust
latest.venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
latest.abstract: The increasing expansion of social media, E-commerce and review websites has transformed how consumers look for and share information related to brands. Complementarily, eWOM — digital word-of-mouth — is consumer driven discussions regarding products, services, brands and companies that work through digital platforms. In contrast with the conventional word-of-mouth, communications shared via the digital medium can rapidly spread to a large audience and still remain accessible for a longer period This review discusses about some of the existing studies available on digital word-of-mouth, brand trust and consumer behaviour. Precisely , the review pays heavy attention on the online reviews, information authenticity, positive and negative eWOM, purchase intention and buyer behaviour. Previous studies indicate that the quality and usefulness of eWOM can influence consumer information and purchasing decisions , Nonetheless the effect of Ewom may also depend on the quality and characteristics of te information. The Research indicates that consumer trust and buying intentions can be influenced by how a brand reacts to negative reviews. The review highlights that digital word-of-mouth has now been an important factor into the consumer decision-making process and the authenticity of the reviews and also talks about the fake reviews and their impacts.

latest.title: Co-designing with Generative AI: consumer participation behaviour and product authenticity
latest.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping consumer–brand interactions, with fashion brands increasingly adopting Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) co-design tools that enable direct consumer participation in product design. This research examines how consumers evaluate the authenticity of the GenAI co-designed products, and how evaluation influences consumers’ future participation with fashion brands. This study further investigates whether consumer self-efficacy and perceived expertise toward the tools serve as key antecedents of the authenticity perceptions. By focusing on an emerging AI-enabled service (GenAI) context, this study expands consumer participation and value co-creation research by offering new insight into the drivers and consequences of the perceived authenticity of the fashion products co-created by GenAI and consumers.

latest.title: A consumer neuroscience approach to examining how augmented reality and QR codes support product and brand sustainability communication in retail settings
latest.abstract: This research explores the use of Augmented Reality (AR) and Quick Response (QR) codes as tools for communicating sustainability-related information in a quasi-realistic retail setting. It combines neurophysiological and self-report measures to investigate how these technologies influence consumers’ sustainability perceptions, emotional engagement, and cognitive workload. Participants took part in a simulated shopping experience, where they were exposed to one of three experimental conditions: traditional packaging, smartphone-mediated QR code scanning, and smartphone-mediated Augmented Reality exploration of coffee packaging. Cognitive workload (measured via electroencephalography) and emotional engagement (measured via skin conductance and heart rate) were recorded alongside self-report measures of green company orientation (GCO), green product informativeness (GPI), and brand familiarity. Findings indicate that while both AR and QR codes evoke more positive emotions and lead to higher perceptions of GCO and GPI, AR usage is also associated with higher cognitive workload. Additionally, brand familiarity enhanced self-report scores but not neurophysiological ones, without interacting with the interaction modality. This research provides a multi-level (implicit neurophysiological and explicit self-reported) perspective on the impact of digital packaging formats on sustainability communication. The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on how interactive technologies can support effective communication, implicit emotions, and consumer engagement with sustainability in retail environments.

latest.title: Different Strokes for Different Folks: Exploring Algorithmic Fairness and Trust in Generative Artificial Intelligence
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is widely used to personalize recommendations, yet questions remain about the representativeness of algorithmic recommendations to recognize diverse consumer needs. This research integrates the stimulus‐organism‐response model and social identity theory to inform how personalization influences recommendation acceptance through algorithmic fairness and trust and how communication style affects these processes, which may differ between ethnic groups. Using a sequential explanatory design, Study 1 ( n = 136) shows that high personalization increases recommendation acceptance, perceived algorithmic fairness and trust compared with low personalization based on an experiment. Study 2 ( n = 300) identifies a positive sequential indirect effect through algorithmic fairness and trust, with competence‐oriented communication producing a stronger effect than warmth‐oriented communication based on an experiment. Study 3 ( n = 340) further reveals differences in these relationships across ethnic groups using a quasi‐experiment. Study 4 ( n = 14) employs semi‐structured interviews to contextualize these findings and explore the underlying reasoning. Theoretically, the findings extend GenAI personalization literature by identifying fairness and trust as key pathways to recommendation acceptance and highlighting ethnic differences in these processes. Practically, the findings guide strategies for GenAI developers to create more equitable and context‐sensitive design across diverse consumers.

latest.title: AI Personalization and Travel Booking Intention in GenAI-Assisted Travel Planning: The Roles of Recommendation Relevance, Perceived Decision Autonomy, and Travel Decision Satisfaction
latest.venue: Advances in management and applied economics
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationships among AI personalization, recommendation relevance, perceived decision autonomy, travel decision satisfaction, and travel booking intention in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)-assisted travel planning. An online survey using convenience sampling yielded 348 valid responses from consumers in Taiwan aged 20 years and older with experience using GenAI for travel planning. Structural equation modeling was used to test seven hypotheses. The model demonstrated good fit, and six hypotheses were supported. AI personalization was positively associated with recommendation relevance and perceived decision autonomy. Recommendation relevance was positively associated with perceived decision autonomy, and both constructs were positively associated with travel decision satisfaction. The direct association between perceived decision autonomy and travel booking intention was not significant after accounting for travel decision satisfaction. The path from travel decision satisfaction to travel booking intention had the largest standardized coefficient. These findings distinguish perceived personalization from recommendation relevance and clarify the different roles of autonomy and satisfaction in travel decision-making. For practitioners, the findings suggest that tourism platforms and GenAI service providers should offer recommendations aligned with consumers’ needs, preserve their autonomy over choices, and improve the decision-making experience. The study provides evidence to inform the design of GenAI travel recommendation services. JEL classification numbers: D12, L83, O33. Keywords: Generative artificial intelligence, AI personalization, Perceived decision autonomy, Travel booking intention.

latest.title: Understanding digital purchase intentions: trust, scarcity marketing, and fomo among generation z
latest.venue: ECOBIZTECH Journal of Economics Business and Technology
latest.abstract: Purpose: to analyze the effects of trust, scarcity marketing, and fear of missing out (fomo) on generation z's purchase intention toward tiktok live shopping in Kendal regency. Method: this study used a quantitative approach and a survey method involving 100 generation z respondents in Kendal regency who had watched tiktok live shopping within the previous three months. Respondents were selected through purposive and snowball sampling techniques. Primary data were collected using an online questionnaire with a five-point likert scale and analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS version 27. Data analysis included validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, and hypothesis testing (t-test, F-test, and adjusted R²). Findings: trust, scarcity marketing, and fomo have positive and significant effects on generation z's purchase intention toward tiktok live shopping. All three variables significantly influence purchase intention, with fomo and scarcity marketing showing stronger effects than trust. The findings highlight the importance of functional, conditional, and social values in shaping generation z's digital purchasing behavior. Implications: this study encourages businesses to build trust, apply transparent scarcity promotions, and strengthen social engagement to increase purchase intention. Originality: lies in integrating trust, scarcity marketing, and fomo within the consumption value theory framework to explain generation z's purchase intention toward tiktok live shopping in Kendal regency.

latest.title: AI as Psychological Surrogate in Consumer Search: A Conceptual Framework and Future Research Directions
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Advanced artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are becoming ubiquitous in consumers' lives and search activities. AI applications that can create content, have conversations, respond to emotions, recognize images and objects, and construct real‐world experiences (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Google Lens, Apple Vision Pro) are transforming consumer search by functioning as psychological surrogates that assume key cognitive, evaluative, perceptual, and relational processes on consumers' behalf. Yet limited research has examined how these technologies transform the psychological mechanisms underlying consumer search. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic narrative review of 75 articles on the psychological foundations of consumer search and introduces the concept of AI psychological surrogacy, which happens when advanced‐AI technologies assume key psychological processes traditionally performed by humans. We develop a conceptual framework that theorizes AI psychological surrogacy across three higher‐order systems (affective‐relational delegation, cognitive‐evaluative substitution, and sensory‐perceptual construction) and six mechanisms: affective transference, relational surrogacy, cognitive delegation, evaluative surrogacy, perceptual offloading, and sensory augmentation. We advance six research propositions and a research agenda for investigating how reliance on AI as a psychological surrogate may alter consumer cognition, evaluation, perception, and relational dynamics.

latest.title: Time Pressure and Impulse Buying: The Mechanism of Limited-Time E-Commerce Promotions in Shaping Consumer Decision-Making
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: Time-limited offers are ubiquitous in online retail, and it is important to understand how they operate and the risks they pose. Drawing on behavioural economics and cognitive psychology, this study uses Tmall's Double-11, Pinduoduo's "flash sales" and Amazon Prime Day as examples, and argues that multi-modal interface signals, such as the countdown clock, real-time inventory, and transaction volume displayed, can narrow the window of consumer deliberation and encourage more impulsive purchases. Although such designs may improve conversion performance, they also create structural vulnerabilities, such as manufactured scarcity in the interface, consumer cognitive overload and irrational herd behaviour resulting in over-buying. When misused, the application of these interfaces can be a form of psychological coercion. To mitigate these risks, the paper suggests three solutions: adding standardised interface rules with independent third-party audits to remove false urgency; enhancing the chances of cooling off and reducing information overload on the pages; and reducing social-proof cues and including rational-consumption reminders to prevent unnecessary spending. The research is both theoretically and practically relevant in terms of balancing commercial efficiency with consumer protection, and it probably has long-term consequences in terms of the sustainability of the e-commerce industry.

latest.title: Too Old to Benefit From FinTech ? An Exploratory Study on Older Adults' Access to and Adoption of Robo‐Advice
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Robo‐advice has the potential to provide affordable financial advice to assist older adults with building and managing retirement income. Yet robo‐advice uptake among those aged 60 to 80 years is low, and little is known about how they engage with robo‐advice. Our study examines the drivers and barriers to robo‐advice access and adoption among older adults, and provides practical recommendations for industry and policymakers. Drawing on qualitative surveys and interviews with academic and industry experts familiar with the Australian financial advice landscape. We identify six core themes and their possible interrelationships, which likely affect older adults' access and adoption: robo‐advice design, digital and financial capabilities, trust, psychological comfort, regulatory deficiencies, and social influence. In integrating our findings with the technology acceptance and financial planning literature, we construct a conceptual framework that responds to calls for more comprehensive explanations of consumer behavior toward robo‐advice.

latest.title: Comparative Analysis Between Subscription Economy and Ownership: A New Consumer Behavioral Model
latest.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
latest.abstract: Subscription-based services are increasingly significant in today’s economy, offering ongoing value to consumers while ensuring consistent revenue for businesses. Understanding consumer behavior within this framework is crucial for improving service offerings and fostering customer loyalty. This study examines the key factors influencing consumer decisions in subscription-based services. Using an exploratory approach, both qualitative and quantitative data are analyzed to identify patterns and motivations behind consumer choices. The analysis focuses on the impact of pricing structures, service quality, engagement strategies, and psychological factors on purchasing behavior. The findings offer actionable insights for service providers, highlighting strategies to enhance customer acquisition and retention. This research emphasizes the complexity of consumer behavior in the subscription economy and provides guidance for developing more effective business strategies.

latest.title: The Bandwagon Effect and Cognitive Biases in Internet-Famous Restaurant Choice: A Mechanism of Distorted Consumer Decision-Making
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: The selection of dining venues increasingly relies on user-generated content (UGC) on local-life platforms. The check-in practice of internet-famous restaurants is not just a dining-related behavior anymore, but rather a dual behavior including experiential consumption and online identity performance. This paper examines how the bandwagon effect, compounded by three cognitive biases, shapes restaurant choice, drawing on publicly observable UGC from Xiaohongshu and Dianping. Unlike the previous studies, which mainly repeat the conclusion of conformity effect, the current paper makes a clear difference between the informational bandwagon, which is derived from genuine consumer experience, and the commercial bandwagon created by marketing activities. In addition, it reveals how representativeness bias, confirmation bias, and availability bias successively exert their effects at each stage of the entire consumer decision process: information exposure, preference formation, pre-consumption expectation formation, and post-purchase feedback. However, it generates systematic mistakes in decision-making as well. Commercial bandwagon signals and the cognitive biases they exploit distort dining choices, inflate expectations, and misallocate capital. The paper proposes a three-party remedy: consumer psychological literacy, platform governance reform, and a merchant reorientation toward core-product value. The study extends consumer-behavior theory and yields operational guidance for sustaining the local catering market.

latest.title: Ảnh hưởng của video được tạo bởi AI trên TikTok đến ý định mua hàng trực tuyến của thế hệ Gen Z tại Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh
latest.venue: Technical Education Science/Giáo dục Kỹ thuật
latest.abstract: Mặc dù nội dung do trí tuệ nhân tạo tạo ra (AIGC) đang bùng nổ tại thị trường Việt Nam, các nghiên cứu hiện hành chủ yếu tập trung vào các lĩnh vực chung mà chưa nhắm tới nền tảng cụ thể là TikTok. Do đó, vẫn còn khoảng trống nghiên cứu về định dạng video AI ngắn trên TikTok. Dựa trên khung lý thuyết SOR, nghiên cứu này đánh giá tác động của năm đặc tính video AI (tính xác thực, giải trí, thông tin, cá nhân hóa và rủi ro cảm nhận) đến ý định mua hàng trực tuyến của Gen Z thông qua vai trò trung gian là thái độ đối với video AI. Dữ liệu thu thập từ 251 người dùng tại Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh được xử lý thông qua việc đo lường PLS-SEM trên phần mềm SmartPLS 4 và hồi quy trung gian bằng PROCESS Macro (Bootstrap 5.000 mẫu). Kết quả cho thấy cả năm yếu tố đều có tác động ý nghĩa đến thái độ, trong đó tính giải trí và tính xác thực là hai động lực thúc đẩy mạnh mẽ nhất. Ngược lại, rủi ro cảm nhận lại tạo ra rào cản tiêu cực. Đáng chú ý là thái độ đóng vai trò trung gian một phần đối với tính xác thực, giải trí, thông tin, và trung gian hoàn toàn đối với tính cá nhân hóa và rủi ro cảm nhận. Nghiên cứu đóng góp vào lý thuyết hành vi người tiêu dùng số và cung cấp hàm ý chiến lược về ứng dụng AI trong truyền thông, định hướng đào tạo kỹ năng số và quản trị rủi ro công nghệ.

latest.title: Emotion Driven Biases in Consumer Decision Making: A Study on Cross Border Hand Made Y2K Retro Jewellery Consumption
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: Against a backdrop of intensifying cross-cultural exchange, emotion-driven decision-making bias is particularly salient in the rapidly expanding market for cross-border Y2K retro handmade jewellery. Integrating the affect-heuristic perspective and cross-cultural consumption frameworks, grounded in the affect heuristic—which posits that affective reactions serve as informational shortcuts in judgment—and cross-cultural consumption theory, this article investigates how combined emotions of nostalgia, exotic curiosity and identity -seeking produce consumer cognitive biases and various corresponding market outcomes. The current research points out both the positive functions, such as the promotion of cultural diversity and the empowerment of micro-creators, with three important issues: the distortions of the willingness to pay due to over-estimation of emotions, misinterpretations of cross-cultural aesthetics causing substantial returns, and impulsive spending amplified by social media. The study has also developed some solutions, including the application of ethical norms in marketing, visualization tools based on AR technologies, and the education of consumers in digital emotional literacy. The research has extended the affect-heuristic approach beyond the context of domestic retail by applying it to the sphere of transnational consumption and offered useful solutions for artisans, platforms, and lawmakers aimed at developing proper approaches to promote cross-national trade, which support sustainable retro shopping activities.

latest.title: One City, Two Kinds of Time: Why Warehouse Clubs and Community Hard Discounters Can Coexist in Shanghai
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Taking the juxtaposition of Sam's Club and Aldi in Shanghai as a case, this paper asks how two almost opposite retail models can take root and earn a profit in the same city. Existing explanations appeal to purchasing power, to format positioning, or to the capabilities of foreign firms. This paper proposes a three-part structure of time, space and symbol. Sam's Club sells "two hours of the weekend"; Aldi sells "fifteen minutes after work." The first rests on the car-borne ring beyond the outer ring road, the second on the walkable ring inside it. The first manufactures institutional trust — "I chose the right system" — through a membership card; the second manufactures price transparency — "I was not taken in" — through the price tag. The three structures reinforce one another and jointly lower the consumer's cost of choosing. Shanghai can hold both kinds of time not because it is richer but because four conditions hold at once: a thick and continuous middle in the income distribution, a sharply layered urban space, a supply chain in the Yangtze River Delta close at hand, and small, ageing households that arrived earlier than elsewhere. The paper further argues that the two firms are not each other's principal rival. Their common opponent is a retail environment of low price, low quality and low trust, and their boundary lies not in format but in whether a city still contains enough people willing to pay for certainty. Author: Ao Zhang, independent researcher; MA, Communication and Media Studies, Monash University. Data and disclaimer: Data as of 4 November 2026. Amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated. This is independent research; it does not constitute investment advice.

latest.title: Can the outcomes of transparent packaging be measured? A primary attempt at item screening
latest.abstract: Packaging has a significant impact on consumer choice and product purchase. Since almost all studies in this field have been conducted experimentally, this study aims to identify appropriate items to measure the outcomes of packaging transparency so that future researchers can use it in descriptive survey studies. This study was conducted using a mixed method (qualitative-quantitative) with the opinions of marketing and packaging experts. Concepts related to the meaning of transparent packaging were extracted from related studies using content analysis in the qualitative stage. Then, an online questionnaire was designed, and its link was provided to the panel members. Eleven concepts that expressed packaging transparency were extracted in the qualitative section, of which nine items were finally used in the quantitative section in the form of a questionnaire. Data were analyzed using SPSS and Excel. Lawshe’s (1975) content validity ratio (CVR) method was used to assess the usefulness of the items, and five items were identified as suitable for measuring the outcomes of packaging transparency. These items relate to the visibility of the packaging contents, trust in product quality, willingness to purchase, preference for seeing the actual contents rather than an image on the package, and preference for buying products with transparent packaging.

latest.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Digital Marketing Strategies for Enhancing Sales Conversion in E-Commerce: An Empirical and Analytical Investigation
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of global e-commerce has intensified competition for consumer attention, rendering traditional demographic-segmented and rule-based marketing increasingly ineffective. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative paradigm in digital marketing, enabling firms to process high-velocity behavioral datasets and deliver hyper-personalized customer journeys in real time. While industry adoption of AI marketing tools is widespread, a substantial maturity gap persists between experimental deployment and fully scaled conversion optimization. This paper integrates a multi-stage analytical research design—combining psychometric Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) of consumer survey data ($N = 420$), econometric before-and-after funnel cohort modeling across retail deployments, and regression-based moderation analysis—to quantify how AI-enabled digital marketing drives sales conversion. Specifically, the study examines four core strategic pillars: neural recommendation engines, predictive programmatic acquisition, dynamic pricing optimization, and generative conversational AI. Analytical results demonstrate that Perceived Personalization significantly enhances Customer Experience Quality ($\beta = 0.499, p < 0.001$) and Digital Marketing Effectiveness ($\beta = 0.488, p < 0.001$), which jointly mediate downstream Purchase Intention and actual checkout conversion ($R^2 = 0.412$). Econometric cohort tracking further reveals a 23.4% to 31.0% relative lift in session-to-purchase conversion rates, a 27% reduction in bounce rates, and up to a 50% increase in Average Order Value (AOV) via real-time affinity bundling. latest.title: An Examination of Key Organizational Drivers, Strategic Leadership Practices and Best Practices for Enhancing Organizational Effectiveness
latest.abstract: This qualitative study explores the key drivers and best practices for building a strong organizational culture within private sector organizations in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. Recognizing that organizational culture significantly influences employee engagement, performance, and retention, the research seeks to understand how culture is formed, sustained, and adapted in contemporary work environments. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews with 18 professionals occupying leadership, HR, and managerial roles across six private organizations. Using thematic analysis, six core themes emerged: Leadership Influence, Recruitment and Cultural Fit, Recognition and Motivation, Culture in Hybrid Work Models, Technology and Culture Transmission, and Feedback Loops and Culture Assessment. The findings highlight the central role of leadership in modeling and reinforcing cultural values, the importance of value-based recruitment in maintaining cultural coherence, and the critical need for recognition systems that reflect organizational priorities. Additionally, the study reveals how hybrid work and digital platforms have redefined cultural expression and interaction. Regular feedback mechanisms emerged as vital tools for assessing and refining culture in dynamic business contexts. This study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on organizational behavior by offering practical recommendations for cultivating resilient and high-performing workplace cultures. It also identifies areas for future research, including sector-specific analysis, longitudinal studies, and quantitative validation of cultural indicators.

latest.title: Rating–text inconsistency, purchase verification and online review helpfulness
latest.abstract: Background Online reviews combine star ratings, written evaluations and platform source cues. This study examines the association between rating–text inconsistency and review helpfulness across purchase-verification groups. Methods This observational study uses 479,493 reviews from six Amazon Reviews’23 categories over 2019–2022. A supervised text model was trained on product-disjoint data. Its calibrated test mean absolute error was 0.474 rating points. Helpful-vote counts were modelled using Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood with product-clustered confidence intervals. Rating indicators, product fixed effects and exploratory specification checks were examined. Results The model-based discrepancy was positively associated with helpful votes in the pooled model (incidence rate ratio = 1.37, 95% confidence interval [1.25, 1.50]). The unverified-review slope was not significant with product and rating fixed effects (incidence rate ratio = 1.025, p = .822). Directional contrasts changed when endpoint ratings were excluded. The verification interaction was negative in the full-sample model ( b = −0.387, p < .001). It was not significant in the product fixed-effects model ( b = 0.117, p = .346). In the two-to-four-star restriction, the pooled M1 association was not statistically significant (IRR = 1.059, p = .067). In the post hoc human-coding diagnostic, model-based and human-implied absolute discrepancies showed limited correspondence (Spearman correlation = 0.234). Conclusions The findings concern a model-based discrepancy measure. Directional patterns and verification moderation depend on the specification and rating range. latest.title: Research on the Interactive Relationship between Consumer Psychology and Behavior under the Trend of Commodity Sustainability
latest.venue: Frontiers in Business Economics and Management
latest.abstract: Against the backdrop of global green transformation and domestic dual carbon goals, Commodity Sustainability has become an important development direction for the consumer market. Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this paper aims to clarify the intrinsic relationship between consumer psychology and behavior by adopting literature analysis and empirical survey data analysis methods, combined with authoritative consumer research data, to explore the interaction mechanism and practical constraints between the two under the trend of Commodity Sustainability. Research has shown that consumers' Behavioral Attitude (BA), subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control can positively promote sustainable consumption, while behavioral practice can in turn reinforce their green consumption cognition; the current sustainable consumption still faces problems such as cognitive and behavioral disconnect, and external constraints. Based on this, this article proposes a targeted optimization path, which can provide a theoretical and empirical reference for the formulation of sustainable marketing for enterprises and the government to improve relevant supporting policies, and help promote the standardized development of the domestic sustainable consumption market.

latest.title: The Psychological Mechanisms of Scarcity Marketing on Gen Z Impulse Buying Behavior in Malaysia: A Conceptual Framework
latest.abstract: Scarcity marketing has become a dominant persuasive strategy in digital retail, yet its psychological impact on Generation Z consumers in Malaysia remains underexplored. This concept paper proposes a conceptual framework examining the psychological mechanisms through which scarcity marketing influences impulse buying behavior among Malaysian Gen Z consumers. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and integrating Commodity Theory and Social Comparison Theory, the framework posits that three scarcity marketing stimuli—time-limited, quantity-limited, and social proof scarcity—activate four psychological mediators: fear of missing out (FOMO), competitive arousal, perceived urgency, and social comparison, which subsequently drive impulse buying behavior. The framework further proposes that self-control, digital literacy, financial literacy, and brand trust moderate these relationships. Drawing upon a systematic review of literature from 2017 to 2026, this paper synthesizes empirical evidence demonstrating that FOMO exerts the strongest mediating influence on impulse buying, while self-control consistently weakens the relationship between psychological mediators and behavioral outcomes. The proposed framework contributes to consumer behavior theory by clarifying the mediating pathways and boundary conditions of scarcity marketing effects and offers practical implications for marketers, policymakers and consumer educators in developing responsible marketing practices and targeted digital literacy interventions. Empirical validation through quantitative survey methods targeting 400 Malaysian Gen Z consumers aged 18–27 is proposed to test the hypothesized relationships using Structural Equation Modelling.

latest.title: Exploring Traditional and Contemporary Retail Factors Shaping Customer Perceptions of Organised Retailing in Thanjavur District, Tamil Nadu
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
authors: S. Rashiya and Dr. T. Priyanga
latest.abstract: Organised retailing in India’s semi-urban and district-level markets is shaped by both established store-based attributes and emerging technology-enabled attributes. This study identifies and empirically validates the traditional and contemporary factors that shape customer perception of organised retailing in Thanjavur District, Tamil Nadu. Data were collected from 536 respondents using a structured questionnaire comprising 40 traditional-factor items and 20 contemporary-factor items, together with measures of customer perception, satisfaction, loyalty and repurchase intention. Following data screening, reliability analysis, sampling-adequacy diagnostics and exploratory factor analysis with varimax rotation were performed on the 60 traditional and contemporary items. The Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin value (.853) and Bartlett’s test of sphericity (χ² = 9,898.742, df = 1,770, p < .001) confirmed the suitability of the data for factor analysis. Parallel analysis supported the retention of eight empirical factors, which together explained 45.62 per cent of the total variance and demonstrated acceptable-to-good internal consistency (α = .648 to .866). In line with the analysis, the originally hypothesised thirteen sub-dimensions eight traditional and five contemporary were not empirically reproduced; instead, the items regrouped into a more defensible eight-factor structure that largely separated traditional store-based attributes from contemporary technology-enabled attributes. The findings indicate that customer perception of organised retailing in this district-level market is multidimensional, but is better represented by a re-specified, data-driven factor structure than by the original conceptual framework. latest.title: Green Product Knowledge, Product Awareness, Attitudes, and Subjective Norms as Determinants of Green Purchase Decisions among Generation Z in Jakarta: The Mediating Role of Purchase Intention
latest.venue: Greenation International Journal of Economics and Accounting
latest.abstract: Green purchasing behavior has become an important component of sustainable consumption; however, the adoption of environmentally friendly products among Generation Z remains inconsistent despite their relatively high environmental awareness. This study aims to examine the effects of green product knowledge, product awareness, attitudes, and subjective norms on green purchase decisions among Generation Z in Jakarta, with purchase intention serving as a mediating variable. The study is grounded in the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and extends the model by incorporating green product knowledge and product awareness as additional antecedents of green purchase decisions. A quantitative explanatory research design was employed using a structured questionnaire administered to 1,525 Generation Z respondents across the five administrative regions of Jakarta. The collected data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3.2.9. The findings reveal that green product knowledge, product awareness, and attitudes have positive and significant effects on green purchase decisions, whereas subjective norms do not exert a significant direct effect. However, purchase intention significantly mediates the relationships between all antecedent variables and green purchase decisions, with full mediation observed for subjective norms. Among the examined predictors, attitudes demonstrate the strongest influence on green purchase decisions (β = 0.312, p < 0.001). The structural model explains 63.2% of the variance in green purchase decisions, indicating substantial predictive capability. The findings suggest that Generation Z's green purchasing behavior is primarily driven by personal evaluations, environmental knowledge, and product awareness

latest.title: Identification and Analysis of Fish Processing and Consumption Characteristics in Restaurants in the Bucharest-Ilfov Area
latest.venue: Bulletin of University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine Cluj-Napoca Animal Science and Biotechnologies
latest.abstract: Fish consumption in restaurants in Romania is a complex phenomenon, influenced by a number of economic, political, cultural and ecological factors. In the context of a growing demand for fish dishes, this report explores the characteristics of the fish processing and consumption market in Romanian restaurants, with a special focus on the Bucharest-Ilfov area. The purpose of this study is to identify and analyse the factors that influence the consumption of fish in restaurants and to provide recommendations for improving menus and increasing sustainability in this sector. The current research was conducted as a survey case analysis within restaurants order to gather quantitative and qualitative data on fish consumption patterns. The results indicate that diversifying menus by introducing more fish dishes can bring significant benefits to restaurants, both economically and operationally. Fish also proves to be a versatile and sustainable raw material, which, if used correctly, can attract new segments of consumers concerned about health and sustainability.

latest.title: Marketing Communication Strategy Through Social Media Content based on Local Wisdom to Increase the Added Value of Indonesian Coffee Brands (Study on Conservation Coffee Brands Based on Local Wisdom)
latest.abstract: The coffee industry is a significant sector in Indonesia, contributing to both domestic production and consumption. However, challenges such as declining production due to climate change, limited agricultural land, and increasing global competition have encouraged coffee businesses to adopt more innovative marketing strategies. One emerging approach involves social media marketing communications that incorporate local cultural values and traditional knowledge. This study aimed to explore the social media marketing communication strategies employed by Indonesian coffee businesses, particularly those incorporating local wisdom, and examine their implications for brand value. A descriptive qualitative approach employing a holistic single-case study design was adopted. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with consumers and coffee business owners who actively incorporated local wisdom-based content into their marketing strategies. The findings indicated that such content fostered emotional connections with consumers, enhanced brand awareness and engagement, and strengthened brand loyalty. These findings highlight the strategic potential of integrating local cultural values into social media marketing communications to enhance brand differentiation, strengthen perceived brand value, and support long-term business sustainability in Indonesia's coffee industry

latest.title: Understanding Smartphone Purchase Behavior Through the Lens of Government Administrative Employees
latest.abstract: This study examines sustainable consumer behavior among 200 Malaysian government administrative employees regarding smartphone acquisition and usage within the framework of Sustainable Development Goal 12 (SDG 12): Responsible Consumption and Production. Despite the public sector's role in advancing sustainability, a significant attitude-behavior gap persists, with consumers often prioritizing product performance and brand reputation over environmental considerations. This study investigates the influence of price sensitivity, brand image, product features, and social influence on smartphone purchasing behavior and replacement cycles. A quantitative approach was employed, using survey data collected from employees across several government entities. Data were analyzed through descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis. The findings reveal that social influence is the only statistically significant predictor of smartphone purchasing behavior (β = 0.384, p < 0.01), highlighting the importance of peer recommendations, workplace social norms, and social conformity in shaping purchasing decisions. In contrast, price sensitivity, brand image, and product features demonstrate no statistically significant relationships with purchasing behavior. Despite respondents' awareness of smartphone costs, environmental considerations, particularly product longevity and energy efficiency, receive limited attention. These findings highlight the need to strengthen sustainable consumption awareness among public sector employees. Accordingly, this study recommends implementing green procurement nudges and internal behavioral awareness programs within government institutions. latest.title: Context-aware forecasting of inter-firm competitive dynamics with graph learning and multi-agent reasoning
latest.abstract: Abstract The evolution of competitive dominance in technology-intensive industries is shaped by complex interactions among research activity, media visibility, strategic disclosures, public attention, and market signals. Understanding these dynamics is critical for strategic intelligence, yet existing predictive models often treat firms as isolated entities and provide limited support for contextualizing long-horizon firm-to-firm competitive forecasts. Here, we introduce an integrated framework that captures the relational nature of market competition by extending our prior Bayesian Multivariate Time-series Graph Neural Network with a newly designed, post hoc, lookahead-free multi-agent reasoning layer. The framework infers inter-firm relational dependencies endogenously from multimodal signals to forecast latent firm competitiveness and pairwise competitive gap trajectories with quantified predictive uncertainty. To evaluate strategic plausibility, specialized persona-driven language model agents critique the forecasted trajectories across technological, financial, and regulatory lenses using retrieved evidence. Evaluated under a rigorous date-based temporal protocol with strictly withheld test horizons, the framework consistently outperforms competitive structural baselines and yields well-calibrated prediction intervals. When applied to thirty leading AI-oriented technology firms, the framework uncovers asymmetric competitive momentum, contested market leadership, and emerging challenger dynamics. By bridging relational time-series forecasting with structured multi-agent deliberation, this study advances competitive dynamics analysis from purely accuracy-centric prediction toward context-aware, uncertainty-informed strategic intelligence.

latest.title: Influence of Chatbots on Consumer Purchase Decision-Making in Luxury Products
latest.venue: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology
latest.abstract: The rapid introduction of artificial intelligence into digital commerce has altered the way brands interact with their customers, particularly in the luxury sector, where personal contact and exclusivity are essential for adding value. Among the different technologies, chatbots have emerged as important tools since they allow for immediate communication, recommend products, and offer personalized help. This study examines how consumers view chatbots in the context of luxury products and develops a conceptual framework that links the features of chatbots – specifically responsiveness, personalization, anthropomorphism, and interactivity – with customers' intention to make a purchase through the intermediary effects of trust, perceived value, and emotional engagement. Unlike in the case of mass-market buying, luxury consumption is rooted in symbolic value, in the demonstration of status, and in the satisfaction obtained from the experience rather than simply in functionality, so the character of the digital interaction becomes particularly significant. An exploratory quantitative approach is used in the study, with a survey carried out of people who have used chatbot services on luxury websites. A Chi-square test of independence reveals a statistically significant relationship between the perception of chatbot design (to the extent that it appeared robotic) and the perception of ease of navigation, indicating that opinions about design and usability are related rather than independent. Since the sample size is small, this result is regarded as exploratory and indicative rather than conclusive, and the proposed connections between personalization, responsiveness, trust, perceived value, and purchase intention are given as a conceptual framework for future empirical researc

latest.title: Hibah Awareness in Takaful Products Among the Community in Lembah Pantai, Malaysia
latest.abstract: Both conventional insurance and Takaful share the common goal of alleviating the financial burden of the unfortunate party. The distinction lies in whether they adhere to Syariah Compliance or not. Recently, there has been a notable increase in the use of Takaful products in Islamic finance. These products offer insurance coverage to consumers while following Islamic principles. Hibah, an Islamic concept about the act of giving or leaving an inheritance, plays a pivotal role in facilitating the equitable allocation of wealth in accordance with Islamic norms. Despite its significance, there is still a noticeable knowledge gap about the advantages of Hibah. This research investigates awareness of the benefits of Hibah in Takaful products among the community in Lembah Pantai, Malaysia. Therefore, this study examines the relationship between age, promotion, education and the community's awareness of the benefits of Hibah in Takaful products. The study has a sample size of 100 respondents and uses a non-probability sampling technique to collect data via structured questionnaires. The study uses reliability, correlation and regression analysis to examine data and determine community awareness of the benefits of Hibah. Results show a strong correlation between age and education as important indicators of the community's awareness of the benefits of Hibah in Takaful products. Furthermore, it seeks to empower individuals to make informed decisions about financial planning and risk management, thereby improving their overall financial resilience and well-being.

latest.title: Artificial Intelligence and Consumer Purchase Behavior: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research Trends and Emerging Directions
latest.abstract: This study maps the academic research landscape on artificial intelligence (AI) and consumer purchase through a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed journal articles from 2020 to 2025. A structured search of titles, abstracts and keywords in Scopus yielded 343 journal articles after excluding conference proceedings, book chapters and other source types. We examined the corpus along five dimensions: document and source types, the evolution of published studies since 2020, the distribution of subject areas, keyword co-occurrence, and citation metrics for highly cited articles. The publication output grew gradually from 2020 to 2023 and increased significantly from 2024 onwards, with 2025 recording the highest number of publications. This growth coincides with the mainstreaming of conversational AI and the advent of generative AI. The field is interdisciplinary, spanning business and management, computer science, the social sciences, psychology and decision sciences. Keyword co-occurrence analysis indicates that purchase intention, consumer behavior, marketing and sales are the conceptual anchors and the most cited articles focus on technology acceptance, trust, chatbot purchase intention, virtual influencer marketing and environmental sustainability. This study provides a quantitative map of the literature on AI and consumer purchase for 2020-2025 and highlights the dominant role of trust and perceived value in the literature, as well as open questions about long-term effects and cross-cultural generalizability.

latest.title: ВОСПРИЯТИЕ КИТАЙСКИХ АВТОМОБИЛЬНЫХ БРЕНДОВ РОССИЙСКИМИ ПОТРЕБИТЕЛЯМИ: УЗНАВАЕМОСТЬ, ФАКТОРЫ ВЫБОРА И ГОТОВНОСТЬ К ПОКУПКЕ
latest.abstract: статья посвящена восприятию китайских автомобильных брендов российскими потребителями в условиях, когда рост рынка, обеспеченный уходом западных производителей, сменился спадом и ужесточением регулирования. Работа опирается на результаты онлайн-опроса 64 респондентов, проведённого в мае 2026 г. в Московской области, Краснодарском крае и на Черноморском побережье, и рассматривает потребительское решение как последовательность «осведомлённость - опыт - оценка - намерение». Показано, что узнаваемость сосредоточена в верхнем сегменте рынка, тогда как значительная часть аудитории не различает отдельные марки, цена и надёжность образуют устойчивое ядро выбора, которому доступность запчастей и ликвидность уступают по весу, но не по влиянию на репутацию бренда. Отдельное внимание уделено разрыву между осведомлённостью и опытом: почти половина опрошенных не имела дела с китайским автомобилем, поэтому их представления формируются вторичными источниками. Автор приходит к выводу, что источник конкурентного преимущества смещается от доступа к рынку к накоплению доверия, а работа с барьерами решения становится важнее дальнейшего расширения присутствия. Полученные результаты могут быть использованы производителями и дистрибьюторами при планировании продуктовой и коммуникационной политики на российском рынке.

latest.title: Pricing and Extended Warranty Strategies for Echelon-Utilized Batteries with Echelon Utilization Rate in a Dual-Stream Supply Chain
latest.abstract: : With the rapid increase in retired power batteries, echelon utilization has become an essential strategy for resource sustainability. However, the commercial application of second-life batteries is often held back by high technical screening costs and consumer worries about product reliability. This paper builds an analytical model for a dual-stream supply chain where collected batteries are either repurposed for echelon utilization products or sent for material recycling, based on a specific echelon utilization rate. We jointly optimize the selling price and the extended warranty price, taking into account time-varying failure rates and a cost structure that covers repair, preventive maintenance, and battery replacement. The results show that an extended warranty can effectively lower consumers' perceived risk and increase market demand. We find that the best pricing strategy depends on the echelon utilization rate. As this rate goes up, the echelon utilization provider should raise the product price and shift from a service-led approach to a strategy centered on hardware reliability. In addition, the analysis shows that the revenue from material recycling can help offset the high maintenance costs that come with early-stage screening technologies. Furthermore, we quantify the environmental benefits of the system, revealing that the extended warranty acts as an environmental amplifier that significantly boosts total carbon emission reductions. However, the viability of this strategy is strictly bounded by a frontier dictated by the battery degradation rate and the offered warranty period. This study gives managers a quantitative basis for balancing technical efficiency and service provision to improve the profitability of the circular battery business.

latest.title: Market Penetration of a Premium Dairy Brand through General and Modern Trade: Exploratory Field Evidence from Pune, India
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: A premium dairy brand entering an established city market has to win over two very different people: the neighbourhood retailer in general trade (GT) and the shopper in modern trade (MT). This paper reports an exploratory field study of Sid’s Farm, a dairy brand that sells on laboratory testing and quality, carried out during a two-month on-the-job training placement in Pune (May–July 2026). I draw on a recorded retailer funnel from Wakad (53 retailers approached), a brand-availability audit of those same 53 outlets, and field observation of customer interactions, freezer merchandising and two sampling activities at a modern-trade store in Baner. Reading the evidence through Ansoff’s market-penetration logic, the AIDA model and retailer relationship management, I find five things. First, 77.8% of interested retailers (21 of 27) placed a first order, yet only 39.6% of everyone approached did. Second, 13 of the 21 first-order retailers (61.9%) were recorded as reordering, while 6 had stopped. Third, Govind and Amul were present in 94.3% and 88.7% of audited outlets, so entry means competing for shelf space that is already taken. Fourth, the main GT barriers were price, demand uncertainty, margin and cold-chain-related spoilage, while MT shoppers pushed back on price, loyalty and low visibility. Fifth, high-protein curd and paneer drew stronger interest in a fitness-adjacent store, and sampling was followed by observed purchase interest in other SKUs. The study is descriptive, rests on a convenience field frame and cannot establish causal effects. What it offers is a channel-specific penetration model and a set of testable propositions for later survey and experimental work. latest.title: The Nexus Among Competitiveness, Sustainability and Corporate Social Responsibility: Evidence from Real Estate Companies in CALABARZON
latest.venue: International Journal of Education, Research, and Innovation Perspectives
latest.abstract: This study examined the nexus among competitiveness, sustainability, and corporate social responsibility (CSR) among 21 Philippine Stock Exchange-listed real estate companies operating in CALABARZON during the last quarter of 2024 and first quarter of 2025. Using a descriptive research design, data were collected through questionnaire checklists and interviews involving 31 management representatives, 394 employees, and 124 external stakeholders. Findings indicated favorable perceptions of competitiveness across external market and policy factors and internal management, marketing, and financial dimensions. Management generally reported higher assessments than employees. Competitiveness did not differ significantly by location, years of operation, payment mode, or years conducting CSR, but significant differences emerged across selected indicators associated with capital, workforce size, client volume, products or services, and branches. Sustainability initiatives were widely implemented, particularly in energy efficiency, green building, water conservation, and eco-friendly design; comparatively weaker ratings concerned climate action, sustainable cities, and community collaboration. Sustainability implementation likewise varied by certain financial and organizational characteristics, but not by location, years of operation, products or services, payment mode, or years conducting CSR. Government policies were generally perceived as influential in integrating economic, social, and environmental CSR practices. Correlation analysis showed a strong positive relationship between competitiveness and sustainability and moderate positive relationships between competitiveness and CSR and between sustainability and CSR. latest.title: When do e-commerce prediction models fail over time? cross-task evidence on temporal reliability and model maintenance
latest.abstract: Machine-learning models in e-commerce are often evaluated on randomly partitioned historical data, whereas deployment requires prediction on future observations under changing populations and information availability. We examine temporal reliability and model maintenance across four public dataset–task settings: late-delivery prediction among eventually delivered Olist orders, matched 24-h cart-to-purchase prediction in Retailrocket and Synerise RecSys 2025, and 30-day repeat-purchase prediction in Online Retail II. Sequential analyses restrict historical features, model updating, and recalibration to information and labels available at each prediction or deployment time. Random-to-future differences varied substantially: Olist showed pronounced deterioration, whereas the other settings showed smaller or qualitatively different changes. In the primary Olist XGBoost analysis, cumulative retraining improved ranking and modestly improved Brier accuracy, while sliding-window retraining improved ranking but worsened probability reliability. Cross-model, matched-exposure, and sensitivity analyses showed that maintenance effects depended on setting, period, model family, and design. Post-hoc recalibration did not provide a consistently reliable repair, and same-base calibration effects differed from net maintenance-policy effects. The matched comparisons do not identify causal task or duration effects. These findings support forward-in-time evaluation that assesses ranking, probability quality, label availability, and maintenance effects separately rather than inferring future reliability from offline performance or task identity.

latest.title: The Influence of Digital Marketing and Service Quality on Grade X Students' Decisions in Choosing Private Vocational School In Jambi Medan
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi, Manajemen dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of Digital Marketing and service quality on the decision of tenth-grade students in choosing a private vocational school in Jambi, Medan. This study used a quantitative approach. The study population was 222 tenth-grade students of a private vocational school in Jambi, Medan, with a sample of 143 students determined using the Proportionate Stratified Random Sampling technique using the Slovin formula. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression using the t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination (R²). The results showed that Digital Marketing had a positive and significant effect on students' decisions in choosing a school (t-test = 9.351; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Service quality also had a positive and significant effect on students' decisions (t-test = 8.085; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Simultaneously, both variables had a positive and significant effect on student decisions (F count = 70.668; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). This finding indicates that 50.2% of the variation in students' decisions in choosing Jambi Medan Private Vocational Schools can be explained by Digital Marketing and service quality, while the remaining 49.8% is influenced by other factors outside the study.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement.
