latest.title: SMART RETAILING IN INTERNET COMMERCE: AN AI-ENABLED CUSTOMER-CENTRIC SERVICE FRAMEWORK
latest.venue: EPH - International Journal of Business & Management Science
latest.abstract: This conceptual paper examines AI-enabled smart retailing as a customer-facing service transformation in Internet commerce rather than as a narrow technological or operational innovation. Drawing on a selective, theory-driven synthesis of services marketing, smart retailing, AI-enabled marketing, customer experience, service-dominant logic, human–AI interaction, and responsible-AI research, it develops a three-layer framework linking AI-enabled service capabilities, customer-experience mechanisms, and Internet-commerce outcomes. The framework identifies three capability groups—algorithmic personalisation and decision support, AI-mediated service interaction, and predictive service intelligence—and four evaluative mechanisms: decision value, interaction quality, transaction confidence, and algorithmic legitimacy. These mechanisms shape customer satisfaction, engagement, service-recovery effectiveness, platform trust, relationship quality, continuance intention, value co-creation, and inclusive service value. Human–AI governance, including privacy protection, transparency, fairness, customer control, human review, and digital accessibility, is treated as a boundary condition that determines whether AI-enabled services are perceived as trustworthy and customer-centred or as intrusive, opaque, unfair, and exclusionary. The paper contributes to Internet-commerce research by repositioning AI as a service-enabling capability and by explaining how customer evaluations translate AI applications into commercial and relational outcomes. It also proposes a focused research agenda for empirical testing across e-commerce websites, mobile applications, online marketplaces, social-commerce platforms, and omnichannel systems.

latest.title: Emotion regulation and venture performance: evidence from rural entrepreneurship
latest.abstract: Introduction Rural entrepreneurs are constrained by resource shortages and institutional barriers, and are prone to experiencing persistent emotional stress. However, existing research has not fully clarified the mechanism by which emotion regulation affects venture performance. Most related studies have focused on urban entrepreneurs, lacking comparative analysis of the mediating roles of explorative learning and exploitative learning, and failing to clearly define the boundary role of entrepreneurial experience. Based on this, drawing on upper echelons theory and Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this paper explores the mechanism of emotion regulation and venture performance among rural entrepreneurs, analyzes the mediating roles of explorative learning and exploitative learning, and empirically examines the moderating effect of entrepreneurial experience. Methods We adopted a two-wave time-lagged survey design to mitigate common method bias, collecting valid questionnaires from 207 Chinese rural entrepreneurs. A series of validity and data screening checks were implemented to ensure the rigor of the analysis. Hierarchical regression analysis was employed to test the main effects and moderating effects, while the bootstrap method was applied to examine the mediating effects and to compare the relative strength of the two mediating pathways. All analyses were conducted using SPSS 21 and Amos 22. Results Emotion regulation is positively related to venture performance. Both exploitative learning and explorative learning mediate the relationship between emotion regulation and venture performance. We also find that the positive effect of emotion regulation on venture performance mainly operates through the channel of explorative learning. Moreover, the study finds th

latest.title: Nghiên cứu thực nghiệm đánh giá mức độ ứng dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo trong việc cá nhân hóa trải nghiệm du khách tại thành phố Đà Nẵng
latest.abstract: Trong bối cảnh chuyển đổi số đang tái định hình ngành du lịch toàn cầu, trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) ngày càng trở thành một công nghệ chiến lược trong phát triển du lịch thông minh. Tuy nhiên, các nghiên cứu hiện nay chủ yếu tập trung vào hiệu quả ứng dụng công nghệ hoặc hành vi chấp nhận công nghệ, trong khi cơ chế tác động của AI đến hành vi hậu trải nghiệm của du khách, đặc biệt là ý định quay lại điểm đến, vẫn chưa được làm rõ tại các thị trường mới nổi như Việt Nam. Nghiên cứu này được thực hiện nhằm phân tích cơ chế tác động của các yếu tố thuộc hệ sinh thái AI đến trải nghiệm du lịch thông minh, niềm tin công nghệ và ý định quay lại của du khách tại Đà Nẵng. Nghiên cứu được xây dựng trên nền tảng tích hợp giữa Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Service-Dominant Logic (SDL) và Trust Theory, từ đó đề xuất mô hình nghiên cứu gồm năm biến công nghệ thế hệ mới: AI Personalization, AI Interactivity, Predictive Intelligence, Data Privacy Assurance và Immersive Technology Integration. Nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp hỗn hợp, bao gồm nghiên cứu định tính thông qua phỏng vấn chuyên gia nhằm hiệu chỉnh thang đo và nghiên cứu định lượng thông qua khảo sát 400 khách du lịch nội địa và quốc tế đã trải nghiệm dịch vụ tại Đà Nẵng. Dữ liệu được phân tích bằng IBM SPSS Statistics và SmartPLS thông qua các kỹ thuật Cronbach’s alpha, EFA, CFA, SEM và Bootstrapping. Kết quả nghiên cứu kỳ vọng sẽ chứng minh rằng các yếu tố AI không chỉ nâng cao trải nghiệm du lịch thông minh mà còn góp phần hình thành niềm tin công nghệ và thúc đẩy hành vi quay lại điểm đến. Nghiên cứu được kỳ vọng đóng góp về mặt lý luận thông qua việc mở rộng các mô hình hành vi công nghệ trong bối cảnh du lịch thông minh; đồng thời cung cấp cơ sở thực tiễn cho doanh nghiệp và cơ quan quản lý trong việc xây dựng chiến lược

latest.title: Who chose the label? Voluntary versus mandated AI disclosure in tourism marketing
latest.abstract: Generative AI is being used extensively by destination marketing organisations (DMOs) to create promotional imagery, and new regulation requires disclosure of some synthetic content. Previous research indicates that revealing an AI source can reduce perceived authenticity but treats disclosure as a single cue. This study investigated whether travellers react differently when the AI label is presented as the DMO's own decision or as a legally mandated requirement. A simulated single factor, three condition (no label, voluntary label, mandated label) between-subjects online experiment with N = 387 adult participants. The analysis was based on the Persuasion Knowledge Model and attribution theory, using ANCOVA, bootstrapped parallel mediation analyses (multicategorical predictor), moderation by attitudes towards AI and robustness checks. Both labels reduced perceived authenticity compared to no label (voluntary: d = −0.59; mandated: d = −0.74). The voluntary label raised perceived DMO integrity (d = 0.38), producing a positive indirect effect on visit intention. The mandated label earned no integrity credit, and its negative indirect effect through authenticity was not compensated. These effects were not significantly moderated by general attitudes toward AI. The study distinguishes between what the AI label says and who is seen to have chosen it, thereby furthering the research on persuasion-knowledge in tourism and providing a model that DMOs can test for disclosure in the regulatory era.

latest.title: Is global positioning better for pharmaceutical advertising? An experimental study on its impact on brand equity
latest.venue: International Journal of Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Marketing
latest.abstract: Purpose To enhance efficiency in pharmaceutical advertising, this study aims to examine and compare the effects of consumer culture positioning (CCP) – global (GCCP) versus local (LCCP) – and doctor recommendations in direct-to-consumer advertising (DTCA) on skepticism, attitude toward the ad (Aad) and customer-based brand equity (CBBE) and examine the mechanisms through skepticism and Aad. Design/methodology/approach A 2 (CCP: GCCP vs LCCP) × 2 (doctor recommendation: with vs without) between-subject factorial experiment was conducted. Hypotheses were tested using the General Linear Model (GLM) and PROCESS Model 4. Findings CCP significantly influences skepticism, Aad and CBBE, whereas doctor recommendations do not. GCCP generates higher Aad and CBBE and lower skepticism than LCCP. Skepticism and Aad also significantly mediate the effect of CCP and doctor recommendations on CBBE. Research limitations/implications Future research could examine how artificial intelligence and social media influence the effectiveness of GCCP in DTCA, assess GCCP effectiveness across countries and cultures, explore the interpersonal dynamics of doctor recommendations and investigate gender differences in skepticism toward DTCA using GCCP. Practical implications Pharmaceutical companies may consider GCCP in DTCA to improve advertising efficiency through standardized global advertising while enhancing CBBE. Its greater effectiveness than doctor recommendations also suggests more efficient allocation of promotional expenditure. Originality/value This study extends the DTCA literature by examining consumer culture positioning as a previously overlooked determinant of DTCA effectiveness. The findings of this study demonstrate that GCCP can enhance CBBE by reducing skepticism and increasing Aad.

latest.title: The Influence of AI-Driven Conversational Commerce on Electric Vehicle Customer Satisfaction and Repeat Purchase Intention in Pune District, Maharashtra (2023–24 to 2025–26)
latest.abstract: This study investigates the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven conversational commerce—comprising multilingual Natural Language Processing (NLP) chatbots, WhatsApp Business API assistants, voice-enabled in-app concierges, and predictive Customer Relationship Management (CRM) interfaces—in shaping customer satisfaction (CSAT) and repeat purchase intention (RPI) among Electric Vehicle (EV) consumers across Pune District, Maharashtra, from FY 2023–24 to FY 2025–26. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) frameworks, the research combines longitudinal secondary registration data from Maharashtra Vahan portals and the Pune Regional Transport Office (RTO) with a structured primary survey of N = 420EV owners across urban, peri-urban, and rural talukas (Pune City, Haveli, Pimpri-Chinchwad, Mulshi, Maval, Baramati, Shirur, and Daund). Statistical analysis using Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression, and one-way ANOVA demonstrates that conversational responsiveness, personalized Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) estimation, and predictive service reminders significantly elevate customer satisfaction (R2 = 0.684, p < 0.001), which in turn strongly mediates repeat purchase and brand advocacy intention (β = 0.742, p < 0.001). However, algorithmic opacity in complex battery-warranty disputes and data privacy concerns remain notable friction points, particularly in semi-urban corridors.

latest.title: Sensor-wide association studies: a methodological architecture for developing and evaluating functional human traits
latest.abstract: Background Wearable and other digital sensors enable longitudinal observation of physiology and behaviour. However, reproducible associations and predictive performance do not establish which physiological construct a sensor-derived representation measures. An explicit framework is needed to distinguish statistical representation, construct interpretation and mechanistic explanation. Objective This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes Functional Human Traits (FHTs) and Sensor-Wide Association Studies (SWAS) as a conceptual and methodological architecture for developing and evaluating individual-level representations of physiological response capacities. Conceptual framework An FHT is defined as a quantitative representation of a specified physiological response capacity, supported by temporal repeatability over a justified interval and independent biological evidence under stated conditions. SWAS links documented sensor features, exploratory analysis, candidate construction and independent evaluation. Outcome-guided screening estimates feature–outcome associations, whereas unsupervised analysis identifies statistical structure; neither directly identifies a physiological construct. Candidate construction requires an explicit measurement model, individual-level estimation with uncertainty and tests addressing competing interpretations. Evaluation distinguishes statistical replication, technical robustness, temporal repeatability and biological support. A hypothetical cardiovascular heat-response example illustrates candidate construction using a longitudinal model. Environmental sensing and semantic integration are optional supporting components where relevant to the research question. Implications SWAS integrates established association-study and sensor-based measurem

latest.title: Mechanisms underlying the role of digital and intelligent mental health services in relation to suicidal ideation among college students: a chain mediation model involving crisis perception and psychological resilience
latest.abstract: Introduction Against the backdrop of global digital transformation and increasing psychological stress among college students, suicidal ideation has emerged as a significant public health concern. Digital and intelligent mental health services, characterized by accessibility, anonymity, and convenience, have become an important complement to traditional mental health service models. However, the psychological mechanisms underlying the association between digital and intelligent mental health service use and suicidal ideation remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between digital and intelligent mental health service use and suicidal ideation among college students and to examine the mediating roles of crisis perception and psychological resilience. Methods Based on the interaction perspective of stress and cognition and positive psychology theory, a cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted among 1,086 undergraduate students from a university in Shandong Province using cluster sampling. Participants completed measures assessing digital and intelligent mental health service use, crisis perception, psychological resilience, and suicidal ideation. SPSS 26.0 was used to conduct common method bias tests and correlation analyses, and Model 6 of the PROCESS macro was employed to examine the chain mediation model. Results Digital and intelligent mental health service use was significantly and negatively associated with suicidal ideation (β = −0.315, p < 0.001). Mediation analyses revealed three significant indirect pathways: the independent mediating effect of crisis perception, the independent mediating effect of psychological resilience, and the chain mediating effect involving crisis perception and psychological resilience.

latest.title: Generative AI in Advertising: Balancing Business Efficiency and Consumer Trust
latest.venue: Student Journal of Business and Economics
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly changed the way businesses can create advertisements by providing custom content for a low cost. However, the use of generative AI has increasingly begun to raise questions about creativity and transparency; for businesses, the use of generative AI has also begun to spark dilemmas involving consumer trust, and the role of humans within advertising. This literature review examines how generative AI affects advertising from both a business and consumer perspective. Existing research was analyzed through AI disclosure, perceived authenticity, creativity, purchase intention, traditional versus generative AI, and business efficiency. The literature generally suggests that consumers can respond negatively when it is revealed that an advertisement was generated by AI, especially when they already have preconceived notions of generative AI being unauthentic or low effort. Nevertheless, recent research has also demonstrated generative AI can also boost engagement by increasing perceptions of novelty, when the audience views generative AI positively. The stark contrast between these findings suggest that consumer responses cannot be determined solely based on whether or not AI was used, but by the nuances of its use: the type of product being advertised, the transparency of the advertisement, and the opinions of the target audience are factors that all influence advertising outcomes. As a whole, generative AI can provide significant opportunities to businesses to reduce cost and increase the scale of advertisement production, but companies must balance these advantages with the concerns regarding consumer expectations for authenticity and creativity.

latest.title: Greenwashing skepticism as a selective moderator: how digital environmental content exposure shapes green e-commerce intentions among Saudi university students
latest.abstract: Introduction As Generation Z consumers increasingly engage with digital platforms in response to environmental considerations, understanding how online sustainability messaging shapes green e-commerce behavior becomes more pressing. Digitalization is often assumed to equalize access to sustainability information, yet digital divide research shows that inequalities persist in how online content is converted into outcomes. Drawing on the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study examines how exposure to digital environmental content (DECE) shapes green e-consumption intention (GECI) among digitally literate Saudi university students. Methods Environmental awareness and personal responsibility (EAR) and message credibility (MC) were modeled as two parallel mediators linking DECE to GECI, with no hypothesized path between them. Greenwashing perception (GP) was expected to moderate specifically the effect of MC on GECI, and perceived barriers (PB) were examined as an independent predictor of GECI. Data from 305 respondents were analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Results The model explained substantial variance in GECI ( R ² = 0.603; Q ² = 0.577). DECE had a significant direct effect on GECI ( β = 0.190, p = 0.001). The EAR-mediated pathway was dominant ( β = 0.311, f ² = 0.333), whereas the MC-mediated pathway was non-significant ( β = 0.006, p = 0.823). GP moderated the credibility–intention link (MC → GECI; β = −0.114, p = 0.005) but not the exposure–intention link (DECE → GECI; β = 0.070, p = 0.095), suggesting that greenwashing skepticism acts as a credibility-related barrier. PB was positively associated with GECI ( β = 0.138, p = 0.023), a counter-intuitive association interpreted tentativ

latest.title: Supply Chain Agility mediates the Influence of Supply Chain Integration, Supply Chain Visibility and Digital Transformation on Supply Chain Performance
latest.venue: Dinasti International Journal of Education Management And Social Science
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of supply chain integration, supply chain visibility, and digital transformation on supply chain performance, with supply chain agility as a mediating variable in Indonesian companies and the logistics industry. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed through a literature review of 60 scientific articles published between 2021 and 2026, sourced from Springer, Wiley, ProQuest, Emerald, Taylor & Francis, Sage, SINTA, Copernicus, and Google Scholar. Data analysis involved reduction, descriptive and comparative presentation, and synthesis of research findings. The results indicate that supply chain integration, visibility, and digital transformation positively influence supply chain agility and performance. Furthermore, supply chain agility contributes to improved supply chain performance. The findings also demonstrate that supply chain agility mediates the relationships between supply chain integration, visibility, digital transformation, and supply chain performance. This study highlights the importance of integrating supply chain processes, enhancing information visibility, and adopting digital technologies to strengthen organizational agility and improve supply chain performance in Indonesia's logistics sector.

latest.title: Islamic Financial Planning for Inclusive and Sustainable Wellbeing
latest.venue: CASHFLOW CURRENT ADVANCED RESEARCH ON SHARIA FINANCE AND ECONOMIC WORLDWIDE
latest.abstract: Backgrounds: Islamic financial planning can connect household resilience, ethical investment and social redistribution within a coherent life-cycle framework. Objectives: This article updates the supplied manuscript by integrating comparative documentary evidence from Saudi Arabia, Malaysia, Indonesia, Türkiye and Pakistan with a proposed digitally enabled operational model. Methodology: A structured narrative review distinguishes observed institutional developments from normative design choices and untested impact propositions. Findings: The model retains four interdependent pillars: wealth protection, accumulation, preservation and distribution. It adds explicit cash flow management, affordable access, consumer protection and measurable wellbeing outcomes. Contemporary official evidence demonstrates the scale of Islamic finance and the feasibility of retail sukuk, social takaful, value-based intermediation and cash waqf-linked sukuk, but does not establish that a comprehensive planning service has caused improvements in household welfare. Blockchain, artificial intelligence, machine learning, the Internet of Things and big data can support traceability, forecasting and monitoring when governed by consent, legal enforceability, Shariah review and human accountability. The article proposes a mind map, implementation sequence and evaluation design. Conclusions: Universal access is a central service principle; religion-specific obligations and legally restricted funds require separate treatment. The resulting framework offers testable pathways toward financial resilience and sustainable development without assuming guaranteed returns or uniform effects.

latest.title: Relational and cultural framing in ai emotional support: perceived understanding and emotional resonance in a Chinese-speaking young-adult context
latest.abstract: Introduction Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used for emotional support, but how supportive messages convey an understanding of culturally and relationally salient concerns remains unclear. We examined evaluations of Chinese-language responses to an academic-disappointment and family-pressure vignette. Methods Two scenario-based studies compared a relationally and culturally congruent message (RC), a culture-neutral message (N), and an autonomy-oriented comparison message (A). Study 1 ( N = 126) evaluated perceived cultural fit and six basic message-quality ratings. Study 2 ( N = 486; 162 per condition) compared perceived understanding, emotional resonance, and related evaluations after randomized exposure. We distinguished the three-condition contrast (RC versus the mean of N and A) from a separate RC-versus-N statistical indirect-association model. Results In Study 1, cultural fit differed across messages, F (2, 123) = 86.24, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0 . 584 ; no statistically significant differences were detected on the six basic quality ratings. In Study 2, RC received the highest ratings for perceived understanding ( M = 5.72) and emotional resonance ( M = 5.63). The unadjusted RC-versus-mean-of-N-and-A contrast was 0.93 scale points for each outcome. Emotional resonance correlated with perceived understanding ( r = 0.66), and an additional simultaneous-adjustment regression yielded a positive resonance coefficient ( b ≈.325, 95% CI [0.243, 0.406]). In the distinct RC-versus-N model, the adjusted total coefficient was 0.66 (95% CI [0.54, 0.78]) and the statistical indirect estimate was 0.37 (95% CI [0.29, 0.47]). Discussion Recognition of relational and situational concerns may influence immediate evaluations of these specific support messages. Be

latest.title: Digitalization of the Socio-Cultural Space: IT Platforms as a Driver of Emotional Experience Capitalization
latest.venue: Проблеми сучасних трансформацій Серія економіка та управління
latest.abstract: This research article addresses the highly important issue of transforming the socio-cultural space under the influence of digitalization, driven by shifting consumer behavior patterns and the growing role of the experience economy. The aim of the study is to analyze the mechanisms of digital transformation in the socio-cultural environment, identify the structural components of emotional experience capitalization via IT platforms, and systematize startup management models for commercializing and scaling creative products. The study employs a qualitative multidisciplinary methodological approach combining systems analysis, Osterwalder’s Business Model Canvas, Lean Startup principles, and a comparative case analysis of empirical projects (SKEIRON, ARTEFACT, Fever, Meow Wolf). The results indicate that emotional experience capitalization is proposed as a three-phase conceptual framework encompassing pre-experience, immersion, and post-experience stages. A matrix mapping key IT technologies (AR/VR, artificial intelligence, Big Data, Phygital) to business effects in the socio-cultural sector is formed, proposing three typical management business models: Reconstruction-Immersive, Data-Driven, and Phygital Acceleration. The scientific novelty of the work lies in the conceptual proposition of IT platforms not merely as external distribution channels, but as architectural engines for co-creating emotional and economic value, as well as proposing the adaptation of startup management frameworks to test Emotional Fit rather than utilitarian functionality. The theoretical significance of the study consists in expanding the conceptual foundations of socio-cultural management and the experience economy through integration with IT product management. latest.title: Digital Transformation and Pandemic Resilience in Global Logistics: A Comparative Case Analysis of DHL's Supply Chain Operations in the United Kingdom and United States
latest.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
latest.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed structural fragilities in global supply chains and accelerated logistics providers' investment in digital technology. This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, and the Internet of Things (IoT) have contributed to pandemic resilience in global logistics, using DHL's operations in the United Kingdom and the United States as an illustrative comparative case. Drawing on industry reports, trade-body surveys, and the academic literature, the analysis finds that these technologies strengthen supply chain visibility, forecasting capability, and transactional trust, while high implementation costs, legacy-system integration, and cybersecurity exposure remain persistent constraints, particularly for smaller operators. A comparison of national contexts suggests that the UK and the US are converging on similar technologies but for different underlying reasons: UK adoption is shaped substantially by post-Brexit uncertainty and shifting consumer behaviour, while US adoption is driven by competition for global technology leadership and by workforce skills shortages. The paper argues that digital investment alone does not guarantee resilience; it must be accompanied by leadership, workforce development, and a long-term strategic orientation toward risk.

latest.title: Effect of Financial Reporting Quality on Operational Performance of Commercial Banks: A Case of Bank of Kigali, Rwanda
latest.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
latest.abstract: Rwanda's commercial banks face several financial reporting quality challenges, including inconsistent reporting practices, lack of transparency, inadequate financial disclosures, delayed reporting, and limited adoption of international financial reporting standards (IFRS).This study investigated the effect of financial reporting quality on the operational performance of commercial banks in Rwanda, focusing on Bank of Kigali.It examined financial reporting accuracy, completeness, and compliance.Agency Theory, Information Theory, and Signaling Theory guided the study.A descriptive and correlational design was adopted, with a census of 115 employees across six departments.Questionnaires and interviews supported data collection, and 104 completed questionnaires were returned, representing a response rate of 90.4%.Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression in SPSS version 25.The model yielded R = 0.822, R² = 0.676, and adjusted R² = 0.666.Financial reporting accuracy (B = 0.390, p < 0.001) and completeness (B = 0.356, p < 0.001) were positive, statistically significant predictors of operational performance.Compliance had a positive but statistically insignificant coefficient (B = 0.118, p = 0.244).Thus, the first two null hypotheses were rejected, while the third was not rejected.The study recommended stronger pre-publication verification, standardized disclosure templates, and regular compliance training and monitoring.

latest.title: The relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust: brand credibility, emotional attachment, and perceived quality effects
latest.abstract: Introduction The purpose of this research was to explore the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Specifically, we developed a conceptual model which proposes that brand credibility has a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust, and that perceived quality and emotional attachment have mediating effects on brand trust. Methods We tested the conceptual model by conducting a 2 × 2 (low versus high brand ethicality and low versus high brand credibility) between-subjects experiment, with brand trust as the dependent variable. Data ( N = 208) were collected at a large university in Bangladesh, and were analysed using PLS-SEM. Results Results of the experiment suggest that brand ethicality has a direct effect on brand trust. Brand ethicality also enhances emotional attachment and perceived quality, which, in turn, lead to increased brand trust. Brand credibility, however, does not have a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Discussion Drawing on signalling theory, the findings provide causal evidence that brand ethicality builds brand trust through two parallel pathways: an affective pathway via emotional attachment and a cognitive pathway via perceived quality. Contrary to expectations, brand credibility did not act as a boundary condition, suggesting that brand ethicality and brand credibility may be better understood as sequential antecedents of brand trust rather than as interacting constructs. For practice, marketers ought to increase brand ethicality to increase brand trust, both directly and via emotional attachment and perceived quality.

latest.title: A unified framework for robots that influence humans over long-term interaction
latest.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research
latest.abstract: Robot actions influence the decisions of nearby humans. Here, influence refers to intentional change: robots influence humans when they shift the human’s behavior in a way that helps the robot complete its task. Imagine an autonomous car trying to merge; by proactively nudging into the human’s lane, the robot causes human drivers to yield and provide space. Influence is often necessary for seamless interaction. However, if influence is left unregulated and uncontrolled, robots will negatively impact the humans around them (e.g., autonomous cars that repeatedly merge in front of humans may cause human drivers to become more aggressive). Prior works have begun to address this problem by creating a variety of control algorithms that seek to influence humans. Although these methods are effective in the short-term, they fail to maintain influence over time as the human adapts to the robot’s behaviors. In this paper we therefore present an optimization framework that enables robots to purposely regulate their influence over humans across both short - term and long - term interactions. Here, the robot maintains its influence by reasoning over a dynamic human model which captures how the robot’s current choices will impact the human’s future behavior. Our resulting framework serves to unify current approaches: we demonstrate that state-of-the-art methods are simplifications of our underlying formalism. Our framework also provides a principled way to generate influential policies: in the best case the robot exactly solves our framework to find optimal, influential behavior. But when solving this optimization problem becomes impractical, designers can introduce their own simplifications to reach tractable approximations.
