hot.title: A Comparison of Responses from Human Therapists and Large Language Model–Based Chatbots to Assess Therapeutic Communication: Mixed Methods Study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consumers are increasingly using large language model-based chatbots to seek mental health advice or intervention due to ease of access and limited availability of mental health professionals. However, their suitability and safety for mental health applications remain underexplored, particularly in comparison to professional therapeutic practices. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate how general-purpose chatbots respond to mental health scenarios and compare their responses to those provided by licensed therapists. Specifically, we sought to identify chatbots' strengths and limitations, as well as the ethical and practical considerations necessary for their use in mental health care. METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods study to compare responses from chatbots and licensed therapists to scripted mental health scenarios. We created 2 fictional scenarios and prompted 3 chatbots to create 6 interaction logs. We recruited 17 therapists and conducted study sessions that consisted of 3 activities. First, therapists responded to the 2 scenarios using a Qualtrics form. Second, therapists went through the 6 interaction logs using a think-aloud procedure to highlight their thoughts about the chatbots' responses. Finally, we conducted a semistructured interview to explore subjective opinions on the use of chatbots for supporting mental health. The study sessions were analyzed using thematic analysis. The interaction logs from chatbot and therapist responses were coded using the Multitheoretical List of Therapeutic Interventions codes and then compared to each other. RESULTS: We identified 7 themes describing the strengths and limitations of the chatbots as compared to therapists. These include elements of good therapy in chatbot responses, conversational style of c

hot.title: The multinational enterprise, capabilities, and digitalization: governance and growth with world disorder
hot.abstract: Abstract This essay revisits my 2014 JIBS article about the potential for integrating international business internalization theory with a strategic management capabilities perspective. It recaps the capabilities framework with an emphasis on the learning required of emerging market multinationals and illustrates this with the case of Hyundai Motor Company’s internationalization and growth. It also discusses two aspects of the global economy that have become more prominent since 2014 in shaping international business: geopolitical uncertainty and digitalization. A rise in geopolitical tensions appears to be rebalancing the relationships between multinationals and home/host governments. Digitalization facilitates international business; but it adds new vulnerabilities by (further) accelerating competition, enabling new rivals, and introducing systemic risks into digital supply chains. Implications for managers, board members, and international business scholars are drawn.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.

hot.title: The Role of Digital Tourism Platforms in Advancing Sustainable Development Goals in the Industry 4.0 Era
hot.abstract: The intersection of digitalization and sustainability is reshaping the tourism industry, with digital platforms playing a transformative role in optimizing travel experiences while simultaneously influencing economic inclusivity, labor dynamics, and environmental responsibility. This paper explores how Industry 4.0 technologies—such as artificial intelligence (AI), big data, blockchain, virtual reality (VR), and the Internet of Things (IoT)—are integrated into digital tourism platforms, assessing their dual impact on sustainability and market structures. The study develops a conceptual framework around five key dimensions: market power and digital dependency, AI-driven automation and workforce transformation, innovation and digital inclusion, sustainability innovations, and data security and governance. While digital platforms enhance personalization, operational efficiency, and eco-conscious travel, they also reinforce economic disparities, monopolization, and regulatory challenges, raising concerns related to SDGs such as SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption, and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions). The study highlights the need for equitable governance frameworks to mitigate risks associated with AI-driven monopolization, algorithmic bias, and data privacy violations while ensuring digital accessibility for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on platform economics, digital governance, and sustainable tourism transformation, offering policy and managerial implications for fostering an inclusive and envi

hot.title: Advancing Sustainable Practices in Electronic Customer Relationship Management
hot.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
hot.abstract: This paper examines the role of sustainability in determining organisational development and the manner in which it has become a necessity in conducting business. Thus, this research aims at determining the enhancement of sustainable practices in the e-CRM systems. Thus, using surveys and measuring certain e-CRM possibilities quantitatively, interviews and case analyses as qualitative data gathering, the research offers a systemic understanding of how e-CRM may be utilized to encourage sustainability. The preliminary results also reveal a high concern of the respondents towards the sustainability factor in e-CRM with the mean score of 4.2 and considerable awareness of the benefits like cost advantage measure with the calculated score of 4.5 mean. Companies are moderately challenged when it comes to cost and complexity (mean score 3.8) that restrict the integration of sustainability aspect in e-CRM systems, Nevertheless the implementation and planning of sustainability initiative in e-CRM system is high (current initiatives mean score 3.7, planned initiatives mean score 4.1). The qualitative results and cases reveal the ideas, experiences, examples, and quantifiable results, such as a 25% decrease in the usage of paper in the cases and a 30% decrease in energy use. These findings established that e-CRM strategies can be made sustainable, thereby creating improved communication between firms and their customers, whilst mitigating damages to the environment and supporting the long-term sustainability of organisations.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Hotel certifications are not only crucial for environmental sustainability, but also serve as

hot.title: Digital literacy, digital accessibility, human capital, and entrepreneurial resilience: a case for dynamic business ecosystems
hot.abstract: This study examines the role of digital literacy, digital accessibility, and human capital in fostering entrepreneurial resilience among entrepreneurs in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These countries serve as exemplary models in digital transformation, particularly in navigating crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Grounded in the resource-based view and the theory of dynamic capabilities, this research investigates how these factors contribute to entrepreneurial resilience. This study employs structural equation modeling to analyze survey data from 317 individuals with entrepreneurial experience. According to the findings, digital literacy, accessibility, and human capital significantly enhance innovation, strengthening entrepreneurial resilience. Agility is identified as a key moderator, amplifying the positive impact of these competencies on resilience. Although the success of entrepreneurial ecosystems has often been attributed to entrepreneurial actors, resource providers, connectors, or entrepreneurial intentions, this study underscores the importance of fostering digital competencies and agility to build resilient entrepreneurial ecosystems. It offers policymakers and business leaders insights into the mechanisms that enhance resilience in dynamic and crisis-affected environments where the digital landscape is rapidly evolving.

hot.title: Cognitive offloading or cognitive overload? How AI alters the mental architecture of coping
hot.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from being a specialized technological tool to an intimate presence in everyday life. Smart assistants organize our schedules, predictive systems anticipate our needs, and therapeutic chatbots promise to listen when no human is available (Zhang & Wang, 2024). The diffusion of AI into mental health care is often framed in highly optimistic terms: technologies that reduce stigma, democratize access, and provide affordable, always-on support (M & N, 2025;Sivasubramanian Balasubramanian, 2023). From meditation applications and emotion-tracking wearables to conversational agents offering cognitive-behavioral interventions, AI is marketed as an efficient and reliable partner in the pursuit of wellbeing (Balcombe, 2023).Beneath this enthusiasm lies a paradox. On one hand, AI enables cognitive offloading: the use of external aids to reduce mental effort and conserve resources for more meaningful activities (Grinschgl & Neubauer, 2022;Risko & Gilbert, 2016). This process can support adaptive coping, helping individuals regulate stress and sustain mental health. On the other hand, the same tools may create cognitive overload: an erosion of introspection, over-reliance on algorithmic feedback, and anxiety induced by hyper-monitoring and optimization (Grinschgl et al., 2021;Skulmowski, 2023). The question is not whether AI is good or bad for mental health but how it is reshaping the very architecture of coping (Gerlich, 2025). This article examines the psychology of this paradox. First, it places copings in mainstream psychological theory. Then it considers the promise of AI to lighten burdens through cognitive offloading. Next, it considers the risks of cognitive overload and theoretical insights that illuminate this conflict. Through practic

hot.title: Authenticity in Influencer Marketing: How Can Influencers and Brands Work Together to Build and Maintain Influencer Authenticity?
hot.abstract: This study examines how different stakeholders perceive influencer authenticity, revealing the misalignments that arise when each group prioritizes different aspects of authenticity. In doing so, the authors generate new theory on influencer marketing and provide managerial insights for brands and agencies to collaborate effectively with influencers to resolve these misalignments and ultimately build and sustain influencer authenticity. Using exploratory, in-depth interviews with consumers, influencers, brand managers, and influencer marketing agencies, the study triangulates stakeholder perspectives on influencer authenticity. Specifically, it examines the misalignment among these groups through the lens of assemblage theory and explores how these misalignments may be resolved to produce successful and lasting influencer assemblages. Finally, it explores how influencer marketing agencies can help manage authenticity misalignments.

latest.title: Strategi Komunikasi Coffee Shop Goodhands dalam Menarik Minat Konsumen
latest.abstract: Persaingan usaha Coffee Shop menuntut pelaku usaha menerapkan strategi komunikasi pemasaran yang efektif untuk menarik perhatian dan meningkatkan minat kunjungan konsumen. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis strategi komunikasi Coffee Shop Goodhands dalam menarik minat konsumen berdasarkan model AISAS (Attention, Interest, Search, Action, dan Share). Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis deskriptif. Informan berjumlah enam orang yang terdiri atas satu pemilik usaha, dua karyawan, dan tiga konsumen yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi nonpartisipan, wawancara semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan model Miles dan Huberman. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa tahap Attention dibangun melalui konten visual Instagram yang menampilkan produk, suasana, dan kegiatan Goodhands. Tahap Interest didukung oleh kualitas produk, konsep interior bergaya vintage, pelayanan, dan kegiatan live music. Pada tahap Search, Instagram menjadi sumber informasi mengenai menu, harga, lokasi, dan kegiatan. Tahap Action dipengaruhi oleh promosi, rekomendasi teman, serta pengalaman konsumen, sedangkan tahap Share terlihat melalui unggahan dan rekomendasi langsung. Namun, tahap Action dan Share belum berjalan optimal. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa Goodhands perlu memperkuat konsistensi konten, promosi kegiatan, dan keterlibatan konsumen untuk meningkatkan efektivitas komunikasi serta minat kunjungan.

latest.title: Analisis Pendekatan Personal Selling Beauty Advisor Berbasis Skin Analysis terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen pada Toko Ettra Kosmetik
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi dan Manajemen Indonesia
latest.abstract: Persaingan industri kosmetik dan skincare mendorong toko ritel menghadirkan layanan yang lebih personal bagi konsumen. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan dan menganalisis pendekatan personal selling Beauty Advisor berbasis skin analysis serta kaitannya dengan keputusan pembelian konsumen pada Toko Ettra Kosmetik. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi non-partisipatif, wawancara semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi selama Praktik Kerja Lapangan pada 31 Agustus sampai 20 November 2026, kemudian dianalisis melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa personal selling dijalankan secara konsultatif, adaptif, dan berorientasi pada hubungan, mulai dari approach, identifikasi kebutuhan, presentasi produk dengan tester, penanganan keberatan, closing yang tidak agresif, hingga follow-up. Skin analysis memperkuat tahap identifikasi kebutuhan sehingga rekomendasi produk disesuaikan dengan kondisi kulit, usia, kebiasaan perawatan, dan anggaran konsumen. Kendala utama meliputi ketidaksediaan sebagian konsumen menjalani skin analysis, toko yang ramai, dan ketidaktersediaan stok produk yang direkomendasikan. Penelitian ini belum membuktikan hubungan sebab-akibat antara skin analysis dan keputusan pembelian.

latest.title: Social media, brand image, and price perception as predictors of purchase decisions: Evidence from kopi kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia
latest.venue: The Contrarian Finance Accounting and Business Research
latest.abstract: This study examines whether social media, brand image, and price perception are associated with the purchase decisions of Kopi Kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia, a regional market in which prior findings for this brand are mixed. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 100 customers, recruited through purposive sampling offline and online, was analyzed with multiple linear regression. Social media and brand image were positively and significantly associated with purchase decisions, with effects of comparable and moderate size. Price perception showed no significant association, and its confidence interval included zero, so no direction of effect can be inferred. Together, the three predictors explained about one quarter of the variance in purchase decisions. The study provides jointly estimated effects, confidence intervals, and effect sizes for three commonly studied predictors in an Eastern Indonesian city. Informative social media content and a consistent brand image are associated with purchase decisions, whereas the study offers no evidence for or against a price-perception association. Non-probability sampling, a single time point, self-reported data, and modestly reliable price and purchase-decision scales limit generalization.

latest.title: Longitudinal association between opposite-gender peer relationships and student motivation: testing the random-intercept cross-lagged panel model
latest.abstract: Abstract Background Although the general role of the school social environment in learning motivation has been demonstrated by many researchers, less attention has been paid to the effects of peer relationships, especially opposite-gender peers, on learning motivation, and the mechanisms of interaction between the two are unclear. Furthermore, most researchers have conflated within-subject and between-subject effects, making it impossible to clearly identify the potential interrelationships among variables in longitudinal data, which presents certain statistical limitations. Method The present study explored the longitudinal relationship between adolescents’ opposite-gender peer relationships and students’ motivation through a four-wave longitudinal study of 2,380 students (52% female) using the random intercept cross-lagged panel modeling (RI-CLPM) method. Results The study findings revealed gender differences: changes within adolescents’ relationships with peers of the opposite gender lead to changes in their levels of learning motivation, and this process is more pronounced among males than among females. Specifically, boys who have positive relationships with peers of the opposite gender at a given point in time are likely to exhibit high levels of learning motivation in the future, whereas this effect is not significant among girls, and there is no cross-lagged effect. Conclusion This study aims to reveal the internal interrelationships and directional effects between peer relationships and learning motivation by exploring their dynamic pathways over time. The findings of this study not only enhance the explanatory power of relevant theories within the specific context of opposite-gender peer relationships but also suggest that educators should fully account for ge

latest.title: Content dynamics and their impact on sponsorship efficiency in digital sports broadcasting: a comparative visual exposure analysis via PSG–Bayern Munich and Atletico Madrid–Arsenal matches
latest.venue: BMC Sports Science Medicine and Rehabilitation
latest.abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the associations between content dynamics and sponsorship efficiency in digital sports broadcasting using a computer vision-based approach and to present a comparative exploratory analysis across two distinct European cup matches. The research adopts a computational content analysis method and a comparative multiple case study design. Within the scope of the study, the official match recordings of the Paris Saint-Germain FC – Bayern Munich (April 28, 2026) and Atlético Madrid – Arsenal FC (April 29, 2026) matches broadcasted on the YouTube platform were analyzed. Sponsorship visibility was examined on a per-second basis using a custom AI-driven computer vision algorithm developed in the MATLAB environment, which integrated the Region of Interest (ROI) technique to evaluate in-screen brand density, temporal exposure duration, and spatial positioning parameters. The research findings demonstrate that the sponsorship visibility performance index tends to reach significantly higher levels in matches characterized by high in-game action and tempo. Specifically, sponsorship visibility was found to peak during critical offensive sequences and goal moments, whereas close-up shots and replay sequences were associated with temporary drops in visibility. In the high-action intensity match, the maximum sponsorship visibility index reached a peak score of 1,446 points, whereas the maximum efficiency score in the lower-tempo, highly controlled match was found to be 23.93% lower. Furthermore, it was observed that camera angles, close-ups, and replay sequences preferred by the broadcasting director exhibit strong associations with the screen persistence and visual exposure potential of brands within this two-match observation. latest.title: Impacts of innovation policy on firm green technology innovation based on evidence from a natural experiment in China
latest.abstract: Abstract Can a national innovation-platform policy raise the quality of firms’ green innovation, and if so, through adding resources or by reallocating existing ones? We study China’s Demonstration Bases for Entrepreneurship and Innovation (DBEI), a multi-actor platform policy rolled out in three staggered batches in 2016, 2017, and 2020. Using 41,600 firm-year observations from 4613 Chinese listed firms over 2010–2023, we estimate a staggered difference-in-differences design and corroborate the estimates with heterogeneity-robust estimators (Sun–Abraham and Callaway–Sant’Anna) and a randomization inference permutation test. We find that DBEI designation raises green invention patent grants by about 4.6%, and patent applications by about 3.6%; the effect emerges only from the fourth year after designation and accumulates thereafter, and it is larger for granted and forward-cited patents than for applications—indicating an improvement in innovation quality and direction rather than a mere increase in patent quantity. A distinctive pattern in the channels—digital transformation is significant, whereas human-capital structure and R&D investment are not—supports a reallocation mechanism: the platform lowers coordination and information costs and reorganizes existing factors rather than inducing additional factor inputs. Enterprise-affiliated bases are markedly more effective than university-affiliated and regional bases (an effect roughly eight times larger), which we interpret as evidence that ecosystem performance depends on a firm-centered orchestration mode rather than on the mere presence of complementary actors. latest.title: Working With Robots: How Robot Proportion in Human-Robot Teams and Robot Anthropomorphism Shape Employee Turnover Intention
latest.abstract: Although robots are increasingly reshaping organizational workflows, how the robot proportion in human-robot teams affects employees’ turnover intention remains underexplored. Drawing on conservation of resources theory, we examine whether, why, and when robot proportion exerts divergent effects on turnover intention through two pathways: resource gain and resource loss. Evidence from a scenario-based experiment (Study 1, N = 290) and a three-wave field study (Study 2, N = 306) reveals that these two pathways operate in opposing directions. Specifically, work goal progress and work loneliness mediate the relationship between robot proportion in human-robot teams and turnover intention. Robot anthropomorphism further moderates these pathways: higher anthropomorphism strengthens the beneficial effect on work goal progress, whereas lower anthropomorphism amplifies the detrimental effect on work loneliness. This study offers initial evidence on how the structural composition of human-robot teams shapes employees’ turnover intention, and it provides practical implications for organizations deploying robotic coworkers.

latest.title: SMART RETAILING IN INTERNET COMMERCE: AN AI-ENABLED CUSTOMER-CENTRIC SERVICE FRAMEWORK
latest.venue: EPH - International Journal of Business & Management Science
latest.abstract: This conceptual paper examines AI-enabled smart retailing as a customer-facing service transformation in Internet commerce rather than as a narrow technological or operational innovation. Drawing on a selective, theory-driven synthesis of services marketing, smart retailing, AI-enabled marketing, customer experience, service-dominant logic, human–AI interaction, and responsible-AI research, it develops a three-layer framework linking AI-enabled service capabilities, customer-experience mechanisms, and Internet-commerce outcomes. The framework identifies three capability groups—algorithmic personalisation and decision support, AI-mediated service interaction, and predictive service intelligence—and four evaluative mechanisms: decision value, interaction quality, transaction confidence, and algorithmic legitimacy. These mechanisms shape customer satisfaction, engagement, service-recovery effectiveness, platform trust, relationship quality, continuance intention, value co-creation, and inclusive service value. Human–AI governance, including privacy protection, transparency, fairness, customer control, human review, and digital accessibility, is treated as a boundary condition that determines whether AI-enabled services are perceived as trustworthy and customer-centred or as intrusive, opaque, unfair, and exclusionary. The paper contributes to Internet-commerce research by repositioning AI as a service-enabling capability and by explaining how customer evaluations translate AI applications into commercial and relational outcomes. It also proposes a focused research agenda for empirical testing across e-commerce websites, mobile applications, online marketplaces, social-commerce platforms, and omnichannel systems.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kompensasi dan Lingkungan Kerja terhadap Loyalitas Karyawan Swasta di Kabupaten Aceh Barat
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of compensation and work environment on the loyalty of private sector employees in West Aceh Regency. The study employs a quantitative approach using a survey method with 247 respondents. Data were analyzed through validity, reliability, and classical assumption tests, as well as multiple linear regression with robust standard error HC3. The results indicate that compensation has a positive and significant effect on employee loyalty, with a regression coefficient of 0.590 and a significance value of 0.000. The work environment also has a positive and significant effect, with a regression coefficient of 0.340 and a significance value of 0.000. Simultaneously, compensation and work environment significantly influence employee loyalty. The coefficient of determination value of 0.601 indicates that these variables explain 60.1% of employee loyalty, while the remaining 39.9% is explained by other variables outside the research model. These findings confirm that fair compensation and a conducive work environment are important factors in enhancing the loyalty of private sector employees in West Aceh Regency.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Word of Mouth, Social Media, and Service Quality on Consumer Purchase Decisions at Culinary Businesses in Surakarta, Indonesia
latest.abstract: Purpose— This study examines the associations of word of mouth, social-media engagement, and perceived service quality with reported culinary purchase decisions among consumers in Surakarta, Indonesia. Research Methodology— A quantitative, cross-sectional questionnaire survey involved 150 purposively selected consumers who used social media and had recently visited local culinary establishments. Reported relationships were estimated using PLS-SEM. Results— Social media had the largest reported positive standardized coefficient (β = 0.518), followed by service quality (β = 0.290) and word of mouth (β = 0.180). The model explained 78.2% of variation in the purchase-decision scores. Research limitations/Implications— Purposive recruitment, reliance on self-reports, possible item overlap, and limited reporting of discriminant validity and bootstrapping constrain causal and population-level inference. The findings support context-specific attention to digital information, recommendations, and service encounters. Originality— The study compares three commonly examined predictors within a single model of culinary-consumer evaluations in Surakarta, highlighting their different estimated magnitudes rather than asserting new causal mechanisms.

latest.title: “The impact of technostress on language anxiety and learning outcomes in EFL students: the moderating effect of digital literacy”
latest.venue: Asian-Pacific Journal of Second and Foreign Language Education
latest.abstract: The integration of digital technologies into EFL instruction has introduced technostress, negative psychological responses to technology use, which may influence learners’ emotional states and academic performance. This study investigated the relationships between technostress, language anxiety, and learning outcomes among Iranian undergraduate EFL students, and examined whether digital literacy moderates these relationships. A correlational design was employed with 29 Iranian undergraduate EFL students majoring in English literature and teaching at Yazd University. Given the specialized sample and exploratory nature of the moderation analysis, Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was utilized. Four validated instruments measured technostress, language anxiety, learning outcomes, and digital literacy. Technostress significantly and positively predicted language anxiety (β = 0.491, p = 0.025) and negatively predicted learning outcomes (β = -0.525, p < 0.001). Digital literacy did not significantly moderate either relationship. Unexpectedly, digital literacy showed a strong negative direct effect on learning outcomes (β = -0.653, p < 0.001). Institutional interventions should prioritize reducing unnecessary technological complexity, enhancing platform usability, and fostering learner resilience to ensure that digital tools facilitate rather than hinder language learning.

latest.title: Nghiên cứu các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến hình ảnh thương hiệu du lịch Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh sau sáp nhập thông qua mô hình truyền thông thương hiệu du lịch
latest.abstract: Trong bối cảnh ngành du lịch Việt Nam nỗ lực tái định vị nhằm nâng cao năng lực cạnh tranh quốc tế, việc hình thành các siêu đô thị thông qua sáp nhập hành chính mang lại cơ hội và thách thức cho công tác quản trị thương hiệu điểm đến. Nghiên cứu tập trung vào việc khám phá các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến hình ảnh thương hiệu du lịch Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh mở rộng, một điểm đến liên vùng sau khi hợp nhất với tỉnh Bình Dương và Bà Rịa − Vũng Tàu. Từ góc nhìn diễn giải, nghiên cứu áp dụng thiết kế định tính khám phá với phỏng vấn bán cấu trúc với 10 chuyên gia thuộc ba nhóm bên liên quan. Dữ liệu được phân tích theo quy trình sáu bước phân tích chủ đề của Braun và Clarke, tập trung vào ý nghĩa ngữ nghĩa và lớp nội dung xuyên suốt dữ liệu. Kết quả nhận diện năm chủ đề cốt lõi: (1) Kiến trúc thương hiệu vùng, (2) Truyền thông số, (3) Bản sắc đặc trưng vùng, (4) Quản trị điểm đến, và (5) Nhất quán thông điệp. Nghiên cứu đề xuất mô hình thương hiệu ô (umbrella brand) và bốn nhóm hàm ý quản trị cho giai đoạn sau sáp nhập.

latest.title: TO WHAT EXTENT DOES AI-DRIVEN MARKETING ADOPTION INFLUENCE THE ECONOMIC PERFORMANCE OF VENDOR COMPANIES AND CONSUMER PURCHASING BEHAVIOUR?

latest.title: Who chose the label? Voluntary versus mandated AI disclosure in tourism marketing
latest.abstract: Generative AI is being used extensively by destination marketing organisations (DMOs) to create promotional imagery, and new regulation requires disclosure of some synthetic content. Previous research indicates that revealing an AI source can reduce perceived authenticity but treats disclosure as a single cue. This study investigated whether travellers react differently when the AI label is presented as the DMO's own decision or as a legally mandated requirement. A simulated single factor, three condition (no label, voluntary label, mandated label) between-subjects online experiment with N = 387 adult participants. The analysis was based on the Persuasion Knowledge Model and attribution theory, using ANCOVA, bootstrapped parallel mediation analyses (multicategorical predictor), moderation by attitudes towards AI and robustness checks. Both labels reduced perceived authenticity compared to no label (voluntary: d = −0.59; mandated: d = −0.74). The voluntary label raised perceived DMO integrity (d = 0.38), producing a positive indirect effect on visit intention. The mandated label earned no integrity credit, and its negative indirect effect through authenticity was not compensated. These effects were not significantly moderated by general attitudes toward AI. The study distinguishes between what the AI label says and who is seen to have chosen it, thereby furthering the research on persuasion-knowledge in tourism and providing a model that DMOs can test for disclosure in the regulatory era.

latest.title: Employee Motivation and Performance of Bank of Kigali Rwanda
latest.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
latest.abstract: The study aimed to examine how employee motivation influences the performance of Bank of Kigali Rwanda.To achieve this purpose, attention was given to four specific dimensions of motivation: employee job autonomy, employee compensation, employee growth prospects, and employee recognition and welfare, with each dimension assessed in relation to organizational performance.The study was guided by Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs Theory, and McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y.A descriptive and correlational research design was applied to 129 employees at Bank of Kigali Headquarters, and all 129 respondents participated, yielding a 100% response rate.Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression.Employee job autonomy had a significant positive effect on performance (B = 0.185, β = 0.216, p = 0.016), employee growth prospects produced the strongest significant effect (B = 0.444, β = 0.407, p = 0.000), and employee recognition and welfare was also significant (B = 0.548, β = 0.299, p = 0.001).Employee compensation was positive but marginal at the 5% level (B = 0.192, β = 0.171, p = 0.051).The model explained 31.9% of the variation in Bank of Kigali performance (R² = 0.319).The study concluded that autonomy, growth opportunities, and recognition and welfare were important motivational drivers of performance and recommended strengthening delegated decision-making, competitive compensation practices, structured career development, and formal recognition and employee welfare programs.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Beyond resistance: deinfluencing, consumer activism and the incorporation of critique on digital platforms
latest.abstract: Deinfluencing is a social media trend where content creators advise audiences not to buy ‘must-have,’ overhyped, overpriced, low-quality, or unnecessary products. It serves as a potential form of resistance to the logic of overconsumption. Gaining momentum on TikTok in early 2023, deinfluencing rapidly spread across social media platforms where the meanings and norms of consumption are publicly negotiated and can acquire collective relevance. This conceptual paper proposes a critical reading of the phenomenon, arguing that deinfluencing does not necessarily constitute a negation of influencer marketing, but may instead be incorporated into the commercial arrangements it contests while retaining critical meanings and effects. Situated at the intersection of consumer culture, consumer activism, influencer marketing and platformisation, the paper examines the infrastructural and commercial conditions through which consumer critique acquires visibility and value. It develops a multilevel conceptual model comprising three analytically distinct but potentially overlapping mechanisms through which critical discourse can be incorporated into influencer marketing: substitution , at the content level, whereby criticism of particular products redirects rather than rejects consumption; hybridisation , at the level of practices, whereby influencing and deinfluencing coexist within creators’ communicative repertoire; and authenticity renewal , at the level of audience relations, whereby rejecting some products can strengthen creator credibility and, under certain conditions, the persuasive value of subsequent endorsements. Platformisation conditions the circulation and visibility of these critical practices without determining their effects. Drawing on the sociological concept of bou

latest.title: THE ROLE OF SOCIAL MEDIA INFLUENCERS IN PROMOTING TOURISM DEVELOPMENT IN INDIA
latest.venue: EPRA International Journal of Economics Business and Management Studies
latest.abstract: Social media has changed how travellers discover, judge, and choose destinations, and India is no exception. This study examines how Social Media Influencers (SMIs) shape travel intention among Indian tourists and how this behaviour connects to national tourism development. It combines secondary data from the Ministry of Tourism with a primary survey of 420 Indian tourists who follow at least one travel influencer. A modified Source Credibility Model was tested, with Interactive Engagement and Destination Image added to the classic dimensions of Trustworthiness, Expertise, and Attractiveness. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, and one-way ANOVA were used. The model explains 75.4% of the variance in travel intention. Destination Image, Trustworthiness, Expertise, and Interactive Engagement are significant positive predictors, whereas Attractiveness has a small, negative, and non-significant effect. Travel intention does not differ significantly across age groups, suggesting that credible influencer content persuades Gen Z, Millennials, and older travellers alike. The findings indicate that Indian tourists value useful information and authenticity over appearance when making high-involvement travel decisions. The paper offers practical guidance for Destination Management Organisations (DMOs) and policymakers on selecting influencers, strengthening the Incredible India Digital Platform, and using influencers to spread visitor flows away from overcrowded and ecologically fragile sites.

latest.title: Is global positioning better for pharmaceutical advertising? An experimental study on its impact on brand equity
latest.venue: International Journal of Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Marketing
latest.abstract: Purpose To enhance efficiency in pharmaceutical advertising, this study aims to examine and compare the effects of consumer culture positioning (CCP) – global (GCCP) versus local (LCCP) – and doctor recommendations in direct-to-consumer advertising (DTCA) on skepticism, attitude toward the ad (Aad) and customer-based brand equity (CBBE) and examine the mechanisms through skepticism and Aad. Design/methodology/approach A 2 (CCP: GCCP vs LCCP) × 2 (doctor recommendation: with vs without) between-subject factorial experiment was conducted. Hypotheses were tested using the General Linear Model (GLM) and PROCESS Model 4. Findings CCP significantly influences skepticism, Aad and CBBE, whereas doctor recommendations do not. GCCP generates higher Aad and CBBE and lower skepticism than LCCP. Skepticism and Aad also significantly mediate the effect of CCP and doctor recommendations on CBBE. Research limitations/implications Future research could examine how artificial intelligence and social media influence the effectiveness of GCCP in DTCA, assess GCCP effectiveness across countries and cultures, explore the interpersonal dynamics of doctor recommendations and investigate gender differences in skepticism toward DTCA using GCCP. Practical implications Pharmaceutical companies may consider GCCP in DTCA to improve advertising efficiency through standardized global advertising while enhancing CBBE. Its greater effectiveness than doctor recommendations also suggests more efficient allocation of promotional expenditure. Originality/value This study extends the DTCA literature by examining consumer culture positioning as a previously overlooked determinant of DTCA effectiveness. The findings of this study demonstrate that GCCP can enhance CBBE by reducing skepticism and increasing Aad.

latest.title: Sustainability-oriented Performance Assessment in Construction Companies Using Structural Equation Modeling
latest.abstract: Abstract The construction industry faces increasing pressure to improve environmental sustainability while maintaining organizational performance. This research investigates the relationships among Green Investment (GI), Green Marketing (GM), Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), and Business Performance (BP) within Indonesian construction companies. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was administered to 212 managers and professionals from firms engaged in sustainability initiatives. We used Covariance-Based Structural Equation Modeling (CB-SEM) to evaluate the measurement and structural models. The results indicate that GI significantly affects CSR (β = 0.505, C.R. = 10.587, p < 0.001) and BP (β = 0.473, C.R. = 10.587, p < 0.001). GM also significantly influences CSR (β = 0.437, C.R. = 6.423, p < 0.001) and BP (β = 0.281, C.R. = 4.330, p < 0.001), while CSR significantly affects BP (β = 0.283, C.R. = 3.702, p < 0.001). Furthermore, CSR mediates the effects of GI on BP (βindirect = 0.143, p = 0.001) and GM on BP (βindirect = 0.123, p = 0.002). The structural model demonstrated a good fit (CMIN/DF = 0.924, CFI = 1.000, RMSEA = 0.002). These findings suggest that environmental investment and sustainability-oriented marketing enhance construction-sector performance both directly and through CSR implementation. This study offers an integrated sustainability-performance framework that links resource allocation and market-oriented sustainability practices with organizational responsibility in construction management.

latest.title: The Role of Emotional Attachment in Mediating the Influence of Parasocial Interaction on Impulsive Buying (Study on BTS Fans in Denpasar City)
latest.abstract: The growing popularity of the Korean Wave (Hallyu) in recent years has contributed to increased consumption of South Korean popular culture products, particularly Korean pop (K-pop), across various countries, including Indonesia. The global popularity of BTS has fostered strong emotional connections between fans and their idols through digital interactions on social media platforms. These interactions may facilitate the development of parasocial relationships and emotional attachment, potentially influencing fans' consumption behavior, including impulsive buying. This study aimed to examine and explain the mediating role of emotional attachment in the relationship between parasocial interaction and impulsive buying among BTS fans, collectively known as ARMY, in Denpasar City, Indonesia. The study population comprised BTS fans residing in Denpasar City, from whom 120 respondents were selected using a nonprobability purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 4.0. The findings revealed that parasocial interaction had a positive and statistically significant effect on impulsive buying and emotional attachment. Furthermore, emotional attachment had a positive and statistically significant effect on impulsive buying and partially mediated the relationship between parasocial interaction and impulsive buying. These findings highlighted the importance of parasocial interaction and emotional attachment in explaining impulsive buying tendencies among BTS fans. The study provided insights into the psychological mechanisms underlying fan consumption behavior and offered practical implications for marketers seeking to understand consumer engagement and purchasing decisions within digital fa

latest.title: Pengaruh Digital Marketing, Harga, dan Cita Rasa terhadap Keputusan Pembelian pada Konsumen Dapur Palapa Bireuen
latest.abstract: This study is motivated by the high level of consumer purchase decisions at Dapur Palapa Bireuen, which are presumed to be influenced by digital marketing, price, and taste. This study aims to analyze the effects of these three variables on purchasing decisions, both partially and simultaneously. The study employed a quantitative approach with an associative research design. The sample consisted of 96 consumers who had previously made purchases at Dapur Palapa Bireuen, Bireuen Regency, Aceh. Data were collected through Likert-scale questionnaires. Data analysis included validity and reliability tests, multiple linear regression, t-test, F-test, correlation coefficient, and coefficient of determination. The results indicate that digital marketing has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions (t-count = 4.872; sig. = 0.000), price has a positive and significant effect (t-count = 4.919; sig. = 0.000), and taste has a positive and significant effect (t-count = 3.070; sig. = 0.003). Simultaneously, all three variables have a significant effect on purchasing decisions (F-count = 77.407; sig. = 0.000). The R value of 0.846 indicates a very strong relationship, while the R Square value of 0.716 shows that the three variables contribute 71.6% to purchasing decisions, while the remaining 28.4% is influenced by other factors. This study recommends that management maintain its digital marketing strategies, affordable pricing, product quality alignment, and consistent taste to improve consumer purchasing decisions.

latest.title: Influence of Corporate Social Responsibility on Performance of Selected Commercial Bank of in Rwanda
latest.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
latest.abstract: This study examined the influence of influence of Corporate Social Responsibility on Performance of Selected Commercial Bank of in Rwanda.It specifically, assessed the influence of environmental-based Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) on the performance of selected commercial banks in Rwanda, namely Bank of Kigali, I&M Bank Rwanda, and GT Bank Rwanda.The study adopted a mixed-methods research approach, combining quantitative and qualitative methods.The target population comprised 1,385 employees, and a sample of 310 participants was selected, including 307 questionnaire respondents and three managers designated as key informants.Questionnaires and interview guides were used to collect data.Quantitative data were analysed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), applying descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation, and simple linear regression analysis.Environmental-based CSR recorded an overall mean of 4.32 (SD = 0.68).Paperless and environmentally friendly banking practices received the highest mean (M = 4.41, SD = 0.61), while participation in environmental conservation activities recorded the lowest mean (M = 4.18, SD = 0.77).Pearson's correlation indicated a positive relationship between environmental-based CSR and bank performance (r = 0.611, p < .001).The findings suggest that environmental sustainability policies, paperless banking, environmental conservation, energy-saving practices, and waste management are important aspects of responsible banking.The study recommends strengthening environmental sustainability policies, promoting paperless and digital banking services, and improving energy efficiency and waste management practices to support sustainable banking operations and long-term institutional performance.

latest.title: Perceived Uncertainty and Perceived Performance of Public-Private Partnerships in Kenya: A Project-Level Stakeholder Survey
latest.venue: Research Journal of Business and Finance
latest.abstract: Anchored in Transaction Cost Economics (TCE), this study examined the association between perceived uncertainty and perceived performance of public-private partnerships (PPPs) in Kenya. Uncertainty was measured as perceived exposure to force majeure events, regulatory and policy change, and market volatility, and performance through project efficiency, financial viability, service delivery and stakeholder satisfaction. Adopting a positivist philosophy and an explanatory, cross-sectional survey design, the study collected primary data with structured five-point Likert questionnaires from respondents engaged in PPP implementation across six sectors. A design-stage target of 260 respondents was set from an estimated population of 400; 215 usable questionnaires (82.7% of the target) were returned and aggregated to 67 PPP projects. Data were analysed with descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and simple linear regression. Projects whose respondents reported more uncertainty also reported lower performance (r = −.66, p < .001; B = −0.34, 95% CI [−0.43, −0.24]), and the fitted line accounted for 43% of the sample variance in rated performance. The null hypothesis (H₀: β₁ = 0) was rejected in favour of H₁: β₁ < 0. The study concluded that perceived uncertainty and perceived performance are negatively associated across the projects studied.

latest.title: Mechanisms of Sustainability Influencer Communication: Credibility, Green Trust, and Greenwashing
latest.abstract: The aim of this study is to explore the communication mechanisms through which social media influencers can influence consumers’ environmentally conscious attitudes and their intention to make sustainable purchases. According to the literature, the credibility of the source, value alignment, self-congruity, and parasocial relationships play a key role in the effectiveness of influencer communication. According to a synthesis of the literature, green trust can act as a mediating mechanism contributing to the development of sustainable purchasing intentions, while the perception of greenwashing can weaken the effects of credibility and trust. Even influencers who do not directly address sustainability can have a positive impact if their communication is consistent and aligned with their followers’ values. The theoretical contribution of this study is the development of an integrated conceptual model.

latest.title: Do competencies matter for bank performance? Evidence from Palestinian banking managers
latest.abstract: Despite the global recognition of competencies as fundamental enablers and vital drivers of organizational performance, banks in Palestine operate under persistent and ongoing political and economic instability, regulatory constraints linked to limited sovereignty and a lack of a unified competency framework. These contextual pressures restrict their ability to fully capitalize on competency-based management to support strategic financial objectives. Understanding how competencies relate to managers’ assessments of business performance in this fragile environment is therefore essential. This study examines the relationship between quality-management, behavioral and contextual competencies and senior managers’ perceptions of business performance in the Palestinian banking sector. The study draws on questionnaire responses from 65 of the 66 eligible managers in human resources, credit and facilities and marketing departments, using a census approach. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS. Published financial reports covering five consecutive years were also examined separately from the regression analysis to provide historical context, focusing on profit before tax, return on assets and return on equity. The regression results revealed a positive and statistically significant association between contextual competencies and perceived business performance (p = .001), while quality-management (p = .440) and behavioral competencies (p = .553) showed no statistically significant independent associations. The model explained 67.3% of the variation in the questionnaire-based outcome (R² = .673; adjusted R² = .657). The findings suggest that contextual competencies, particularly those concerning regulatory requirements, stakeholder interests and organization

latest.title: Pengaruh Harga, Kualitas Produk, dan Word of Mouth (WOM) terhadap Keputusan Pembelian di Obama Market
latest.abstract: Increasingly intense retail competition has made consumers more selective in choosing products and shopping destinations. This study aims to analyze the effects of price, product quality, and Word of Mouth (WOM) on consumer purchasing decisions at Obama Market, both partially and simultaneously. This research employs a quantitative approach with a causal design. The population comprises all Obama Market customers, whose exact number is unknown. A sample of 96 respondents was determined using Cochran’s formula and accidental sampling. Data were collected through questionnaires, observations, and documentation, then analyzed using regression analysis and hypothesis testing. The results indicate that price has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a t-value of 9.261 and a significance level of 0.000. Product quality also has a positive and significant effect, with a t-value of 6.376 and a significance level of 0.000. Meanwhile, WOM has a positive and significant effect, with a t-value of 17.299 and a significance level of 0.000. Simultaneously, all three variables have positive and significant effects on purchasing decisions, with an F-value of 1,197.448 and a significance level of 0.000. The Adjusted R-squared value of 0.974 indicates that these variables explain 97.4% of the variation in purchasing decisions, while the remaining 2.6% is attributable to other factors. WOM is the most dominant variable influencing consumer purchasing decisions at Obama Market.

latest.title: IMPROVING MARKETING ACTIVITIES IN UZBEK ENTERPRISES THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES: A MATURITY-BASED MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORK
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming an integral part of marketing practice. However, Uzbek enterprises need a practical instrument for assessing the maturity of their marketing activities and identifying priorities for future investment. This conceptual study proposes a maturity-based management framework grounded in research on AI in marketing, the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities and technology adoption, as well as Uzbekistan's national digitalisation and AI strategies. The framework comprises three components: a system of 20 indicators grouped into five blocks (data foundation; market insights and personalisation; automated communication; organisational capabilities; and governance and compliance); a composite AI Marketing Maturity Index (AMMI), calculated using min–max normalisation and a weighted geometric mean; and a decision matrix linking index ranges to appropriate managerial interventions. A hypothetical example illustrates how the weakest-link property influences investment priorities. Four testable propositions are formulated for subsequent empirical investigation.

latest.title: TO WHAT EXTENT DOES AI-DRIVEN MARKETING ADOPTION INFLUENCE THE ECONOMIC PERFORMANCE OF VENDOR COMPANIES AND CONSUMER PURCHASING BEHAVIOUR?
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Article published in Junior Journal, volume 9.

latest.title: Change fatigue as social contagion: a network dynamics model of propagation, psychological capital mediation, and leadership buffering
latest.abstract: Introduction Change fatigue—the resigned, low-energy response that accumulates as change initiatives pile up—is normally treated as an individual appraisal outcome, yet managers describe it as something that travels across a team. We ask whether workplace ties carry it. Methods Two survey waves, 12 weeks apart, covering 647 employees in 19 departments of four firms, supply communication, advice and emotional support nominations from which we build a weighted multiplex network; a threshold-based susceptible-infected-susceptible formalism supplies the diffusion logic. Results An exponential random graph model shows fatigue-similar employees adjacent more often than chance allows, and a network autocorrelation model returns a positive autoregressive coefficient once the wave-1 baseline, individual covariates and department effects are absorbed. Latent profile analysis recovers three configurations that differ in dimensional composition rather than severity alone. A multilevel 1-1-1 mediation with departments at level 2 indicates that psychological capital transmits roughly a third of the association between exposure to fatigued alters and later fatigue, and moderated path analysis shows the indirect path weakening as leadership change support rises. Agent-based simulation on the empirical topology reproduces the observed distribution, but the gain over a no-change null is slight and shrinks further out of sample, so we read the simulation as a plausibility demonstration rather than confirmation. Discussion Two waves cannot separate influence from homophily or shared exposure; the evidence is consistent with a diffusion account without establishing one.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Analisis Sikap Konsumen dan Strategi SWOT dalam Penguatan Posisi Pasar Produk Minuman Jahe Instan Berserat Rumput Laut
latest.venue: Ranah Research Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Development
latest.abstract: An instant ginger drink enriched with dietary fiber from Gracilaria sp. seaweed is a research-based innovation adopted by a micro enterprise, yet its market reach remains limited. The research gap is that consumer attitude studies and business strategy formulation for innovative fishery products are usually separate, so attributes associated with purchase intention rarely inform strategy. This study analyzed consumer attitudes and purchase intention toward product attributes and formulated a strategy to strengthen the product's market position. In this descriptive quantitative case study, data from 110 purposively selected consumers were analyzed using the Fishbein multiattribute model and Spearman rank correlation, and assessments by eight expert panelists using SWOT analysis. Attitudes were positive to very positive for all eight attributes; the halal label scored highest and ginger taste and aroma lowest. Purchase intention correlated positively with overall attitude, most strongly for dietary fiber and health benefits, but not significantly for the halal label and shelf life information. The enterprise was in quadrant I, supporting an aggressive strategy. The novelty lies in distinguishing attributes that shape attitudes from those associated with purchase intention, positioning dietary fiber and health benefits as differentiators, the halal label as baseline assurance, and ginger flavor and aroma reformulation as the priority improvement

latest.title: Vai trò của nội dung do người dùng tạo ra trong việc hình thành hình ảnh và thương hiệu điểm đến: bằng chứng từ du khách sử dụng mạng xã hội
latest.abstract: Sự lớn mạnh của truyền thông số khiến nội dung do người dùng tạo ra (User-Generated Content – UGC) trên mạng xã hội tác động ngày càng rõ đến cách du khách nhìn nhận các điểm đến du lịch. Nghiên cứu này phân tích vai trò của nội dung do người dùng tạo ra trong việc hình thành hình ảnh điểm đến và nâng cao nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến của du khách. Dựa trên mô hình Kích thích – Chủ thể – Phản ứng (SOR), nghiên cứu đề xuất mô hình phân tích mối quan hệ giữa nội dung do người dùng tạo ra, độ tin cậy của thông tin, hình ảnh điểm đến, nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến và ý định thăm điểm đến. Dữ liệu được thu thập từ 225 người sử dụng mạng xã hội để tìm kiếm thông tin du lịch và được phân tích bằng phương pháp PLS-SEM. Kết quả cho thấy, nội dung do người dùng tạo ra có ảnh hưởng tích cực đến độ tin cậy của thông tin và hình ảnh điểm đến, từ đó tác động đến nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến và ý định thăm điểm đến của du khách.

latest.title: Greenwashing skepticism as a selective moderator: how digital environmental content exposure shapes green e-commerce intentions among Saudi university students
latest.abstract: Introduction As Generation Z consumers increasingly engage with digital platforms in response to environmental considerations, understanding how online sustainability messaging shapes green e-commerce behavior becomes more pressing. Digitalization is often assumed to equalize access to sustainability information, yet digital divide research shows that inequalities persist in how online content is converted into outcomes. Drawing on the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study examines how exposure to digital environmental content (DECE) shapes green e-consumption intention (GECI) among digitally literate Saudi university students. Methods Environmental awareness and personal responsibility (EAR) and message credibility (MC) were modeled as two parallel mediators linking DECE to GECI, with no hypothesized path between them. Greenwashing perception (GP) was expected to moderate specifically the effect of MC on GECI, and perceived barriers (PB) were examined as an independent predictor of GECI. Data from 305 respondents were analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Results The model explained substantial variance in GECI ( R ² = 0.603; Q ² = 0.577). DECE had a significant direct effect on GECI ( β = 0.190, p = 0.001). The EAR-mediated pathway was dominant ( β = 0.311, f ² = 0.333), whereas the MC-mediated pathway was non-significant ( β = 0.006, p = 0.823). GP moderated the credibility–intention link (MC → GECI; β = −0.114, p = 0.005) but not the exposure–intention link (DECE → GECI; β = 0.070, p = 0.095), suggesting that greenwashing skepticism acts as a credibility-related barrier. PB was positively associated with GECI ( β = 0.138, p = 0.023), a counter-intuitive association interpreted tentativ

latest.title: Pengaruh Content Marketing terhadap Purchase Intention dengan Customer Engagement sebagai Variabel Mediasi pada Platform Marketplace Shopee
latest.venue: Jurnal Inovasi Manajemen, Kewirausahaan, Bisnis dan Digital.
latest.abstract: The increasing competition among marketplace platforms has encouraged companies to utilize content marketing as a strategy to influence consumer behavior, particularly purchase intention. This study aims to analyze the effect of content marketing on purchase intention with customer engagement as a mediating variable among Shopee marketplace users in Makassar City. This research employed a quantitative approach using a survey method involving 110 respondents selected through purposive sampling technique. Data were collected using Likert-scale questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Square-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that content marketing has a positive and significant effect on customer engagement and purchase intention. However, customer engagement does not have a significant effect on purchase intention and is unable to mediate the relationship between content marketing and purchase intention. These findings suggest that consumers’ purchase intentions on the Shopee marketplace are more directly influenced by the quality and relevance of content rather than by customer engagement. This study provides empirical contributions to the development of digital consumer behavior research, particularly regarding the limited role of customer engagement as a mediating variable in the marketplace context. The practical implication of this study is that businesses should optimize informative, relevant, and engaging content marketing strategies to enhance consumers’ purchase intention on digital platforms.

latest.title: Necro-Branding in ethical fashion: the moderating roles of minimalist visuals and celebrity characteristics with the mediating role of moral resonance
latest.abstract: This study explores Necro-Branding, the use of deceased celebrities in marketing, as a novel strategy to boost consumer engagement in ethical fashion on social media. Analysing 12,518 Instagram posts from 11 ethical fashion accounts using tools including Google Cloud Vision and the Moral Foundations Dictionary, we find Necro-Celebrity endorsements significantly enhance engagement. The effect is moderated by minimalist visuals and celebrity traits, mediated by moral resonance. More visible and older celebrities perform best. Our research provides the first empirical evidence on the role of Necro-Branding in ethical fashion, with the causal main effect and the mediating role of moral resonance confirmed in a follow-up online experiment. These findings provide strategic guidance for marketers seeking to promote sustainability while respectfully leveraging legacy figures for strong(er) audience connection.

latest.title: When Firms Go Influencer: Engagement in the Influencer Economy and Crash Risk
latest.abstract: As social media ecosystems evolve and digital communication channels become increasingly influential, firms are incorporating the influencer economy into their marketing strategies and operational decisions. Despite the growing prevalence of firms’ participation in the influencer economy, its implications for capital market outcomes, particularly stock price crash risk, remain largely unexplored. This study uses a panel of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2016 to 2024 to construct a firm-level measure of influencer-economy engagement based on textual information extracted from annual reports and investigates its association with crash risk. The results demonstrate that firms with greater engagement in the influencer economy are less likely to experience stock-price crashes. Further analyses indicate that this relationship operates through enhanced external monitoring, stronger reputational capital, and improved value creation capacity, all of which contribute to a transparent information environment and stable market expectations. Moreover, the mitigating effect is particularly evident among highly profitable firms, firms in eastern China, and firms operating in high-technology industries. These findings extend the existing research on the digital economy and capital markets by identifying the risk implications of firm engagement in the influencer economy. Furthermore, the results provide insights for regulators and investors regarding the role of digital communication strategies in shaping market outcomes.

latest.title: Impact of Sustainability-Oriented Marketing on Consumer Attitudes and Purchase Decisions
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The increasing urgency of environmental and social challenges has positioned sustainability at the forefront of modern marketing practices. This study explores the role of marketing and consumer behavior in achieving a sustainable future by examining how marketing strategies influence consumer attitudes and purchasing decisions toward environmentally responsible products. The research focuses on key elements such as green advertising, eco-labeling, and corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives, and their impact on shaping consumer perceptions and trust. Using a combination of primary and secondary data, the study analyzes consumer awareness, preferences, and behavioral patterns related to sustainable consumption. The findings indicate a significant positive relationship between sustainability-oriented marketing efforts and pro-environmental consumer behavior. Consumers are increasingly inclined to support brands that demonstrate transparency, ethical practices, and environmental commitment, although factors such as price sensitivity and limited awareness continue to affect purchasing decisions. The study highlights the importance of leveraging consumer insights to design effective marketing strategies that encourage responsible consumption. It concludes that businesses integrating sustainability into their marketing frameworks can enhance brand loyalty, gain competitive advantage, and contribute meaningfully to sustainable development. The research offers practical implications for marketers, policymakers, and organizations aiming to foster a more sustainable and consumer-driven marketplace.

latest.title: Claims Handling Efficiency and Customer Satisfaction: A Case of Zigama Credit and Savings Society in Kigali, Rwanda
latest.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
latest.abstract: This study examined the influence of claims handling efficiency on customer satisfaction at Zigama Credit and Savings Society in Rwanda.It addressed limited empirical evidence concerning claims processing timeliness, transparency in claims procedures, and claim-related communication effectiveness within cooperative financial institutions.Guided by Expectations Confirmation Theory and SERVQUAL Model, the study adopted an explanatory mixed-methods research design.The target population comprised 240 customers, with a sample of 218 respondents selected through stratified random sampling.Data were collected using structured questionnaires and key informant interviews and analyzed through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and regression analysis using SPSS.Claims processing timeliness positively influenced customer satisfaction, recording an overall mean of 4.01, a significant correlation (r = 0.689, p < 0.001), and a positive regression coefficient (β = 0.462, p < 0.001).Transparency in claims procedures also showed a significant relationship with customer satisfaction (mean = 4.00; r = 0.724, p < 0.001; β = 0.503, p < 0.001).Claim-related communication effectiveness recorded the strongest association and coefficient (mean = 3.99; r = 0.748, p < 0.001; β = 0.538, p < 0.001).The study concluded that efficient claims processing, transparent procedures, and effective communication contributed positively to customer satisfaction at Zigama Credit and Savings Society.It recommended improving digital claims systems, clarifying procedural requirements, providing timely customer updates, and strengthening claims officers' communication skills through continuous training and promote consistent monitoring of claims performance.These measures could improve service quality, cu

latest.title: Social Media Marketing and Customer Purchase Decisions in Enugu State, Nigeria
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This study examined the relationship between social media marketing and customer purchase decisions in Enugu State, Nigeria. Specifically, the study sought to examine the relationship between social media advertising and customer purchase decisions, and ascertain the relationship between social media engagement and customer purchase decisions in Enugu State. The study was conducted among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Enugu State and adopted a descriptive survey research design. Primary data were collected through the administration of structured questionnaires. The population of the study comprised 1,102 respondents, while a sample size of 284 was determined using Freund and Williams' statistical formula at a 5% margin of error. Out of the 284 questionnaires distributed, 244 were correctly completed and returned. The data collected were presented and analysed using descriptive statistics, while the hypotheses were tested using the Z-test statistic. The findings revealed that social media advertising had a significant positive relationship with customer purchase decisions in Enugu State, Nigeria (Z = 7.752, p < .05). Similarly, social media engagement had a significant positive relationship with customer purchase decisions (Z = 8.087, p < .05). The study concluded that social media marketing plays an important role in influencing customer purchase decisions in Enugu State, Nigeria.
