hot.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Personalizing Social Media Marketing Strategies for Enhanced Customer Experience
hot.abstract: This paper explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in personalizing social media marketing strategies and its impact on customer experience, with a focus on consumers within the MENA region. Using data collected from an online questionnaire completed by 893 individuals, the study confirms that AI significantly enhances social media marketing by offering personalized content, optimizing influencer selection, and enabling real-time consumer interaction. These capabilities not only increase customer awareness but also improve user experience and purchase intentions. Key AI tools such as influencer marketing, content optimization, and customization are effective in capturing consumer attention, although further research is necessary to deepen understanding. By examining AI's ability to analyze vast datasets and support targeted marketing efforts, the study contributes to both academic and practical discourse, offering insights that businesses can use to refine their AI-driven social media strategies. Ultimately, the research aims to guide marketers through the complexities of AI deployment, ensuring its benefits are fully realized for consumers.

hot.title: Influence of short video content on consumers purchase intentions on social media platforms with trust as a mediator
hot.abstract: Short videos on social media platforms have boomed with the rapid growth of the video consumption industry and have become an important marketing tool for businesses. With the rise of platforms such as TikTok or Douyin, short videos have profoundly impacted consumer behavior, making it crucial to understand their role in shaping consumer purchase intention. However, there is still a need for further research on how short video content promotes consumer purchase intent. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, this study constructs a structural model to explore the impact of short video content on consumer purchase intention, focusing on the mediating role of consumer trust. The model incorporates usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment as external stimuli, consumer trust as internal psychological responses, and purchase intention as the final behavioral outcome. This study collected 372 valid data from Chinese consumers through an online questionnaire and empirically analyzed it using structural equation modeling. The study results show that short-form video content's usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment significantly affect consumers' trust and purchase intention. Moreover, consumer trust positively affects purchase intention and mediates the relationship between short video content and purchase behavior. This research extends the application of the SOR model to the context of social media short videos, highlighting the crucial role of consumer trust in shaping consumer purchase decisions. Based on these findings, we propose actionable strategies for businesses to optimize short video content and build consumer trust, ultimately enhancing marketing effectiveness and driving consumer purchases.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
hot.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies sparked a rapid development of smartphone applications designed to help individuals experiencing mental health problems through an AI-powered chatbot agent. However, the safety of such agents when dealing with individuals experiencing a mental health crisis, including suicidal crisis, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed the ability of 29 AI-powered chatbot agents to respond to simulated suicidal risk scenarios. Application repositories were searched and the app descriptions screened in search of apps that claimed to be beneficial when experiencing mental distress and offered an AI-powered chatbot function. All agents were tested with a standardized set of prompts based on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale designed to simulate increasing suicidal risk. We assessed the responses according to pre-defined criteria based on the ability to provide emergency contact information and other factors. None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate. Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding. These findings raise concerns about the deployment of AI-powered chatbots in sensitive health contexts without proper clinical validation.

hot.title: Barriers and Enablers of AI Adoption in Human Resource Management: A Critical Analysis of Organizational and Technological Factors
hot.abstract: This paper examines the key factors recognized as transformative in the field of human resource management (HRM) and explores their influence on the global adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). While AI holds significant promise for enhancing HRM efficiency, employee engagement, and Decision Making, its implementation presents a range of organizational, technical, and ethical challenges that organizations worldwide must navigate. Change aversion, data security worries, and integration expenses are major roadblocks, but strong digital leadership, company culture, and advancements in NLP and machine learning are key enablers. This paper presents a complex analysis that questions the common perception of AI as only disruptive by delving into the relationship between power dynamics, corporate culture, and technology infrastructures. In this paper, we bring together research from several fields to help scholars and practitioners understand the nuances of AI adoption in HRM, with an emphasis on the importance of inclusive methods and ethical frameworks.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: A Comparison of Responses from Human Therapists and Large Language Model–Based Chatbots to Assess Therapeutic Communication: Mixed Methods Study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consumers are increasingly using large language model-based chatbots to seek mental health advice or intervention due to ease of access and limited availability of mental health professionals. However, their suitability and safety for mental health applications remain underexplored, particularly in comparison to professional therapeutic practices. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate how general-purpose chatbots respond to mental health scenarios and compare their responses to those provided by licensed therapists. Specifically, we sought to identify chatbots' strengths and limitations, as well as the ethical and practical considerations necessary for their use in mental health care. METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods study to compare responses from chatbots and licensed therapists to scripted mental health scenarios. We created 2 fictional scenarios and prompted 3 chatbots to create 6 interaction logs. We recruited 17 therapists and conducted study sessions that consisted of 3 activities. First, therapists responded to the 2 scenarios using a Qualtrics form. Second, therapists went through the 6 interaction logs using a think-aloud procedure to highlight their thoughts about the chatbots' responses. Finally, we conducted a semistructured interview to explore subjective opinions on the use of chatbots for supporting mental health. The study sessions were analyzed using thematic analysis. The interaction logs from chatbot and therapist responses were coded using the Multitheoretical List of Therapeutic Interventions codes and then compared to each other. RESULTS: We identified 7 themes describing the strengths and limitations of the chatbots as compared to therapists. These include elements of good therapy in chatbot responses, conversational style of c

hot.title: The multinational enterprise, capabilities, and digitalization: governance and growth with world disorder
hot.abstract: Abstract This essay revisits my 2014 JIBS article about the potential for integrating international business internalization theory with a strategic management capabilities perspective. It recaps the capabilities framework with an emphasis on the learning required of emerging market multinationals and illustrates this with the case of Hyundai Motor Company’s internationalization and growth. It also discusses two aspects of the global economy that have become more prominent since 2014 in shaping international business: geopolitical uncertainty and digitalization. A rise in geopolitical tensions appears to be rebalancing the relationships between multinationals and home/host governments. Digitalization facilitates international business; but it adds new vulnerabilities by (further) accelerating competition, enabling new rivals, and introducing systemic risks into digital supply chains. Implications for managers, board members, and international business scholars are drawn.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.

hot.title: The Role of Digital Tourism Platforms in Advancing Sustainable Development Goals in the Industry 4.0 Era
hot.abstract: The intersection of digitalization and sustainability is reshaping the tourism industry, with digital platforms playing a transformative role in optimizing travel experiences while simultaneously influencing economic inclusivity, labor dynamics, and environmental responsibility. This paper explores how Industry 4.0 technologies—such as artificial intelligence (AI), big data, blockchain, virtual reality (VR), and the Internet of Things (IoT)—are integrated into digital tourism platforms, assessing their dual impact on sustainability and market structures. The study develops a conceptual framework around five key dimensions: market power and digital dependency, AI-driven automation and workforce transformation, innovation and digital inclusion, sustainability innovations, and data security and governance. While digital platforms enhance personalization, operational efficiency, and eco-conscious travel, they also reinforce economic disparities, monopolization, and regulatory challenges, raising concerns related to SDGs such as SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption, and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions). The study highlights the need for equitable governance frameworks to mitigate risks associated with AI-driven monopolization, algorithmic bias, and data privacy violations while ensuring digital accessibility for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on platform economics, digital governance, and sustainable tourism transformation, offering policy and managerial implications for fostering an inclusive and envi

hot.title: Greenwashing and market value of firms: An empirical study
hot.abstract: In today's business environment, green or sustainable claims are rising as companies strive to strengthen environmental practices in response to climate change and sustainable development challenges. However, with increasing expectations of sustainable performance, companies encounter mounting financial pressure to adopt more efficient sustainable practices, which may lead some to exploit sustainability efforts for their own gain. Many companies make environmentally friendly assertions to conceal or mask their actual activities—a phenomenon known as greenwashing—which fosters public scepticism about the authenticity of their green messaging. This study employs an event study methodology to examine how the stock market values greenwashing news, drawing on 121 global greenwashing news since the 2015 Paris Agreement. Our findings reveal a negative correlation between greenwashing news and stock market reactions. The market reactions to greenwashing news are more negative for firms with greater ESG performance than for weak ESG performance. Additionally, greenwashing news supported by concrete evidence elicits stronger adverse reactions. Companies operating in the manufacturing industry experience more significant market value losses than those in the service sector. The findings also indicate that the Asia-Pacific market demonstrates particularly strong negative responses to greenwashing news compared to other stock markets. This study contributes to the signalling theory and advances the literature on corporate sustainability practices by providing empirical insights in a global context.

hot.title: Advancing Sustainable Practices in Electronic Customer Relationship Management
hot.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
hot.abstract: This paper examines the role of sustainability in determining organisational development and the manner in which it has become a necessity in conducting business. Thus, this research aims at determining the enhancement of sustainable practices in the e-CRM systems. Thus, using surveys and measuring certain e-CRM possibilities quantitatively, interviews and case analyses as qualitative data gathering, the research offers a systemic understanding of how e-CRM may be utilized to encourage sustainability. The preliminary results also reveal a high concern of the respondents towards the sustainability factor in e-CRM with the mean score of 4.2 and considerable awareness of the benefits like cost advantage measure with the calculated score of 4.5 mean. Companies are moderately challenged when it comes to cost and complexity (mean score 3.8) that restrict the integration of sustainability aspect in e-CRM systems, Nevertheless the implementation and planning of sustainability initiative in e-CRM system is high (current initiatives mean score 3.7, planned initiatives mean score 4.1). The qualitative results and cases reveal the ideas, experiences, examples, and quantifiable results, such as a 25% decrease in the usage of paper in the cases and a 30% decrease in energy use. These findings established that e-CRM strategies can be made sustainable, thereby creating improved communication between firms and their customers, whilst mitigating damages to the environment and supporting the long-term sustainability of organisations.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Hotel certifications are not only crucial for environmental sustainability, but also serve as

latest.title: Coping with sustainability information overload: The role of generative artificial intelligence literacy
latest.venue: Ho Chi Minh City Open University Journal of Science- Economics and Business Administration
latest.abstract: Consumers can use sustainability information to consume responsibly; however, excessive and complex sustainability claims might confuse consumers and hinder proper evaluations. Based on cognitive appraisal theory, this study empirically investigates the impacts of sustainability information overload (SIO) on green information avoidance (GIA) and green information verification behavior (GIVB) and examines the moderating role of generative AI literacy (GAIL) and the associations of GIA and GIVB with green purchase decision confidence (GPDC). Data from an online cross-sectional survey of 468 adult consumers in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings revealed that SIO positively influenced GIA, and GIA negatively influenced GPDC. However, SIO did not negatively influence GIVB on average. GAIL significantly moderated the SIO-GIVB relationship: SIO was negatively associated with GIVB at low GAIL but not significantly at mean or high GAIL.GIVB positively influenced GPDC. An indirect effect of SIO on GPDC through GIA is significant, but the indirect effect through GIVB is not significant unconditionally. These results suggest that sustainability information overload is associated with distinct coping responses. From a practical perspective, sustainability portals and shopping applications involving GenAI should emphasize evaluability and verifiability rather than enhancing disclosures. Through defining GAIL as a digitally mediated capability from the consumer’s perspective which can serve as a coping tool, this paper builds on cognitive appraisal theory in the context of AI-mediated sustainable consumption and explains the critical engagement of consumers with sustainability information amid overload situations

latest.title: SMART RETAILING IN INTERNET COMMERCE: AN AI-ENABLED CUSTOMER-CENTRIC SERVICE FRAMEWORK
latest.venue: EPH - International Journal of Business & Management Science
latest.abstract: This conceptual paper examines AI-enabled smart retailing as a customer-facing service transformation in Internet commerce rather than as a narrow technological or operational innovation. Drawing on a selective, theory-driven synthesis of services marketing, smart retailing, AI-enabled marketing, customer experience, service-dominant logic, human–AI interaction, and responsible-AI research, it develops a three-layer framework linking AI-enabled service capabilities, customer-experience mechanisms, and Internet-commerce outcomes. The framework identifies three capability groups—algorithmic personalisation and decision support, AI-mediated service interaction, and predictive service intelligence—and four evaluative mechanisms: decision value, interaction quality, transaction confidence, and algorithmic legitimacy. These mechanisms shape customer satisfaction, engagement, service-recovery effectiveness, platform trust, relationship quality, continuance intention, value co-creation, and inclusive service value. Human–AI governance, including privacy protection, transparency, fairness, customer control, human review, and digital accessibility, is treated as a boundary condition that determines whether AI-enabled services are perceived as trustworthy and customer-centred or as intrusive, opaque, unfair, and exclusionary. The paper contributes to Internet-commerce research by repositioning AI as a service-enabling capability and by explaining how customer evaluations translate AI applications into commercial and relational outcomes. It also proposes a focused research agenda for empirical testing across e-commerce websites, mobile applications, online marketplaces, social-commerce platforms, and omnichannel systems.

latest.title: Paradoxical leadership and preschool teachers' innovative behavior: the mediating role of psychological capital and the moderating role of professional identity
latest.abstract: Introduction This study examined how kindergarten-level paradoxical leadership, characterized by high performance expectations and strong management support, is associated with preschool teachers' innovative behavior, and whether psychological capital and professional identity explain and condition this association. Methods Survey data from 1,029 preschool teachers nested within 91 kindergartens in China were analyzed using multilevel models to account for the hierarchical data structure. Indirect and conditional indirect associations were evaluated using cluster bootstrap confidence intervals obtained by resampling kindergartens. Results The findings showed that paradoxical leadership was positively associated with teachers' psychological capital and innovative behavior. Psychological capital accounted for a positive indirect association between paradoxical leadership and innovative behavior at the between-kindergarten level. Professional identity strengthened the positive association between paradoxical leadership and psychological capital, as well as the corresponding indirect association with innovative behavior. At lower levels of professional identity, neither association was statistically distinguishable from zero. Discussion These findings suggest that paradoxical leadership is associated with preschool teachers' innovative behavior partly through their psychological capital, with professional identity shaping the strength of this pathway. By identifying a cross-level psychological pathway and its boundary condition, the study extends paradoxical leadership research to early childhood education. Practically, the findings suggest that kindergarten principals should combine clear performance expectations with meaningful management support, while professional devel
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: What drives sustainable fashion behaviour: fashion interest and environmental attitudes
latest.abstract: Introduction: The fashion industry is among the most resource-intensive and polluting consumer sectors, and consumer behavior is central to reducing its environmental impact. Although research has extensively examined pro-environmental attitudes, it has treated fashion interest inconsistently, often assuming it conflicts with sustainability despite evidence that sustainable consumers can be highly fashion-conscious. This study examines how environmental attitudes and fashion interest relate to clothing behavior across the consumption cycle, distinguishing three behavioral types: sufficiency (buying less, keeping garments longer), care and efficiency (maintenance, repair, lower-impact laundering), and circular and reuse (second-hand acquisition and diverting used clothing from disposal). Materials and methods: Drawing on an online survey of 2000 Canadian consumers, we measured fashion interest using standardized scales. We regressed each of 27 ordinal outcomes on the two attitudes using ordered logistic regression; reported odds ratios per standard deviation, with and without demographic controls; and verified results with Brant tests, generalized ordered logit models, and false-discovery-rate correction. Results: The two attitudes function as distinct motivational orientations, with associations that vary systematically by behavioral type. Environmental attitude is positively associated with sustainable behavior across all three types and is unaffected by demographic controls. Fashion interest is the strongest predictor of purchase frequency but is not uniformly unsustainable: it is positively associated with circular and reuse behaviors, negatively with sufficiency behaviors, and only weakly and inconsistently with care and efficiency behaviors. Conclusions: The centra

latest.title: Greenwashing skepticism as a selective moderator: how digital environmental content exposure shapes green e-commerce intentions among Saudi university students
latest.abstract: Introduction As Generation Z consumers increasingly engage with digital platforms in response to environmental considerations, understanding how online sustainability messaging shapes green e-commerce behavior becomes more pressing. Digitalization is often assumed to equalize access to sustainability information, yet digital divide research shows that inequalities persist in how online content is converted into outcomes. Drawing on the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study examines how exposure to digital environmental content (DECE) shapes green e-consumption intention (GECI) among digitally literate Saudi university students. Methods Environmental awareness and personal responsibility (EAR) and message credibility (MC) were modeled as two parallel mediators linking DECE to GECI, with no hypothesized path between them. Greenwashing perception (GP) was expected to moderate specifically the effect of MC on GECI, and perceived barriers (PB) were examined as an independent predictor of GECI. Data from 305 respondents were analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Results The model explained substantial variance in GECI ( R ² = 0.603; Q ² = 0.577). DECE had a significant direct effect on GECI ( β = 0.190, p = 0.001). The EAR-mediated pathway was dominant ( β = 0.311, f ² = 0.333), whereas the MC-mediated pathway was non-significant ( β = 0.006, p = 0.823). GP moderated the credibility–intention link (MC → GECI; β = −0.114, p = 0.005) but not the exposure–intention link (DECE → GECI; β = 0.070, p = 0.095), suggesting that greenwashing skepticism acts as a credibility-related barrier. PB was positively associated with GECI ( β = 0.138, p = 0.023), a counter-intuitive association interpreted tentativ

latest.title: Impact of Sustainability-Oriented Marketing on Consumer Attitudes and Purchase Decisions
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The increasing urgency of environmental and social challenges has positioned sustainability at the forefront of modern marketing practices. This study explores the role of marketing and consumer behavior in achieving a sustainable future by examining how marketing strategies influence consumer attitudes and purchasing decisions toward environmentally responsible products. The research focuses on key elements such as green advertising, eco-labeling, and corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives, and their impact on shaping consumer perceptions and trust. Using a combination of primary and secondary data, the study analyzes consumer awareness, preferences, and behavioral patterns related to sustainable consumption. The findings indicate a significant positive relationship between sustainability-oriented marketing efforts and pro-environmental consumer behavior. Consumers are increasingly inclined to support brands that demonstrate transparency, ethical practices, and environmental commitment, although factors such as price sensitivity and limited awareness continue to affect purchasing decisions. The study highlights the importance of leveraging consumer insights to design effective marketing strategies that encourage responsible consumption. It concludes that businesses integrating sustainability into their marketing frameworks can enhance brand loyalty, gain competitive advantage, and contribute meaningfully to sustainable development. The research offers practical implications for marketers, policymakers, and organizations aiming to foster a more sustainable and consumer-driven marketplace.

latest.title: Buy Smart: Estudio piloto de un juego de mesa cooperativo para trabajar el consumo responsable en educación infantil
latest.abstract: This study presents a pilot assessment of the effectiveness and potential for improvement of a cooperative board game aimed at promoting the purchase of local and seasonal products and reducing waste generation. The game was piloted in three preschool classrooms comprising 41 children aged 4-5 years. Qualitative feedback was collected from teachers to assess its playability, suitability, and pedagogical value. Educators highlighted the importance of engaging materials, simple rules, and prior contextual instruction to support meaningful participation. The findings suggest that, although responsible consumption is a challenging concept for children at this developmental stage, sustainability learning can be supported by collaborative games through guided play. Finally, the study provides a framework for evaluating analogue educational games and underscores the potential of play-based learning to promote critical environmental thinking in early childhood education.

latest.title: Emission Differentiation as a Self‐Financing Transition Mechanism: The Case of Sustainability in Automotive Repair and Maintenance
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Global commitments to reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions have focused policy and managerial attention on upstream production and use‐phase emissions, leaving downstream repair and maintenance services (RMS) largely overlooked. This paper examines whether lower‐emission service provision can become a self‐financing differentiation strategy for capital‐constrained, small‐ and medium‐sized service firms. We develop a price‐competition model where firms choose between traditional and cleaner service offerings, and customers exhibit heterogeneous emission sensitivity. From this framework, we derive a self‐financing condition that links emission‐sensitive demand, market size, operating‐cost variations, and upfront abatement investments. To ground the model empirically, we collect detailed operational data from 13 German and 6 Australian RMS shops, combining these inputs with life cycle assessment (LCA) estimates to map Scope 1–3 emission channels and characterize abatement pathways. The results show that energy‐related measures in heating and electricity provide low‐risk entry points that reduce or stabilize operating costs. Conversely, spare parts and material strategies dominate total lifecycle emissions; while they offer higher absolute abatement potential, they demand greater capital investment and value‐chain coordination. This study contributes to the business case for sustainability literature by demonstrating that environmental differentiation operates not only as a demand‐side premium driver but also as an operating‐cost and investment‐feasibility mechanism. Finally, we offer actionable guidance for RMS managers, insurers, Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), and policymakers on sequencing decarbonization pathways within service industries dominated

latest.title: Diseño de un modelo de negocio circular para la revalorización de residuos textiles postconsumo mediante un enfoque Design Science Research
latest.venue: Ibero Ciencias - Revista Científica y Académica
latest.abstract: Waste management poses major challenges for the transition toward sustainable production and consumption models, particularly for post-consumer textiles. This study presents an alternative approach to recovering these materials through collaborative practices independent of conventional textile production. A circular business model was developed using the Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, integrating a situational assessment in the Laguna Metropolitan Area (ZML), preliminary design, and iterative cycles enriched by the practical experience of upcyclers through interviews and participatory workshops for social, educational, operational, and financial validation. The result is an operational structure capable of generating social and economic value from locally recovered post-consumer textile waste, offering a practical framework with potential for application and adaptation to different contexts.

latest.title: A consumer neuroscience approach to examining how augmented reality and QR codes support product and brand sustainability communication in retail settings
latest.abstract: This research explores the use of Augmented Reality (AR) and Quick Response (QR) codes as tools for communicating sustainability-related information in a quasi-realistic retail setting. It combines neurophysiological and self-report measures to investigate how these technologies influence consumers’ sustainability perceptions, emotional engagement, and cognitive workload. Participants took part in a simulated shopping experience, where they were exposed to one of three experimental conditions: traditional packaging, smartphone-mediated QR code scanning, and smartphone-mediated Augmented Reality exploration of coffee packaging. Cognitive workload (measured via electroencephalography) and emotional engagement (measured via skin conductance and heart rate) were recorded alongside self-report measures of green company orientation (GCO), green product informativeness (GPI), and brand familiarity. Findings indicate that while both AR and QR codes evoke more positive emotions and lead to higher perceptions of GCO and GPI, AR usage is also associated with higher cognitive workload. Additionally, brand familiarity enhanced self-report scores but not neurophysiological ones, without interacting with the interaction modality. This research provides a multi-level (implicit neurophysiological and explicit self-reported) perspective on the impact of digital packaging formats on sustainability communication. The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on how interactive technologies can support effective communication, implicit emotions, and consumer engagement with sustainability in retail environments.

latest.title: Different Strokes for Different Folks: Exploring Algorithmic Fairness and Trust in Generative Artificial Intelligence
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is widely used to personalize recommendations, yet questions remain about the representativeness of algorithmic recommendations to recognize diverse consumer needs. This research integrates the stimulus‐organism‐response model and social identity theory to inform how personalization influences recommendation acceptance through algorithmic fairness and trust and how communication style affects these processes, which may differ between ethnic groups. Using a sequential explanatory design, Study 1 ( n = 136) shows that high personalization increases recommendation acceptance, perceived algorithmic fairness and trust compared with low personalization based on an experiment. Study 2 ( n = 300) identifies a positive sequential indirect effect through algorithmic fairness and trust, with competence‐oriented communication producing a stronger effect than warmth‐oriented communication based on an experiment. Study 3 ( n = 340) further reveals differences in these relationships across ethnic groups using a quasi‐experiment. Study 4 ( n = 14) employs semi‐structured interviews to contextualize these findings and explore the underlying reasoning. Theoretically, the findings extend GenAI personalization literature by identifying fairness and trust as key pathways to recommendation acceptance and highlighting ethnic differences in these processes. Practically, the findings guide strategies for GenAI developers to create more equitable and context‐sensitive design across diverse consumers.

latest.title: ЦИРКУЛЯРНА ЕКОНОМІКА ЯК ЛОГІЧНА МОДЕЛЬ ФІЛОСОФІЇ СУЧАСНОГО БІЗНЕСУ
latest.abstract: The link between the circular economy model and sustainable development stems from Sustainable Development Goal 12, which aims to ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns. This is important given the significant growth rates in resource consumption worldwide. Therefore, it is crucial to develop a model that promotes the efficient use of resources, reduces waste and creates business sustainability. Creating such a model requires the creative potential of humanity, constant innovative research and a deep understanding of the needs of everyone involved in the value chain. There is currently a demand for durable, resource-efficient products that are easy to repair and reuse, as well as for the reuse of resources from products that cannot be repaired or have lost their consumer value. This has contributed to the emergence and spread of a new business philosophy that transforms the linear economic model into a circular one. In the circular economy, businesses focus on the entire chain of resource movement and transformation processes to ensure the reproduction and rational consumption of resources. Consumers act as one of the economy's resource donors by owning waste. The philosophy behind starting a business is important, not so much in terms of having the courage to take risks to achieve its founders' goals, but in terms of choosing the right economic foundation. In such circumstances, it is necessary to refuse to use or create demand for harmful or unnecessary materials or products. Rethinking enables businesses to make more efficient use of resources by reformatting existing or selected consumption and use models. A resource-saving approach enables businesses to focus on using resources efficiently, thereby reducing their material footprint. The philosophy o

latest.title: Embracing nature virtually: how virtual reality helps to promote pro-environmental consumption
BM Sürdürülebilir Üretim ve Tüketim Hedefi Bağlamında (SDG 12) FOMO ve JOMO’nun Genç Tüketicilerin Alışveriş Kararlarına Etkisi: Sakarya İli Öğrencileri Örneği
latest.abstract: Dijitalleşme, tüketim kararlarını yalnızca ekonomik değişkenler üzerinden açıklanabilen bir süreç olmaktan çıkararak sosyal ve psikolojik faktörlerin daha belirgin hâle geldiği bir yapıya dönüştürmektedir. Bu çalışmanın amacı, genç tüketicilerin tüketim niyeti ve sürdürülebilir tüketim niyeti üzerinde Planlı Davranış Teorisi (PDT) değişkenleri ile FOMO (Fear of Missing Out) ve JOMO (Joy of Missing Out) değişkenlerinin etkisini incelemektir. Araştırmada nicel araştırma yöntemi kullanılmış ve Sakarya ilindeki 525 üniversite öğrencisinden kolayda örnekleme yöntemiyle anket aracılığıyla veri toplanmıştır. Veriler IBM SPSS kullanılarak analiz edilmiş; faktör analizi, güvenirlik analizi, Pearson korelasyon analizi, çoklu regresyon ve farklılık analizlerinden yararlanılmıştır. Regresyon sonuçları, tüketim niyetinin başlıca öznel norm ve tutum tarafından açıklandığını, sürdürülebilir tüketim niyetinde ise algılanan davranışsal kontrolün öne çıktığını göstermektedir. Tüketim niyetinin en güçlü belirleyicisi öznel norm iken sürdürülebilir tüketim niyetinin en güçlü belirleyicisi algılanan davranışsal kontroldür. FOMO’nun tüketim niyeti, JOMO’nun ise sürdürülebilir tüketim niyeti üzerindeki etkisi pozitif olmakla birlikte görece sınırlıdır. Ayrıca FOMO düzeyinin cinsiyete ve influencer takip durumuna göre anlamlı biçimde farklılaştığı, JOMO düzeyinin ise incelenen demografik ve davranışsal değişkenlerin çoğuna göre anlamlı farklılık göstermediği belirlenmiştir. Bulgular, sürdürülebilir tüketim niyetinin açıklanmasında sosyal normların, algılanan davranışsal kontrolün ve psikolojik yönelimlerin birlikte değerlendirilmesinin önemine işaret etmektedir.

latest.title: Going Green, Buying Green: The Impact of Green Marketing on Gen Z’S Purchase Decisions of Sariayu Mask Products in Palembang
latest.venue: Equivalent Journal Of Economic Accounting and Management
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of green marketing on consumers’ purchase decisions regarding Sari Ayu facial mask products in Palembang. A quantitative research approach was employed. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to consumers who had previously used Sari Ayu facial mask products in Palembang. The respondents were selected using a purposive sampling technique, resulting in a total sample of 100 respondents. Data analysis was conducted using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, t-test, F-test, and the coefficient of determination (R²), with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics. The results indicate that, partially, green product and green price have positive and significant effects on purchase decisions, whereas green promotion does not have a significant effect on purchase decisions. Simultaneously, green product, green price, and green promotion have a significant effect on consumers’ purchase decisions regarding Sari Ayu facial mask products in Palembang. These findings suggest that the effective implementation of green marketing strategies can enhance consumers’ purchase decisions toward Sari Ayu facial mask products.

latest.title: Uncovering selective moral disengagement: driving and mediating tour guide performance at the Nuremberg rally sites
latest.abstract: Tour guides are essential in tourism. Their role is challenging, ever-changing and a central theme in tourism literature. Prior research has examined tour guide performance across a range of contexts; however, little is known about the relationship between morality and performance at dark sites. Drawing on the lens of moral disengagement and adopting an ethnographic approach, we present data from the Nuremberg rally site. We reveal that acts of moral disengagement are selective, justified and reflect “expectations.” The data show that selective moral disengagement is part of guide performance, underpins coping strategies, enhances relationships, supportss emotional regulation, and strengthens professional perception.

latest.title: Strengthening Inclusive Economic Development through Mango-Based Green Entrepreneurship: Cross-Border Mentoring of Women MSMEs in Indonesia and Malaysia
latest.venue: American Journal of Economic and Management Business (AJEMB)
latest.abstract: Women operating mango-based micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) face challenges related to limited product diversification, access to finance, market reach, and adoption of sustainable production practices, which constrain their potential contribution to inclusive economic development. This study evaluated an integrated green entrepreneurship mentoring program implemented through an academic partnership between Indonesia and Malaysia. Using a participatory action research (PAR) approach, the study involved 25 purposively selected women entrepreneurs in North Sumatra, Indonesia, from May to October 2026. Participants completed 90 hours of training covering green entrepreneurship, mango processing, digital marketing, sustainable packaging, and financial literacy. Program outcomes were assessed through pre- and post-training competency assessments, direct observation, focus group discussions, document reviews, and participatory capacity scoring. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and normalized gain (N-gain) calculations. Mean competency scores increased from 40.3 to 72.4, corresponding to a moderate normalized gain of 0.54. The average number of product varieties increased from 1.6 to 4.2, while mango byproduct utilization rose from 12% to 76%. The proportion of participants holding formal business bank accounts increased from 40% to 92%, and marketplace participation reached 88%. The proportion of participants using nonrecyclable plastic packaging decreased from 88% to 28%. These findings suggested that integrated mentoring could support improvements in product innovation, financial inclusion, digital market participation, and environmentally sustainable business practices. The program demonstrated potential as an approach to stre

latest.title: De la intención a la acción: conceptualización y medición de la conducta
latest.abstract: Introducción: Las actitudes y las intenciones son antecedentes centrales de la conducta, pero su traducción en acciones no es uniforme y puede verse afectada por la forma en que la conducta se conceptualiza y mide. Objetivo: Analizar cómo las revisiones publicadas entre 2020 y 2026 conceptualizan y miden la conducta en estudios sobre actitudes e intenciones, e identificar condiciones psicológicas, contextuales y metodológicas asociadas con su correspondencia. Metodología: Se realizó una revisión de revisiones con orientación crítica. Se analizaron 130 revisiones recuperadas en Scopus, siguiendo componentes pertinentes de PRISMA 2020. Se aplicaron criterios de inclusión y exclusión, codificación temática, análisis descriptivo mediante frecuencias y porcentajes, y evaluación metodológica con la lista JBI. Resultados: Se identificaron 49 revisiones con conducta sintetizada, 34 con evidencia conductual sin efecto único y 47 centradas solo en intención. En 68 de las 83 revisiones con evidencia conductual (81,9 %) no fue posible determinar uniformemente la modalidad de medición ni la relación temporal entre disposiciones y conducta. Conclusiones: La brecha intención-conducta no debe interpretarse únicamente como una discontinuidad psicológica; también puede reflejar condiciones contextuales y limitaciones metodológicas en la producción y síntesis de evidencia conductual.

latest.title: Consumer Drivers of Green Supply Chain Perceptions in Selangor, Malaysia: Implications for Sustainable Halal Ecosystems
latest.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
latest.abstract: The transition toward sustainable halal ecosystems requires businesses to consider environmental responsibility alongside halal integrity, ethical sourcing, transparency, and consumer confidence. Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) provides a practical approach for embedding environmental considerations into product design, procurement, manufacturing, packaging, logistics, and end-of-life management. However, consumer-related factors associated with perceptions of such practices have not been extensively examined in the Malaysian context. This study examines the relationships between environmental concern, environmental awareness, willingness to pay, trust in green claims, and consumers’ perceptions of GSCM practices, and discusses their implications for sustainable halal ecosystem development. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 184 consumers in Selangor, Malaysia, using purposive sampling and a structured questionnaire. Environmental awareness, trust in green claims, and environmental concern emerged as significant positive predictors of GSCM perceptions, while willingness to pay did not make a significant unique contribution when the other factors were considered. Environmental awareness was the strongest predictor, highlighting the importance of consumer knowledge in sustainability evaluation. The findings suggest that consumer perceptions are associated more strongly with awareness, credibility, and environmental concern than with financial willingness alone. The halal relevance is interpretive rather than a direct empirical test. Accordingly, the study offers exploratory implications for halal-oriented businesses by highlighting the value of credible green practices, transparent communication, consumer education, and trustworthy environmenta

latest.title: Entrepreneurial Trust and Corporate Green Innovation: Evidence From Chinese Entrepreneurs
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Why do entrepreneurs respond so differently to environmental innovation imperatives? Prior research emphasizes structural pressures, overlooking the cognitive and social frames shaping environmental decisions. Using survey data from 3163 Chinese micro and small firms, we find composite entrepreneurial trust is positively associated with green innovation. Disaggregating trust reveals a distinct institutional division of labor: Locally embedded in‐group trust accompanies green innovation—particularly local pollution abatement in lower‐pollution sectors—whereas institutional trust is linked to climate‐related innovation specifically among politically connected entrepreneurs. Generalized out‐group trust shows no association. Furthermore, trust aligns with green innovation alongside active behavioral commitments—risk‐taking, employee training, and proactive policy search—rather than passive expectations like future optimism or perceived policy effectiveness. This research advances the microfoundations of environmental strategy by illuminating how distinct trust objects shape responses to uncertainty. Practically, policymakers must lower policy‐information search costs, and entrepreneurs should pair relational trust with concrete capability investments.

latest.title: Formation of green purchase behavior among Indonesian Generation Z consumers: extending norm activation theory with green price sensitivity
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine why environmental awareness among Indonesian Generation Z consumers does not consistently translate into green purchase behavior (GPB) by testing the roles of awareness of consequences (AC), ascription of responsibility (AR), personal norms (PN) and green price sensitivity (GPS) within norm activation theory (NAT). Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 342 Indonesian Generation Z consumers were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling to test direct, mediating and moderated mediation effects. Findings PN significantly predicted GPB, whereas AC had no significant direct effect but showed a significant indirect effect through PN, indicating indirect-only mediation; AR had both significant direct and indirect effects through PN, indicating partial mediation; and GPS did not significantly moderate either indirect relationship. Practical implications Social marketing interventions should move beyond awareness raising by linking environmental consequences to consumers’ personal responsibility and strengthening PN. Interventions should also support accessible, affordable and credible green choices. Social implications Sustainable consumption initiatives should help young consumers recognize their role as marketplace actors and translate environmental concern into PN that guide everyday purchasing decisions. Originality/value This study refines NAT by using contrasting mediation patterns to locate the awareness–behavior gap within the norm-activation process. It distinguishes AC as a relatively distal form of environmental problem recognition from AR as a more proximal antecedent of GPB, while testing, but not supporting, GPS as a pathway-specific boundary condition.

latest.title: How does the digital economy empower new quality productive forces: evidence from China
latest.abstract: This study proposes a more comprehensive and reasonable measurement framework for new quality productive forces that incorporates two core dimensions, new quality input factors and new quality output efficiency, and further analyzes their temporal evolution and spatial distribution. On this basis, the study investigates both the direct impact of the digital economy on new quality productive forces and the mediating pathways through which this impact occurs. The research findings indicate that while China’s new quality productive forces have shown a steady upward trend over the years, issues of insufficient development and spatial imbalance persist. The digital economy plays a crucial role in promoting the growth of new quality productive forces, with notable heterogeneity across different geographic locations, levels of economic development, and policy environments. Furthermore, the mechanism analysis confirms that the digital economy can drive micro-enterprise innovation, promote meso- industry upgrading, and optimize macro-economy resource allocation. Overall, the findings provide both theoretical insights and empirical evidence for promoting new quality productive forces in alignment with regional characteristics and accelerating the modernization of the industrial system.

latest.title: Adapting marketing mix strategies to cultural dimensions: a comparative study of Iraq and selected MENA economies
latest.abstract: This research aims to evaluate the impact of cultural criteria, as described in G. Hofstede’s model, on the elements of the marketing mix (7Ps) in Iraq and their differences from similar parameters in countries within the MENA region. To achieve the research objectives, semi-structured interviews were conducted with experts in the field of marketing, as well as surveys of respondents working at companies in Iraq, the UAE, Egypt, Jordan, and Kuwait, who are involved in making marketing decisions within their organizations. Data processing was carried out using cluster analysis and analysis of variance (ANOVA). The interpretation of the obtained data led to the following conclusions: successful marketing strategies that have proven effective in the Iraqi market are often focused on collective values and the social significance of brands, and are implemented through traditional communication channels. Significant differences were also identified between Iraq and neighboring countries, particularly that most successful marketing solutions in the UAE and Kuwait are based on the transmission of individualistic values and are oriented toward the demonstration of high social status.

latest.title: Perceived CSR and Consumer Confidence at Personal and National Levels: The Moderating Role of Self-Efficacy
latest.abstract: Rebuilding social trust and promoting sustainable consumption have emerged as significant research topics. Thus, this study investigates the associations between perceived corporate social responsibility (CSR) and consumer confidence (CC) at both the personal and national levels. It also explores the moderating role of self-efficacy in the relationship between perceived CSR and consumer confidence. Drawing on survey data from 207 university students in Eastern China, the findings indicate that perceived CSR is positively associated with both personal consumer confidence (PCC) and national consumer confidence (NCC). In addition, self-efficacy positively moderates the relationships between perceived CSR and consumer confidence. That is, the positive associations between perceived CSR and consumer confidence are stronger among consumers with higher self-efficacy. These findings provide theoretical and practical implications for understanding the relationships among perceived CSR, consumer confidence, and market prosperity.

latest.title: Toward a Behavioral–Institutional Framework of Socially Responsible Investment Adoption: A Bibliometric Review and Research Agenda
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The growing prominence of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations has increased scholarly and market attention to socially responsible investment (SRI) as an approach that combines financial and sustainability considerations. This study examines the development, intellectual structure, and determinants of SRI adoption through an integrated bibliometric analysis, systematic literature review, and thematic analysis. This study analyses Scopus‐indexed publications from 2015 to 2026; it combines bibliometric mapping of 358 documents with a systematic synthesis of 72 eligible studies. The findings indicate substantial growth in SRI research, particularly in recent years, alongside increasing thematic attention to investor behavior, sustainability, ESG, and responsible investment. The systematic review identifies 13 recurring determinants associated with SRI adoption, organized through thematic analysis into five themes: psychological and Behavioral; social, moral and sustainability; knowledge and literacy; financial and risk; and institutional. Building on these themes, the study proposes a Behavioral–institutional framework in which the four individual‐level themes serve as antecedents of SRI intention and adoption, while government policy support acts as a contextual moderator of the intention–adoption relationship. The framework is presented as a conceptual synthesis, with its relationships offered as propositions for future empirical testing. The study offers directions for future research and suggests possible implications for policymakers, financial institutions, and investment practitioners.

latest.title: Research on the Interactive Relationship between Consumer Psychology and Behavior under the Trend of Commodity Sustainability
latest.venue: Frontiers in Business Economics and Management
latest.abstract: Against the backdrop of global green transformation and domestic dual carbon goals, Commodity Sustainability has become an important development direction for the consumer market. Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this paper aims to clarify the intrinsic relationship between consumer psychology and behavior by adopting literature analysis and empirical survey data analysis methods, combined with authoritative consumer research data, to explore the interaction mechanism and practical constraints between the two under the trend of Commodity Sustainability. Research has shown that consumers' Behavioral Attitude (BA), subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control can positively promote sustainable consumption, while behavioral practice can in turn reinforce their green consumption cognition; the current sustainable consumption still faces problems such as cognitive and behavioral disconnect, and external constraints. Based on this, this article proposes a targeted optimization path, which can provide a theoretical and empirical reference for the formulation of sustainable marketing for enterprises and the government to improve relevant supporting policies, and help promote the standardized development of the domestic sustainable consumption market.

latest.title: Omnichannel Integration and Seamless Experience in Generation Z Loyalty: Customer Engagement as a Mediator
latest.abstract: Objectives: This study examines the effects of Omnichannel Integration and Seamless Experience on Customer Loyalty among Generation Z consumers of Erigo, with Customer Engagement as a mediating variable.Methodology: This study employed a quantitative explanatory research design using a cross-sectional survey of 250 respondents aged 17–29 who had purchased Erigo products through multiple channels. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0.Finding: The results show that Omnichannel Integration has a positive and significant effect on Customer Engagement (β = 0.335; p < 0.001) and Customer Loyalty (β = 0.159; p = 0.006). Similarly, Seamless Experience positively and significantly affects Customer Engagement (β = 0.317; p < 0.001) and Customer Loyalty (β = 0.197; p < 0.001). Furthermore, Customer Engagement has a positive and significant effect on Customer Loyalty (β = 0.400; p < 0.001). The results also demonstrate that Customer Engagement plays a mediating role in the relationship between Omnichannel Integration, Seamless Experience, and Customer Loyalty.Conclusion: This study concludes that Omnichannel Integration and Seamless Experience contribute to enhancing Customer Loyalty, both directly and indirectly through Customer Engagement. Customer Engagement serves as an important mediating mechanism that transforms integrated and seamless omnichannel experiences into stronger customer loyalty. These findings support the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) framework in the context of Generation Z consumers of Erigo.

latest.title: Digitalisation, Eco‐Innovation and SME Internationalisation: A Dynamic Capabilities Perspective
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT This study integrates the digitalisation and dynamic capabilities literature to examine the relationship between digitalisation, eco‐innovation and internationalisation in small and medium‐sized enterprises (SME). Using data obtained from 300 SME owner‐managers operating in the United Kingdom, the findings suggest that digitalisation positively impacts eco‐innovation and consequently the nature of internationalisation activities. In addition, there is a moderating effect of internationalisation experience on the relationship between eco‐innovation and internationalisation. These findings highlight the pivotal role of eco‐innovation, digitalisation and international experience in enabling SMEs to thrive in international markets. Furthermore, the study offers empirical evidence of how SMEs dynamically develop digital resources, and internationalisation is an outcome of building such capabilities. The implications for practice and future research avenues are examined.

latest.title: Pengaruh Green Brand Image dan Perceived Taste Quality dalam Membentuk Repurchase Intention Konsumen Fore Coffee
authors: I Dewa Ayu Shanti Kumala Prabaswari
Ni Putu Eka Ayu Chandra Wijaya
Ni Komang Trisa Bali Meyin Dandra Tirta
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dampak citra merek ramah lingkungan (Green Brand Image) dan kualitas rasa produk (Perceived Taste Quality) terhadap loyalitas pelanggan Fore Coffee di Kota Denpasar. Penelitian ini bersifat kuantitatif, yang meneliti hubungan sebab-akibat antarvariabel melalui pengujian hipotesis. Dari populasi konsumen Fore Coffee di Kota Denpasar, sebanyak 112 individu dipilih sebagai responden dengan menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Responden yang terpilih merupakan individu berusia 17 tahun yang saat ini pernah mengonsumsi produk minuman di Fore Coffee lebih dari satu kali. Instrumen penelitian dievaluasi menggunakan uji validitas, uji reliabilitas, dan uji asumsi klasik, sementara data dilakukan menggunakan regresi linear berganda, dengan hipotesis yang diuji menggunakan uji F dan uji t. Seluruh analisis statistik dilakukan menggunakan perangkat lunak SPSS. Hasil temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa kualitas rasa menjadi salah satu pertimbangan penting bagi konsumen dalam menentukan minat untuk kembali membeli produk Fore Coffee. Oleh karena itu, perusahaan perlu menjaga konsistensi rasa dan terus mengembangkan kualitas produk sekaligus mempertahankan komitmen terhadap praktik ramah lingkungan guna meningkatkan minat beli ulang konsumen

latest.title: Dari Kualitas ke Keputusan: Peran Green Brand Trust dan Green Skepticism pada Pembelian Produk Daur Ulang 100% (Cleo Eco Green)
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini menganalisis pengaruh Perceived quality terhadap keputusan pembelian Cleo Eco Green , AMDK berbahan 100% PET daur ulang (rPET), dengan Green brand trust sebagai mediator dan Green skepticism sebagai moderator berdasarkan Signaling Theory . Survei dare dilakukan pada 100 konsumen di Indonesia berusia minimal 17 tahun yang mengetahui atau pernah membeli Cleo Eco Green , dipilih dengan purposive sampling , dan data dianalisis dengan PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4, bootstrapping 5.000 subsampel). Perceived quality tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Green brand trust (β = −0,135; p = 0,256) maupun keputusan pembelian (β = 0,114; p = 0,189). Green brand trust berpengaruh positif tetapi tidak signifikan pada taraf 5% (β = 0,248; p = 0,072). Mediasi dan moderasi tidak terbukti (interaksi β = −0,086; p = 0,162). Skeptisisme hijau memiliki hubungan terkuat dengan keputusan pembelian (β = 0,557; p < 0,001; f² = 0,540). Model menjelaskan 45,1% varian keputusan pembelian , tetapi hanya 1,8% varian kepercayaan merek ramah lingkungan . Klaim kualitas saja kurang cukup mendorong pembelian; manajer disarankan memperkuatnya dengan bukti yang dapat memenuhi, seperti sertifikasi food grade dan ketertelusuran.

latest.title: Omnichannel Marketing Strategies in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Customer Experience Personalisation and Sales Automation
latest.abstract: Purpose: The research objective is to develop an artificial intelligence-driven omnichannel marketing planning model to personalise customer interactions and optimise a company’s sales. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study combines systemic, process and economic-mathematical approaches. Customer journeys are mapped through deterministic identity mapping of events using stable identifiers (customer ID, loyalty ID, hashed e-mail, order ID). Eight contact points were selected. The Omnichannel Data Integration Index (ODII) includes six integration components and two error components. Component weights were obtained by the CRITIC method. Comparison of three planning modes on the same budget of USD 100,000: the baseline channel plan (S₀), independent channel optimisation by KPIs (S₁), and joint journey-based optimisation (S₂). Calculations used a control testing array covering a 12-month period, 8 channels, 3 segments and 3 offers. Research Limitation: The applicability of the results is limited by the accuracy of the input forecasts and the quality of customer data. Findings: The transition from autonomous channel estimation to analysis of identified customer routes distinguished between actual losses and cross-channel migration. Unlike the baseline S₀ mode, the artificial intelligence-driven S₂ mode increased the number of conversions by 13.9%, the marginal result by 11.0%, return on advertising spend by 11.9%, and the target function by 15.5%. Compared with the autonomous channel optimisation S1, the target function increased by 7.1%. Practical Implication. Marketing managers can use it to select contacts, personalise interactions, and allocate budgets.
