hot.title: Secondhand fashion consumers exhibit fast fashion behaviors despite sustainability narratives
hot.abstract: The fashion industry contributes 2-8% of global greenhouse gas emissions, driven by rising clothing consumption and the proliferation of fast fashion. Fast fashion accelerates environmental harm through rapid production cycles, low costs, and short garment lifespans. Secondhand clothing markets are often promoted as a sustainable alternative, promising extended use and reduced waste. These markets have grown rapidly, with global sales reaching $177 billion in 2022 and projected to double by 2027. Despite this growth, few studies have empirically examined whether secondhand purchasing displaces or merely supplements primary market consumption. This study addresses that gap using a nationally representative survey of 1,009 U.S. consumers. We find that secondhand consumption is positively correlated with new clothing purchases (r = 0.58, p < 0.01), particularly among younger consumers and frequent shoppers. Cluster and principal component analyses reveal that highly engaged secondhand consumers also exhibit high overall consumption and short garment retention. Although many report high sustainability knowledge, such knowledge does not reliably predict sustainable behavior. Drawing on rebound and moral licensing theories, we suggest that secondhand purchases may psychologically or economically justify continued overconsumption. These findings challenge assumptions about resale's environmental benefits and support policy interventions to realign resale practices with sustainability goals.

hot.title: Investigating the factors influencing customer loyalty and the mediating effect of customer satisfaction in online food delivery services: empirical evidence from an emerging market
hot.abstract: This study investigates the factors affecting customer loyalty and the mediating role of customer satisfaction in online food delivery services (OFDS) in Bangladesh. An analysis of 300 responses via structural equation modeling (SEM) revealed that perceived food and service quality alone did not significantly impact customer loyalty. While these qualities are essential, they must enhance customer satisfaction in order to boost loyalty. Significant relationships exist among perceived price, ease of payment, time efficiency, and customer loyalty, with customer satisfaction acting as a crucial mediator. Strategies focusing on pricing, payment convenience, and timely delivery are the most effective for building loyalty. The interplay between perceived quality, pricing, payment, and delivery efficiency enhances the overall customer experience. This study contributes to the literature by applying Attribution Theory and the Technological Acceptance Model (TAM), emphasizing external factors such as pricing, delivery, and payment ease as key loyalty drivers. The findings suggest that OFDS businesses should prioritize reasonable pricing, efficient payment systems, and timely delivery to foster loyalty. Combined with high-quality food and services, these strategies can enhance customer satisfaction, promote business growth, and increase revenue.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing: Enhancing Consumer Engagement and Supporting Sustainable Behavior Through Social and Mobile Networks
hot.abstract: This article explores the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital marketing through social and mobile networks and its role in fostering sustainable consumer behavior. AI enhances personalization, sentiment analysis, and campaign automation, reshaping marketing dynamics and enabling brands to engage interactively with users. A quantitative study conducted on 501 social media users evaluates how perceived benefits, risks, trust, transparency, satisfaction, and social norms influence the acceptance of AI-driven marketing tools. Using structural equation modeling (SEM), the findings show that social norms and perceived transparency significantly enhance trust in AI, while perceived benefits and satisfaction drive user acceptance; conversely, perceived risks and negative emotions undermine trust. From a sustainability perspective, AI supports the efficient targeting and personalization of eco-conscious content, aligning marketing with environmentally responsible practices. This study contributes to ethical AI and sustainable digital strategies by offering empirical evidence and practical insights for responsible AI integration in marketing.

hot.title: Willingness to pay a premium for eco-label products in China: a mediation model based on quality value
hot.abstract: Sustainable consumption plays an important role in achieving sustainable development. Eco-labels can help to convey this message to consumers. In China, the new carbon label represents a new kind of sustainable eco-label; as such, the relationship between carbon labeling and consumers' willingness to pay (WTP) a premium is worth studying. This paper explores the impact of carbon label recognition on WTP a premium, which is also affected by the perceived value of quality attributes and effective advertising campaigns. The results show that the former plays an intermediary role in carbon label recognition and premium payment intention, while the latter regulates the relationship between perceived value of quality attributes and premium payment intention. The research shows that when consumers are aware of carbon labeling, they are more willing to pay higher prices for products as they believe the quality of these products to be higher. For others, effective advertising campaigns can encourage paying a premium. This not only provides suggestions for enterprises promoting green products and for governments wishing to raise environmental awareness via guidance and education but also promotes the sustainable development of green products.

hot.title: The Digital-Sustainability Ecosystem: A conceptual framework for digital transformation and sustainable innovation
hot.venue: Journal of Entrepreneurship Management and Innovation
hot.abstract: PURPOSE: This study introduces the Digital-Sustainability Ecosystem, a conceptual framework to integrate digital transformation and sustainable innovation. It examines how emerging digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, blockchain, and the Internet of Things, drive sustainability transitions by serving as strategic enablers. Addressing a critical gap in the literature, this research focuses on the dynamic mechanisms and synergies that connect digital transformation with sustainable innovation within a complex ecosystem. METHODOLOGY: The study employs a systematic literature review (SLR) of 50 studies and a comparative analysis of 13 existing frameworks to identify and analyze key mechanisms that link digital transformation and sustainable innovation, culminating in the development of the Digital-Sustainability Ecosystem framework. FINDINGS: The study identifies five interconnected mechanisms: efficiency gains, dematerialization, circular economy enablement, innovation acceleration, and digital collaboration. These mechanisms illustrate the relationships between technological advancements and sustainability objectives while addressing synergies and tensions, such as the trade-offs between energy demands and environmental benefits. The Digital-Sustainability Ecosystem emphasizes multi-stakeholder collaboration, iterative feedback loops, and adaptable processes to address gaps in existing models, positioning digital transformation as a transformative force for systemic sustainability improvements. IMPLICATIONS: The Digital-Sustainability Ecosystem advances theoretical discourse by positioning sustainability as a systemic outcome of digital transformation, extending beyond traditional efficiency-focused models. It emphasizes organizational resilience and s

hot.title: Role of Greenwashing in Influencing Brand Attitude and Consumption: Identifying Sustainable Business Strategies
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT With firms' increasing adoption of green marketing strategies, greenwashing is also becoming more prevalent. Despite the negative consequences of greenwashing, limited studies have investigated its impact on attitude and consumption. Earlier studies have used greenwashing as a one‐dimensional construct and do not distinguish between different greenwashing practices. Based on the integrated framework of the Attribution Theory and the elaboration likelihood model, this study examines the effects of situational involvement with greenwashing practices on perceived greenwashing, green skepticism, and ultimately, brand attitude and purchase intention. Additionally, it investigates the moderating effect of environmental knowledge. Using a cross‐sectional research design, the study uses structural equation modeling to analyze the data collected from 353 US consumers. Findings suggest that greenwashing practices influence attitude and purchase intentions. The mediating role of green skepticism was also established. Additionally, the study highlights environmental knowledge's moderating role in the relationships studied. The results have implications for sustainable business practices and improving positive brand attitudes and green consumption by understanding customer perception of greenwashing.

hot.title: The impact of green HRM practices on green innovative work behaviour: empirical evidence from the hospitality sector of China and Pakistan
hot.abstract: Amid a global shift towards eco-friendly practices, this study investigates the impact of green human resource management (GHRM) practices on green innovative work behavior (GIWB) in the hospitality sector, focusing on emerging and developing countries, specifically China and Pakistan. The research also explores the mediating roles of green perceived organizational support (GPOS) and organizational citizenship behavior towards the environment (OCBE), as well as the moderating role of green transformational leadership (GTL). This study is grounded in the AMO (ability, motivation, and opportunity) theory and organizational support theory. Data were collected through a questionnaire, yielding 503 valid responses from hotel employees in Beijing, China, and 498 valid responses from Islamabad, Pakistan. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was employed to examine and compare the results across both samples. The findings reveal positive and significant relationships between GHRM and GIWB, as well as notable mediation and moderation effects among the specified variables. Interestingly, GTL did not significantly moderate the relationship between GHRM and GIWB in Pakistan's sample, highlighting a regional contrast. This study contributes to advancing the implementation of GHRM practices to enhance GIWB in the hospitality sector, with insights into the role of GTL across different cultural contexts.

hot.title: The Role of Organizational Culture in Digital Transformation and Modern Accounting Practices Among Jordanian SMEs
hot.venue: Journal of risk and financial management
hot.abstract: This study investigates the impact of digital transformation on modern accounting practices among Jordanian SMEs, focusing on the moderating role of organizational culture. Digital transformation using AI, blockchain, and cloud computing improves operational efficiency, real-time financial reporting, and decision making. However, the integration of these technologies poses challenges such as skill gaps, cost constraints, and cultural resistance. A quantitative survey of 480 employees in managerial roles from Jordanian SMEs shows that organizational culture plays a dual role as a driver and moderator of digital transformation. The findings confirm the role of digital transformation in reshaping modern accounting practices. Also, this study shows that to get the most out of digital transformation in accounting, a culture of innovation and continuous learning is required.

hot.title: Leveraging social media for sustainable fashion: how brand and user-generated content influence Gen Z’s purchase intentions
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study examines how brand-generated content (BGC) and user-generated content (UGC) on TikTok and Instagram shape Gen Z consumers’ purchase intentions for sustainable fashion. It also investigates the mediating role of social media engagement (SME) in these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative approach was employed, using stratified random sampling to target Gen Z consumers aged 16–28. Data were collected from 643 respondents through structured surveys and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS. Findings Both BGC and UGC positively influence purchase intentions, with BGC demonstrating a stronger effect due to its professional quality and emotional appeal. SME partially mediates these relationships, amplifying the impact of both content types on purchase behavior. Originality This research advances the sustainable fashion marketing literature by integrating insights from social media influence and consumer behavior, specifically within the Gen Z demographic. Unlike previous studies that focus solely on BGC or UGC in isolation, this study examines their interplay and the crucial mediating role of SME. The findings offer practical guidance for brands on how to strategically balance BGC and UGC to optimize consumer engagement and drive sustainable purchasing decisions.

hot.title: Gamification for sustainable consumption: A state‐of‐the‐art overview and future agenda
hot.abstract: Abstract Unsustainable consumption is a pressing issue requiring innovative solutions. Gamification is a promising approach with the potential to drive a shift toward sustainable consumption. This study delivers a state‐of‐the‐art overview of gamification as a strategy for sustainable consumption, shedding light on its role at the intersection of environmental sustainability , sustainability education , sustainable behavioral changes , sustainable living , sustainable tourism , and workplace sustainability , underscoring that sustainable consumption (e.g., energy) is not only personal but also professional. This study also offers a rich organizer of antecedents (game mechanics, incentives and mechanisms, social dynamics, sustainability focus, and user experience), mediators and moderators (psychographic and socio‐cultural), controls (demographic and contextual), and outcomes (behavioral changes, consumption patterns, and psychographic shifts), alongside relevant theories and methods , to provide a finer‐grained, toolbox‐like understanding of gamification for sustainable consumption. This study concludes with avenues for future research to drive new frontiers where gamification can contribute to sustainable consumption, and by extension, the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 12 on Responsible Consumption and Production.

hot.title: Forty years of the theory of planned behavior: a bibliometric analysis (1985–2024)
hot.abstract: Abstract The goal of the study is a comprehensive and systematic analysis of the literature and research landscape of the TPB between 1985–2024. This paper presents a comprehensive bibliometric study of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) literature over the past forty years (1985–2024), analyzing 14,461 articles and 542,479 citations published in the Web of Science Core Collection. Utilizing performance analysis and science mapping techniques, the study leverages bibliographic coupling, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence analysis, and a temporal assessment of the field across six distinct periods (1985–1999; 2000–2004, 2005–2009; 2010–2014; 2015–2019; and 2020–2024). Employing VOS Viewer software for visualization, this research maps the evolution, intellectual structure, and networks of relationships in the TPB field for the first time. The results highlight significant patterns and interdisciplinary connections, identifying the most influential publications, authors, journals, and institutions. A distinguishing feature of the study is the identification of thematic clusters based on multiple criteria and a triangulation analysis of these clusters. Additionally, the study investigates the most influential articles within the six periods and provides an evolutionary phase-wise analysis of TPB. Another highlight is the detailed guidance on future research avenues, which are actionable and based on a rigorous assessment of the most cited articles from 2020 to 2024. The study makes a significant contribution to the ongoing research conversations on the trajectory and growth of TPB across various disciplines.

hot.title: Integrating Industry 4.0, Circular Economy, and Green HRM: A Framework for Sustainable Transformation
hot.abstract: The integration of Industry 4.0 technologies, Circular Economy (CE) principles, and Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) offers transformative potential to address global sustainability challenges. Industry 4.0, characterized by advanced digital technologies like IoT, Additive Manufacturing (AM), and Big Data Analytics (BDAA), enhances operational efficiency, resource optimization, and waste minimization. Concurrently, CE redefines economic models through resource conservation, lifecycle extension, and reduced environmental impact, supported by frameworks like ReSOLVE. GHRM aligns human resource practices with sustainability objectives, fostering Green behaviors and embedding environmental considerations into organizational culture. Despite the individual benefits of these frameworks, their combined application remains underexplored, with limited research on their systemic integration. This study addresses this gap by examining the synergies between Industry 4.0 technologies, CE principles, and GHRM strategies, identifying opportunities and challenges in their implementation. A theoretical model is proposed, emphasizing systemic innovation, resource efficiency, and collaborative value chains as key enablers of sustainable development. The model highlights the necessity of aligning technological advancements with human-centric approaches to overcome behavioral, organizational, and infrastructural barriers in transitioning toward sustainability. The findings offer practical insights for policymakers and industry leaders, outlining strategies for integrating Industry 4.0 with CE and GHRM to drive sustainability transitions. By synthesizing technological, environmental, and human resource dimensions, this research contributes both theoretically and practically, positionin

hot.title: Closing the loop at the local scale: Investigating the drivers of and barriers to the implementation of the circular economy in cities and regions
hot.abstract: Transitioning to a circular economy (CE) at the local level is important for addressing the strain on natural resources caused by population growth and climate change. This study aims to investigate the factors that influence or impede the adoption of CE practices in French cities and regions. To achieve this goal, 47 interviews were conducted with practitioners from local authorities to identify the key elements that facilitate or hinder the implementation of CE. The findings highlight the crucial role of local authorities in enabling the transition to a CE, with critical support from political endorsement, strategic foresight, and effective leadership. However, obstacles such as organizational inertia, financial constraints, and a limited understanding of a CE present challenges to a CE's broader adoption. The study also emphasizes the critical role of partnerships and collaborative networks in overcoming these barriers and promoting the advancement of CE initiatives.

hot.title: Product reuse and repurpose in circular manufacturing: a critical review of key challenges, shortcomings and future directions
hot.abstract: Abstract This paper explores the transformative potential of reuse and repurposing strategies in the manufacturing industry, with a focus on sustainability and circular economy principles. Through an extensive review of 115 articles from Scopus using 6 different queries for broad topic coverage, the study provides a comprehensive analysis of reuse and repurposing frameworks, highlighting their benefits and challenges. The research identifies three essential pillars for successful implementation: product design, operational processes, and consumer acceptance. The study emphasizes the significance of modular designs, lifecycle extensions, and advanced cost models to maximize resource efficiency and sustainability. The paper also discusses the integration of advanced technologies, such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and IoT-enabled systems, to enhance traceability, streamline reverse logistics, and optimize predictive maintenance. Automated disassembly and collaborative robotics are highlighted as critical enablers for efficient and scalable reuse operations. Furthermore, the study advocates for flexible supply chains and real-time data analytics to address uncertainties in core acquisition and product variability. Despite the progress, the lack of standardized frameworks and metrics remains a significant barrier to widespread adoption. The paper concludes by proposing a cohesive framework that incorporates technological advancements, regulatory support, and collaborative approaches to overcome these limitations. This study provides actionable insights to foster a scalable, transparent, and sustainable manufacturing ecosystem.

hot.title: Digital marketing strategies in expanding the market for MSME creative products in Indonesia—state of art
hot.abstract: Digital marketing strategy is the planning and actions taken by companies or individuals to utilize digital technology to market products or services effectively and efficiently to target markets. In this strategy, companies use various digital channels such as social media, search engines, email marketing, websites, or e-commerce to achieve marketing objectives, including increasing brand awareness, attracting new customers, and boosting sales and customer loyalty. However, challenges in using digital marketing still exist due to the digital literacy gap among creative product practitioners. This study reviews digital marketing for creative products, including social media marketing, search engine marketing, influencer marketing, email marketing, and content marketing. Using Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) method, 22 articles from leading sources such as MDPI, Wiley, ScienceDirect, and IEEE Xplore were analyzed. The objectives of this study are to determine (1) what the definitions of digital marketing strategies and the creative product market are. (2) Which countries have implemented digital marketing in the creative market for SMEs? (3) Who is involved, and how familiar are SMEs with the creative product market? (4) What strategies are used in digital marketing in Indonesia? How is it implemented, what are the challenges, and what is the level of success? (R5): What are the future research and recommendations for digital marketing in expanding the creative market? Future research directions include the application of AI and technology for automated content creation for creative product practitioners, strengthened digital education and literacy, and community-based campaigns that foster collaboration among local creators to build a mutually supportive e

hot.title: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Factors for Sustainable Tourism Development: The Way Forward Toward Destination Resilience and Growth
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT Although environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance is increasingly gaining popularity in corporate and financial domains, its application in the tourism industry is still relatively underexplored. Hence, the objectives of this research are fivefold: (1) A systematic review appraises the extant literature on the intersection of the ESG dimensions and sustainable tourism; (2) It provides a synthesis of the content of the extracted articles and maps thematic intersections related to travel destinations' environmental stewardship, social equity and governance frameworks; (3) It assesses ESG‐aligned strategies that are intended to address the destinations' challenges including their carrying capacities and overtourism issues, climate risks, sociocultural tensions as well as institutional accountabilities; (4) It provides a holistic conceptual framework that guides policymakers, practitioners and stakeholders in integrating ESG into tourism planning and development, for sustainable and economically viable outcomes. In conclusion, (5) it advances theoretical and managerial implications.

hot.title: Green human resources management and green innovation: a meta-analytic review of strategic human resources levers for environmental sustainability
hot.abstract: Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) has become a vital lever for driving organizational sustainability, yet the empirical relationship between GHRM and Green Innovation (GI) remains fragmented and inconclusive. This meta-analysis integrates findings from 52 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025, encompassing 23,103 observations, to estimate the overall effect of GHRM on GI and to examine the influence of specific HR practices and contextual moderators. Grounded in the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) framework, the Resource-Based View (RBV), and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), the study reveals a significant positive pooled effect, affirming that GHRM is a consistent and influential driver of GI. Among HR practices, green-linked compensation demonstrated the strongest impact, surpassing training and recruitment. Moderator analyses reveal that effect sizes differ meaningfully by industry type, firm size, and year of publication, but not by country development status or statistical method. These results contribute to theoretical advancement by integrating behavioral, strategic, and cognitive perspectives on sustainability-oriented innovation. Practically, the findings offer actionable insights for managers and policymakers on designing effective GHRM systems that stimulate eco-innovation. This study delivers the first quantitative synthesis clarifying when, where, and how GHRM enhances green innovation across diverse sectors and economies, providing a robust foundation for future research and strategy in sustainability-driven human capital development.

hot.title: The implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation for sustainability
hot.abstract: The interconnected phenomena of digital transformation and environmental innovation exert a major impact on sustainability . This research attempts to shed light on the sustainability implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation. Both digital transformation and environmental innovation offer multiple opportunities to address global challenges such as climate change , resource depletion , and social inequality. This study highlights the need to integrate digital technologies and innovation with environmental initiatives. By following this approach, the sustainability implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation can lead to a more resilient and sustainable society. Fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) is used to determine the necessary or sufficient factors to increase sustainability. The study thus provides insights into what the environmental priorities should be. The results show how to reduce environmental impacts , improve quality of life , and support economic development. They can also be used to inform policies that support sustainability initiatives by encouraging the combinations of interventions that work best. By harnessing the potential of digital transformation and environmental innovation, it is possible to build a greener and more prosperous future for generations to come.

latest.title: Beyond Shared Values: Rethinking Organizational Culture and Employee Commitment through a Communication Lens
latest.venue: Journal of Ethnic and Diversity Studies
latest.abstract: Organisational culture is associated with employee commitment, yet the communicative processes shaping how employees interpret cultural meanings remain insufficiently differentiated.This article develops a communication-centred framework informed by a critical descriptive reappraisal of an earlier survey in Omani governmental institutions.A purposive synthesis of culture, organizational commitment and communicative constitution scholarship is combined with a document-level audit of survey counts, descriptive statistics and regression reporting.The archival source documented 130 questionnaires distributed, 99 returned and 89 usable responses.Reported cultural dimension means ranged from 3.81 to 3.97, while the general commitment mean was 3.632.However, inconsistencies between the documented sample and reported regression degrees of freedom prevent independent verification of inferential findings.The framework proposes four communicative processes-belief articulation, attitudinal expression, value enactment and norm negotiation-and positions communicative consistency as a potential moderator of the culture-affective commitment relationship.Norm negotiation is conditionally associated with normative commitment.Since the original questionnaire measured neither communication processes nor differentiated commitment components, these propositions remain untested.The contribution is a process-oriented theoretical integration that explicitly distinguishes source-reported observations from relationships requiring future empirical validation.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Unlocking the nexus from innovativeness perceptions to customer loyalty: the roles of omnichannel trust and emotional brand attachment
latest.abstract: Recently, the bonding between consumers and service providers is getting more complex as the current trend shows the importance of innovation for long-run viability. Innovativeness also plays an imperative role in ensuring sustainability for hospitality businesses. Hence, the purpose of this study is to investigate the effects of a holistic concept of innovativeness on trust in omnichannel and behavioral loyalty while the mediating influences of trust in omnichannel of a restaurant and emotional brand attachment on the domain linkages were further explored. This study tested using a structured questionnaire from a sample of chain restaurant customers in Klang Valley area of Malaysia. The results indicate that menu innovativeness, technology-based service innovativeness and experiential innovativeness influence trust in omnichannel. Besides, only dimension of technology-based service innovativeness influences repeat purchase intention while experiential innovativeness influences positive electronic words of mouth (eWOM). Further findings also demonstrated that trust in omnichannel and emotional brand attachment play several important mediating roles in predicting behavioral loyalty. Through application of Stimulus-Organism-Response theory, this study assesses the impacts of innovativeness holistically that employed by restaurateurs, on trust in omnichannel of the restaurant which this perspective has never been explored previously. Apart from making theoretical contributions, this study provides additional insights on practical implications for restaurateurs to invest on salient resources accurately and to innovate their offers more effectively.

latest.title: Gender stereotypes and portrayals in advertising: implications for emotional brand attachment and brand sacredness among young consumers and young adults
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals in advertising shape early-stage emotional brand attachment and brand sacredness among young consumers and young adults. It positions gendered advertising as both a branding issue and a responsible-marketing concern in youth-oriented marketplaces. Design/methodology/approach A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment was conducted with 159 valid responses from a Vietnamese sample concentrated mainly in the younger age segment; 83.6% of respondents were aged 14–26. Skincare and automobile advertising stimuli were used to manipulate stereotype congruity and the gender of the focal protagonist. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed relationships. Findings Both gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals significantly influence emotional brand attachment across the experimental conditions. Emotional brand attachment, in turn, positively predicts brand sacredness and its three dimensions: communitas, supremacy and mesmerization. The findings are interpreted as immediate relational and symbolic responses within a youth- and young-adult-oriented sample, not as evidence of fully matured brand attachment or sacredness. Originality/value This study contributes to young-consumer and gender-in-advertising research by extending attention from proximal persuasion outcomes to early relational and symbolic brand outcomes. It clarifies the conceptual distinction between gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals and explains how these cues may shape early-stage attachment and sacredness-related perceptions among young consumers and young adults. The findings also offer responsible-marketing implications: although gendered portrayals may strengthen consumer–brand

latest.title: Ảnh hưởng của truyền thông mạng xã hội đến nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến du lịch của thế hệ Gen Z tại Việt Nam
latest.abstract: Nghiên cứu phân tích ảnh hưởng của truyền thông mạng xã hội đến nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến du lịch của thế hệ Gen Z tại Việt Nam. Nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp định lượng, dữ liệu được thu thập bằng khảo sát trực tuyến thông qua Google Forms đối với những người thuộc thế hệ Gen Z có sử dụng mạng xã hội để tìm kiếm, xem hoặc tương tác với nội dung về điểm đến du lịch. Sau quá trình sàng lọc và làm sạch dữ liệu, 214 phiếu hợp lệ được sử dụng để phân tích bằng phần mềm SPSS 27.0 thông qua các kỹ thuật kiểm định độ tin cậy Cronbach's alpha, phân tích nhân tố khám phá và hồi quy tuyến tính bội. Kết quả cho thấy chất lượng thông tin, nội dung do người dùng tạo ra và mức độ tương tác đều ảnh hưởng tích cực đến nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến du lịch; trong đó nội dung do người dùng tạo ra có tác động mạnh nhất. Nghiên cứu bổ sung bằng chứng thực nghiệm về vai trò của truyền thông mạng xã hội trong xây dựng thương hiệu điểm đến và đề xuất hàm ý định vị điểm đến Việt Nam theo hướng trực quan, tương tác, đáng tin cậy và phù hợp với Gen Z.

latest.title: The relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust: brand credibility, emotional attachment, and perceived quality effects
latest.abstract: Introduction The purpose of this research was to explore the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Specifically, we developed a conceptual model which proposes that brand credibility has a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust, and that perceived quality and emotional attachment have mediating effects on brand trust. Methods We tested the conceptual model by conducting a 2 × 2 (low versus high brand ethicality and low versus high brand credibility) between-subjects experiment, with brand trust as the dependent variable. Data ( N = 208) were collected at a large university in Bangladesh, and were analysed using PLS-SEM. Results Results of the experiment suggest that brand ethicality has a direct effect on brand trust. Brand ethicality also enhances emotional attachment and perceived quality, which, in turn, lead to increased brand trust. Brand credibility, however, does not have a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Discussion Drawing on signalling theory, the findings provide causal evidence that brand ethicality builds brand trust through two parallel pathways: an affective pathway via emotional attachment and a cognitive pathway via perceived quality. Contrary to expectations, brand credibility did not act as a boundary condition, suggesting that brand ethicality and brand credibility may be better understood as sequential antecedents of brand trust rather than as interacting constructs. For practice, marketers ought to increase brand ethicality to increase brand trust, both directly and via emotional attachment and perceived quality.

latest.title: Co-designing with Generative AI: consumer participation behaviour and product authenticity
latest.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping consumer–brand interactions, with fashion brands increasingly adopting Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) co-design tools that enable direct consumer participation in product design. This research examines how consumers evaluate the authenticity of the GenAI co-designed products, and how evaluation influences consumers’ future participation with fashion brands. This study further investigates whether consumer self-efficacy and perceived expertise toward the tools serve as key antecedents of the authenticity perceptions. By focusing on an emerging AI-enabled service (GenAI) context, this study expands consumer participation and value co-creation research by offering new insight into the drivers and consequences of the perceived authenticity of the fashion products co-created by GenAI and consumers.

latest.title: A consumer neuroscience approach to examining how augmented reality and QR codes support product and brand sustainability communication in retail settings
latest.abstract: This research explores the use of Augmented Reality (AR) and Quick Response (QR) codes as tools for communicating sustainability-related information in a quasi-realistic retail setting. It combines neurophysiological and self-report measures to investigate how these technologies influence consumers’ sustainability perceptions, emotional engagement, and cognitive workload. Participants took part in a simulated shopping experience, where they were exposed to one of three experimental conditions: traditional packaging, smartphone-mediated QR code scanning, and smartphone-mediated Augmented Reality exploration of coffee packaging. Cognitive workload (measured via electroencephalography) and emotional engagement (measured via skin conductance and heart rate) were recorded alongside self-report measures of green company orientation (GCO), green product informativeness (GPI), and brand familiarity. Findings indicate that while both AR and QR codes evoke more positive emotions and lead to higher perceptions of GCO and GPI, AR usage is also associated with higher cognitive workload. Additionally, brand familiarity enhanced self-report scores but not neurophysiological ones, without interacting with the interaction modality. This research provides a multi-level (implicit neurophysiological and explicit self-reported) perspective on the impact of digital packaging formats on sustainability communication. The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on how interactive technologies can support effective communication, implicit emotions, and consumer engagement with sustainability in retail environments.

latest.title: Canine Companions in the Digital Age: Exploring Pet-Centric Social Media through the Lens of the Extended Self Theory
latest.abstract: This study investigates how Dutch dog owners use non-commercial Instagram profiles for their dogs and how managing these profiles relates to identity construction and self-perception. Guided by Belk’s Extended Self Theory, the study employed a cross-sectional qualitative design and semi-structured interviews with 10 Dutch women who actively managed Instagram accounts for their dogs without seeking monetization. Narrative analysis focused on structure, style, identity, context, and theme, followed by thematic analysis. Five themes emerged: memory preservation; the human-pet bond; social interaction and community; expression and identity; and consumer behavior and pet products. Participants described Instagram as a digital archive for shared memories, a medium for presenting dogs as family members, a site for developing relationships and support networks, and a space for expressing personality, values, humor, and expertise. The accounts also exposed participants to pet products and peer recommendations, influencing consumer knowledge and behavior. Taken together, the findings indicate that pet Instagram profiles operate as digital extensions of owners’ selves, linking personal identity with the represented identity of the dog and with the social networks surrounding the account. The study extends discussion of the Extended Self Theory into everyday, non-commercial pet-centered social media use.

latest.title: Beyond likes and shares: how social media marketing communications build brand equity and drive electronic word-of-mouth in emerging E-commerce markets
latest.abstract: Abstract Social media is a primary setting in which consumers form brand judgements and recommend products to others. Yet most studies either examine a single social media communication source or combine firm advertising, peer conversation, consumer reviews and influencer endorsements into one composite construct, so the relative associations of these sources with brand equity are rarely compared within one model. It is also unclear whether perceived performance risk weakens or strengthens the translation of brand equity into electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) intention. Using stimulus–organism–response (SOR) theory as an organising framework, this study models four communication sources social media advertising, social media word of mouth, user-generated content and influencer-generated content as stimuli (S), customer-based brand equity (CBBE) as the organism (O) and eWOM intention as the response (R), with performance risk as a moderator of the CBBE → eWOM path. Survey data from 384 e-commerce consumers in Pakistan were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. All four sources were positively associated with CBBE, with user-generated content showing the largest association (β = 0.432), followed by social media advertising (β = 0.183), influencer-generated content (β = 0.178) and social media word of mouth (β = 0.155). CBBE was strongly associated with eWOM intention (β = 0.695), and, contrary to a simple risk-aversion expectation, performance risk strengthened this association (β = 0.157, p < .001). CBBE transmitted significant indirect effects from each source to eWOM intention; when direct paths were added, the associations of social media advertising, social media word of mouth and user-generated content with eWOM intention were fully trans

latest.title: Word-of-Mouth Dissemination of User-Generated Content and Brand Interaction Strategies in Online Marketing
latest.abstract: Online marketing has gradually shifted from enterprise-dominated information dissemination to content communication involving both businesses and consumers. User-generated content (UGC), as an important means through which consumers express product experiences, share consumption opinions, and participate in brand communication, has become a major source of online word-of-mouth. Consumers transform their personal consumption experiences into publicly accessible information through product reviews, usage experiences, videos, images, and comments, thereby influencing other consumers' brand perceptions and purchasing decisions. Meanwhile, UGC provides businesses with new opportunities to understand consumer needs, improve products and services, and establish brand relationships. However, several problems remain in current online marketing practices, including insufficient content authenticity, repetitive content, superficial brand interactions, and delayed responses to negative reviews. Businesses need to improve their marketing strategies in terms of content authenticity, user participation mechanisms, interactive feedback, and long-term brand relationship management. By doing so, they can transform UGC into a sustainable resource for brand communication and promote the transition from one-way promotion to two-way communication.

latest.title: How is AI companionship reshaping young consumers’ emotional engagement and future brand relationships in digital marketing?
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping digital marketing by shifting engagement from transactional interactions to emotionally driven relationships. This practitioner viewpoint aims to explore the rise in AI companionship, including conversational agents, virtual influencers and emotional responsive AI systems, and their role in shaping young consumers’ engagement within digital ecosystems. These technologies enable human-like emotional interaction, fostering trust, attachment and sustained relational bonds between young consumers and AI-mediated brand environments. Design/methodology/approach This article draws on a purposive selected body of recent and seminal literature on consumer psychology to explain how parasocial interactions, anthropomorphism and emotional attachment increasingly influence young consumer-brand relationships. The literature was selected based on its relevance to the study objectives, conceptual contribution and practical implications for marketing. The reviewed studies were synthesised into connected themes, which originally provided the foundation for developing foundational practical and managerial implications presented. Findings It highlights strategic opportunities such as hyper-personalisation, continued engagement and customer value creation, while also identifying governance challenges related to transparency, emotional manipulation, data ethics and consumer vulnerability. Practical implications The viewpoint synthesises these developments into young consumers psychological transformation, strategic implications and socio-technical governance challenges. It further outlines future scenarios where AI companions become embedded actors in digital marketing ecosystems, fundamentally transforming both professional practice and soci

latest.title: Designing transparency in AI influencer marketing: a consumer–agency architecture
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to develop an understanding of AI influencer transparency and its effects on affective and cognitive trust, engagement and consumer well-being. Design/methodology/approach This paper presents a conceptual synthesis of influencer marketing, consumer psychology and human–algorithm interaction research. Findings This paper introduces the Consumer–Agency Architecture (CAA) framework, distinguishing between information, control and provenance transparency. CAA posits that effects of transparency on consumer outcomes are driven by reductions in reactance, whether affective or cognitive. Information transparency primarily mitigates affective reactance; control transparency reduces cognitive reactance; and provenance transparency can attenuate both. Lower reactance, in turn, can support the formation of affective and cognitive trust, engagement and consumer well-being. The framework further identifies boundary conditions that either strengthen or weaken the relationship between transparency and reactance. Research limitations/implications This paper proposes a conceptual framework that remains to be empirically tested. It also posits that transparency effects in AI influencer marketing are primarily driven by reactance, not gains in perceived authenticity. The developed model also assumes that transparency forms have distinct rather than additive or even nonlinear effects on cognitive and affective reactance. Such assumptions could be tested in future work. Practical implications Brands and platforms should treat transparency as a portfolio of design levers rather than a single disclosure: match the specific type of transparency to the focal objective, anticipate trade-offs and avoid one-size-fits-all transparency that can erode trust. latest.title: The Impact of Internal Branding on Brand Attitudes of Customers in the IT Industry: An empirical Study
authors: Malan begum Zardi Dr Charu Bisaria
latest.abstract: Internal branding has emerged as a critical strategic tool in the IT industry, where customer loyalty and brand differentiation are increasingly shaped by employees’ alignment with organizational values. This empirical study investigates the impact of internal branding on brand attitudes of customers, with a focus on demographic dimensions such as age, educational qualification, and job designation. Using a structured questionnaire, data were collected from 200 respondents representing various roles and educational backgrounds in the IT sector. The study employed chi-square analysis to test the association between demographic variables and perceptions of the impact of internal branding. However, the results of chi-square tests indicate no statistically significant relationship between demographic factors and perceptions of internal branding effectiveness, suggesting that the influence of internal branding is relatively consistent across diverse groups. The study contributes to the literature by demonstrating that internal branding strategies can be uniformly applied in the IT industry without significant variation in effectiveness across different demographic profiles. This highlights the universal importance of internal branding practices in fostering positive brand attitudes among customers.

latest.title: Digital marketing strategies and their relationship with customer loyalty in poultry companies in Northern Peru
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe accelerated adoption of digital communication channels has transformed customer relationship management in the poultry sector, particularly in emerging economies where companies face increasing competitive pressure and limited differentiation. In Peru’s poultry industry, many firms have incorporated digital tools into their commercial activities; however, empirical evidence regarding the relationship between digital marketing strategies and customer loyalty remains limited. This study aims to analyze the relationship between digital marketing strategies and customer loyalty in poultry companies located in the Northern Highlands of Peru. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional, and correlational research design was adopted. Data were collected through structured surveys administered to 150 customers who made recurring purchases via digital channels between January and March 2025. Given the non-normal distribution of the data, Spearman’s rho coefficient was used for statistical analysis. The results revealed a strong and statistically significant positive association between digital marketing strategies and customer loyalty (ρ = 0.898; p < 0.001). High correlations were also identified between customer loyalty and specific dimensions of digital marketing, including tangible digital aspects (ρ = 0.854), digital promotions (ρ = 0.826), and digital responsiveness (ρ = 0.831). A complementary multiple regression analysis showed that the three dimensions remained significantly associated with customer loyalty when considered simultaneously, explaining 82.2% of its variance (R2 = 0.822). In conclusion, the findings indicate that digital communication quality, promotional strategies, and rapid responsiveness may contribu

latest.title: Brand Experience Strategy in Building Wardah's Brand Awareness Through Skinverse Campaign
latest.abstract: Brands with already high levels of brand awareness face challenges that differ from those of emerging brands, particularly in maintaining relevance and memorability amid increasingly intense competition. This study examines Wardah's brand experience strategy through the Skinverse campaign, which was conducted in 2024, 2025, and 2026, and its potential contribution to brand awareness. The study employs a qualitative approach with a case study design based on document analysis. Data were obtained from company press releases, 17 articles published by national online media outlets, and Top Brand Index data from 2022 to 2026. These sources were analyzed through deductive coding based on Schmitt's five Strategic Experiential Modules (SEMs). The findings reveal that Skinverse evolved from a science-based educational exhibition in 2024 to an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered skincare clinic in 2025, followed by a skin longevity clinic integrating skin health with lifestyle factors in 2026. Throughout this evolution, the experiential emphasis shifted from the Think module toward the Act module. The document analysis identified four potential mechanisms for strengthening brand awareness: the consistent use of the Skinverse campaign name as a distinctive brand asset; MURI (Indonesian World Records Museum) records and collaborations with experts as drivers of media coverage; personalized artifacts, such as the Skin ID Blueprint, as memory cues; and the expansion of brand associations into skin science and healthy lifestyles. However, the study also found that the campaign's contributions to brand awareness could not be directly substantiated by the Top Brand Index data for the facial moisturizer category.

latest.title: Theoretical Analysis of the Formation Path of Social Identity and Virtual Community Belonging on Brand Loyalty
latest.venue: Journal of Education Humanities and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: With the rise of internet technology and social media, virtual communities have become important platforms for communication between brands and consumers, playing an increasingly significant role in shaping brand loyalty. Based on social identity theory and social belonging theory, this paper summarizes consumer psychological cognition and behavioral responses within virtual communities, analyzing how social identity and community belonging influence the formation of brand loyalty. First, it outlines the relationships among social identity, virtual community belonging, and brand loyalty by defining these concepts. Then, drawing on relevant literature and theoretical reasoning, it proposes a theoretical model—"social identity → community belonging → brand loyalty"—to explain how consumers gradually develop brand loyalty through identity recognition, group interaction, and emotional connection within virtual communities. Next, by examining the classification, comparison, and psychologization of social identity, the paper analyzes how individuals identify with brand communities through self-categorization and group affiliation, and further explores how community belonging acts as a mediator in influencing consumer trust, emotional attachment, and willingness to continue participation. The study argues that social identity strengthens consumers' sense of group identity, making them more receptive to the values and culture of brand communities, while virtual community belonging enhances the psychological contract between consumers and brands through emotional bonds and interactive experiences—both contributing positively to the development of brand loyalty. Additionally, the paper discusses the impact of factors such as community atmosphere, interaction frequency, and inform

latest.title: Digital nostalgia and purchase intention among young consumers: roles of attachment, authenticity and brand trust
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to understand how nostalgia proneness and social media engagement influence consumers’ emotional attachment, perceived authenticity, brand trust and purchase intention in digitally mediated, hyper-connected environments. Based on the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework, nostalgia proneness and social media engagement are treated as stimulus factors; emotional attachment and perceived authenticity as organism factors; and brand trust and purchase intention as response factors. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional research design was adopted using survey data collected from 501 consumers across multiple sectors in India. Structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed conceptual framework and examine the direct and mediating relationships among the constructs. Findings Results show that nostalgia proneness positively impacts consumers’ emotional attachment and perceived authenticity. Social media engagement positively affects emotional attachment. Emotional attachment and perceived authenticity significantly predict brand trust, which leads to higher purchase intention among consumers. In addition, emotional attachment fully mediates the impact of nostalgia proneness on consumers’ brand trust. The study contributes to emerging digital nostalgia literature by explaining how algorithmically mediated nostalgic experiences influence young consumers’ emotional and behavioral responses, Gen Z and Millennials in particular. Research limitations/implications First, the study used a cross-sectional research design. A causal relationship among the study’s variables cannot be concluded because of its cross-sectional nature. Researchers can use longitudinal studies in the future to understand nostalgic exper

latest.title: Digital entrepreneurship challenge: the effect of website/app hopping on information usefulness
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine website/app hopping as a digital entrepreneurship challenge that shapes consumers' perceptions of information usefulness. Specifically, the study investigates how Generation Z (Gen Z) consumers' digital savviness, pragmatism and preference for curated products relate to website/app hopping and how website/app hopping is associated with information usefulness. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a two-study mixed-method design. Study 1 draws on semi-structured interviews with 12 small business entrepreneurs to identify key themes related to Gen Z consumers' website/app hopping. Study 2 tests the resulting model using survey data from 314 US Gen Z consumers aged 18–24, analyzed through exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling and multi-group moderation analysis. Findings The results show that pragmatism and preference for curated products positively predict website/app hopping, while digital savviness might serve as an enabling condition rather than a direct motivator. Website/app hopping is positively related to information usefulness. Multi-group analysis shows that for low-frequency shoppers, digital savviness, pragmatism and preference for curated products all predict website/app hopping. For high-frequency shoppers, pragmatism is the only significant predictor. These findings suggest that digital savviness may be an enabling condition, while pragmatism is the primary motivational driver. Originality/value This study contributes to digital entrepreneurship by reframing website/app hopping as an entrepreneurial information-management challenge rather than merely a consumer search behavior. It shows how Gen Z consumers verify information across fragmented digital platf

latest.title: Between emotion and ethics: a review of advertising appeals, communication and socially responsible consumption (SRC)
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to provide a literature review of the role of advertising appeal and communication on socially responsible consumption (SRC). It synthesizes 75 peer-reviewed articles indexed in Scopus and/or SSCI from the period of 1990–2025. Design/methodology/approach This review adopted a multi-source, iterative search process, incorporating searches via databases, keyword/journal searching, Google Scholar and backward citation searches. Conducted on August 15, 2025, the search provided partial coverage of 2025 publications. Three-stage screening and author-led quality appraisal were applied. The selected articles were analyzed by publication year, geographical context, methodology, respondent characteristics, theoretical framework and advertising appeal themes. Findings The review reveals a transition from traditional rational-emotional appeals toward integrated sustainable, digital, influencer and identity-based communication. Green and corporate social responsibility appeals emerged after 2010, whereas digital and influencer-based persuasion has been gaining prominence since 2015. Emotional and social appeals tend to produce more persuasive results compared with rational appeals, depending on such factors as credibility, authenticity, culture, generations, consumer identity and communication context. Practical implications The results will assist marketing experts, policymakers and communication strategists in creating context-based, credible, authentic and emotional campaigns aimed at promoting socially responsible behavior. Originality/value This review provides an analysis of fragmented literature on advertising appeals by applying the SRC approach, which highlights the idea that no single appeal is universally effective. latest.title: A Theoretical Study on the Conceptual Integration of Plasticity and Resilience in Lifespan Developmental Psychology
latest.venue: Journal of Education Humanities and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Over decades, lifespan developmental psychology has gradually developed a research paradigm centered on the entire life course. Within this framework, "plasticity" and "resilience" have emerged as two key concepts, each reflecting human development from different perspectives—plasticity emphasizing changeability and adaptability, while resilience highlighting stability and stress resistance. However, for a long time, these two constructs have often been studied separately in both theoretical construction and empirical research: plasticity primarily focuses on the potential and extent of changes in cognition, emotion, and behavior due to internal or external influences, underscoring openness and malleability in development; resilience, by contrast, examines individuals' capacity to maintain or restore optimal functioning after facing adversity, setbacks, or stress, emphasizing developmental stability and coping strength. This separation has limited the explanatory power of existing theories, making it difficult to fully account for the coexistence of change and continuity, vulnerability and strength throughout development. This article, grounded in the holistic perspective of lifespan developmental psychology, reviews the origins, meanings, and applications of plasticity and resilience in lifespan research, and compares their similarities and differences in theoretical assumptions, research methods, and measurement tools. It argues for the possibility and necessity of integrating these two concepts. The paper contends that plasticity serves as a prerequisite for resilience—what people demonstrate as resilience in times of hardship is essentially a manifestation of plasticity under specific conditions. latest.title: The Role of Branding in Enhancing the Perceived Marketing Value of Sports Clubs: An Analytical Field Study of Selected Clubs in Wasit Province, Iraq
latest.abstract: Sports clubs increasingly depend on the strength of their brands to retain supporters and attract commercial partners, yet strong fan attachment does not automatically translate into sponsorship, merchandising or revenue. This study examined the relationship between five dimensions of branding (identity, awareness, image, perceived quality and loyalty) and five dimensions of perceived marketing value (fan, sponsorship, media/digital, financial and merchandising value) among stakeholders of three sports clubs in Wasit Province, Iraq. A descriptive–analytical cross-sectional survey was conducted with 264 respondents (200 supporters, 34 players and 30 coaches and administrators) selected by stratified random sampling. Data were collected with a 42-item five-point Likert questionnaire (Cronbach’s α = 0.94) and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression, one-way ANOVA with Tukey–Kramer post hoc tests and independent-samples t tests. Overall branding was rated high (M = 3.59, SD = 0.62), whereas perceived marketing value was moderate (M = 3.09, SD = 0.66). Loyalty was the strongest branding dimension (M = 3.94) and perceived quality the weakest (M = 3.18); among the value dimensions, fan value scored highest (M = 3.71) and merchandising lowest (M = 2.68). Branding correlated strongly with perceived marketing value (r = 0.781, p < .001), and the five dimensions together explained 65.9% of its variance (F(5, 258) = 99.72, p < .001). Loyalty (β = 0.298) and perceived quality (β = 0.241) were the strongest unique predictors. The results reveal a gap between stakeholder attachment and the clubs’ commercial capacity. latest.title: Are Prediction Platform Bettors Distinct from Sportsbook Bettors? Evidence from Skill Perceptions and Positive Play Attitudes
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of sports betting in the United States has been accompanied by the emergence of prediction market platforms offering sports event contracts, which closely resemble traditional wagering while differing in how they are framed and regulated. This study examines whether individuals who buy and sell sports event contracts differ from sportsbook bettors in their perceptions of skill versus luck and their positive play attitudes. Data were collected from two separate samples of U.S. participants recruited through Prolific, including sportsbook bettors (n = 523) and prediction market users (n = 503). A multivariate analysis of covariance (MANCOVA) was conducted to assess group differences across perceived skill, perceived luck, and four dimensions of Positive Play: gambling literacy, honesty and control, personal responsibility, and pre-commitment. Results indicate that prediction market users report significantly higher perceived skill and lower perceived luck compared to sportsbook bettors. Additionally, prediction market users exhibit lower levels of gambling literacy, honesty and control, and personal responsibility. These findings suggest a misalignment between perceived control and responsible engagement among prediction market users. The study contributes to emerging research on sports wagering by highlighting the importance of understanding consumer behavior across differing wagering platforms and offers implications for consumer protection in the evolving sports wagering space.

latest.title: Omnichannel Integration and Seamless Experience in Generation Z Loyalty: Customer Engagement as a Mediator
latest.abstract: Objectives: This study examines the effects of Omnichannel Integration and Seamless Experience on Customer Loyalty among Generation Z consumers of Erigo, with Customer Engagement as a mediating variable.Methodology: This study employed a quantitative explanatory research design using a cross-sectional survey of 250 respondents aged 17–29 who had purchased Erigo products through multiple channels. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0.Finding: The results show that Omnichannel Integration has a positive and significant effect on Customer Engagement (β = 0.335; p < 0.001) and Customer Loyalty (β = 0.159; p = 0.006). Similarly, Seamless Experience positively and significantly affects Customer Engagement (β = 0.317; p < 0.001) and Customer Loyalty (β = 0.197; p < 0.001). Furthermore, Customer Engagement has a positive and significant effect on Customer Loyalty (β = 0.400; p < 0.001). The results also demonstrate that Customer Engagement plays a mediating role in the relationship between Omnichannel Integration, Seamless Experience, and Customer Loyalty.Conclusion: This study concludes that Omnichannel Integration and Seamless Experience contribute to enhancing Customer Loyalty, both directly and indirectly through Customer Engagement. Customer Engagement serves as an important mediating mechanism that transforms integrated and seamless omnichannel experiences into stronger customer loyalty. These findings support the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) framework in the context of Generation Z consumers of Erigo.

latest.title: The Psychological Mechanisms of Scarcity Marketing on Gen Z Impulse Buying Behavior in Malaysia: A Conceptual Framework
latest.abstract: Scarcity marketing has become a dominant persuasive strategy in digital retail, yet its psychological impact on Generation Z consumers in Malaysia remains underexplored. This concept paper proposes a conceptual framework examining the psychological mechanisms through which scarcity marketing influences impulse buying behavior among Malaysian Gen Z consumers. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and integrating Commodity Theory and Social Comparison Theory, the framework posits that three scarcity marketing stimuli—time-limited, quantity-limited, and social proof scarcity—activate four psychological mediators: fear of missing out (FOMO), competitive arousal, perceived urgency, and social comparison, which subsequently drive impulse buying behavior. The framework further proposes that self-control, digital literacy, financial literacy, and brand trust moderate these relationships. Drawing upon a systematic review of literature from 2017 to 2026, this paper synthesizes empirical evidence demonstrating that FOMO exerts the strongest mediating influence on impulse buying, while self-control consistently weakens the relationship between psychological mediators and behavioral outcomes. The proposed framework contributes to consumer behavior theory by clarifying the mediating pathways and boundary conditions of scarcity marketing effects and offers practical implications for marketers, policymakers and consumer educators in developing responsible marketing practices and targeted digital literacy interventions. Empirical validation through quantitative survey methods targeting 400 Malaysian Gen Z consumers aged 18–27 is proposed to test the hypothesized relationships using Structural Equation Modelling.

latest.title: Gamification in Digital Marketing: Enhancing Engagement and Loyalty
latest.abstract: In the contemporary digital marketplace, consumer attention has become increasingly fragmented due to information overload and constant exposure to competing stimuli. Traditional marketing strategies often fail to sustain meaningful engagement, necessitating innovative approaches that integrate motivational design with experiential value. This paper proposes the Gamified Experiential Marketing Framework (GEMF), a novel conceptual model that unites gamification mechanics with experiential marketing principles to address declining consumer attention and foster sustainable brand loyalty. Drawing upon Self-Determination Theory, Flow Theory, and the Technology Acceptance Model, GEMF explains how gamification elements such as points, badges, leaderboards, and narratives activate psychological mediators of motivation, experiential value, and emotional engagement. These mediators, moderated by contextual factors including platform characteristics, cultural context, and demographics, lead to enhanced consumer engagement, loyalty, and immersive brand experiences. The paper contributes theoretically by bridging gamification and experiential marketing, offering a holistic framework that positions gamification as a motivational engine within digital marketing. Practically, GEMF provides actionable insights for marketers to design personalized, ethical, and technologically integrated campaigns. Recommendations for future research include longitudinal studies, cross-cultural validation, and exploration of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and augmented reality. By situating gamification within experiential marketing, GEMF advances both academic discourse and managerial practice, offering a pathway to reimagine consumer-brand relationships in an era of attention sca

latest.title: Marketing Communication Strategy Through Social Media Content based on Local Wisdom to Increase the Added Value of Indonesian Coffee Brands (Study on Conservation Coffee Brands Based on Local Wisdom)
latest.abstract: The coffee industry is a significant sector in Indonesia, contributing to both domestic production and consumption. However, challenges such as declining production due to climate change, limited agricultural land, and increasing global competition have encouraged coffee businesses to adopt more innovative marketing strategies. One emerging approach involves social media marketing communications that incorporate local cultural values and traditional knowledge. This study aimed to explore the social media marketing communication strategies employed by Indonesian coffee businesses, particularly those incorporating local wisdom, and examine their implications for brand value. A descriptive qualitative approach employing a holistic single-case study design was adopted. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with consumers and coffee business owners who actively incorporated local wisdom-based content into their marketing strategies. The findings indicated that such content fostered emotional connections with consumers, enhanced brand awareness and engagement, and strengthened brand loyalty. These findings highlight the strategic potential of integrating local cultural values into social media marketing communications to enhance brand differentiation, strengthen perceived brand value, and support long-term business sustainability in Indonesia's coffee industry

latest.title: Influence of Chatbots on Consumer Purchase Decision-Making in Luxury Products
latest.venue: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology
latest.abstract: The rapid introduction of artificial intelligence into digital commerce has altered the way brands interact with their customers, particularly in the luxury sector, where personal contact and exclusivity are essential for adding value. Among the different technologies, chatbots have emerged as important tools since they allow for immediate communication, recommend products, and offer personalized help. This study examines how consumers view chatbots in the context of luxury products and develops a conceptual framework that links the features of chatbots – specifically responsiveness, personalization, anthropomorphism, and interactivity – with customers' intention to make a purchase through the intermediary effects of trust, perceived value, and emotional engagement. Unlike in the case of mass-market buying, luxury consumption is rooted in symbolic value, in the demonstration of status, and in the satisfaction obtained from the experience rather than simply in functionality, so the character of the digital interaction becomes particularly significant. An exploratory quantitative approach is used in the study, with a survey carried out of people who have used chatbot services on luxury websites. A Chi-square test of independence reveals a statistically significant relationship between the perception of chatbot design (to the extent that it appeared robotic) and the perception of ease of navigation, indicating that opinions about design and usability are related rather than independent. Since the sample size is small, this result is regarded as exploratory and indicative rather than conclusive, and the proposed connections between personalization, responsiveness, trust, perceived value, and purchase intention are given as a conceptual framework for future empirical researc

latest.title: Ethical Consumerism and Identity Construction in Bangladeshi Advertising
latest.abstract: This study looks at the production of an ethical consumer subjectivity in Bangladesh and argues that a distinctive pious consumer culture is constructed, linking both global Islamic laws and local cultural practices. Examining interview-based data of 50 Bangladeshi advertisers from a cultural studies perspective, this paper demonstrates how Islamic cues around ethical consumption narratives work through advertising to sustain a neoliberal logic of global capitalism in the country. It offers an understanding of the emergence of Islamic cultural texts through an interaction among culture, consumption, religion, advertising, and neoliberal capitalism. The ambivalent position of Bangladeshi advertisers in upholding an Islamic identity is also the focal point of this study. Philosophy and Progress, Vol#77-78; No#1-2; Jan-Dec 2025 P 243-280

latest.title: When technological innovation and sustainability meet: extending the push–pull–mooring model of customers’ switching intention to unmanned smart hotels
latest.abstract: This study investigates factors influencing customers’ intention to switch from human-staffed hotels to unmanned smart hotels (USHs) in China. Results indicate that perceived inconvenience, personalization, and environmental benefits directly affect switching intention, whereas perceived efficiency, safety and security, and hygiene and cleanliness influence switching intention only indirectly through switching costs. Attachment to traditional hotel brands moderates the effect of perceived inconvenience on switching costs, whereas surveillance moderates the relationship between safety and security and switching costs. This study is among the first to apply the PPM model to USHs, offering practical insights for hoteliers.

latest.title: Transformation of Business Communication Model in Crisis: Rebranding of Warung New Bahari into Ekspresss Bahari
latest.venue: Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Economy and Management Study
latest.abstract: This study examines the transformation of the business communication model in the franchise crisis experienced by Warung New Bahari (WNB), which underwent rebranding into Ekspresss Bahari (WEB) and succeeded in maintaining only 30 of 125 outlets in the Jabodetabek region. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participatory observation of 8 outlets, business document analysis, and two focus group discussions. Findings reveal that there is a structural disjunction between the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technology and the Cultural Intelligence (CQ) of organizational actors, manifested in seven forms of communication gaps. The transformation of the communication model was designed through three phases—restart-up, reconcept, and rebranding—by integrating CQ into every layer of business communication. The recommended communication model integrates ERP as a strategic communication platform, CQ as the core competence of organizational actors, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an operational enabler. The novelty of this research lies in bridging the studies of ERP, business communication, and cultural intelligence in the context of crisis, downsizing, and rebranding of franchise-based MSMEs.

latest.title: Brand Image, e-WoM, and Hedonic Motivation in GTA V Purchase Decisions among Indonesian Generation Z
