The discussion further delves into outlining key layers of such hubs including AI-powered knowledge extraction and enrichment, knowledge customization, adaptive project management as well as collaboration outcome enhancement and feedback optimization. A set of key elements for AI-enhanced competency transfer hubs was also developed and presented including the issues of technical alignment, advanced AI integration as well as value aspects. The study wraps up by exploring key areas of application in the establishment of AI-enhanced competency transfer hubs and their wider societal significance.

latest.title: Social media, brand image, and price perception as predictors of purchase decisions: Evidence from kopi kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia
latest.venue: The Contrarian Finance Accounting and Business Research
latest.abstract: This study examines whether social media, brand image, and price perception are associated with the purchase decisions of Kopi Kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia, a regional market in which prior findings for this brand are mixed. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 100 customers, recruited through purposive sampling offline and online, was analyzed with multiple linear regression. Social media and brand image were positively and significantly associated with purchase decisions, with effects of comparable and moderate size. Price perception showed no significant association, and its confidence interval included zero, so no direction of effect can be inferred. Together, the three predictors explained about one quarter of the variance in purchase decisions. The study provides jointly estimated effects, confidence intervals, and effect sizes for three commonly studied predictors in an Eastern Indonesian city. Informative social media content and a consistent brand image are associated with purchase decisions, whereas the study offers no evidence for or against a price-perception association. Non-probability sampling, a single time point, self-reported data, and modestly reliable price and purchase-decision scales limit generalization.

latest.title: Word of Mouth, Social Media, and Service Quality on Consumer Purchase Decisions at Culinary Businesses in Surakarta, Indonesia
latest.abstract: Purpose— This study examines the associations of word of mouth, social-media engagement, and perceived service quality with reported culinary purchase decisions among consumers in Surakarta, Indonesia. Research Methodology— A quantitative, cross-sectional questionnaire survey involved 150 purposively selected consumers who used social media and had recently visited local culinary establishments. Reported relationships were estimated using PLS-SEM. Results— Social media had the largest reported positive standardized coefficient (β = 0.518), followed by service quality (β = 0.290) and word of mouth (β = 0.180). The model explained 78.2% of variation in the purchase-decision scores. Research limitations/Implications— Purposive recruitment, reliance on self-reports, possible item overlap, and limited reporting of discriminant validity and bootstrapping constrain causal and population-level inference. The findings support context-specific attention to digital information, recommendations, and service encounters. Originality— The study compares three commonly examined predictors within a single model of culinary-consumer evaluations in Surakarta, highlighting their different estimated magnitudes rather than asserting new causal mechanisms.

latest.title: The relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust: brand credibility, emotional attachment, and perceived quality effects
latest.abstract: Introduction The purpose of this research was to explore the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Specifically, we developed a conceptual model which proposes that brand credibility has a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust, and that perceived quality and emotional attachment have mediating effects on brand trust. Methods We tested the conceptual model by conducting a 2 × 2 (low versus high brand ethicality and low versus high brand credibility) between-subjects experiment, with brand trust as the dependent variable. Data ( N = 208) were collected at a large university in Bangladesh, and were analysed using PLS-SEM. Results Results of the experiment suggest that brand ethicality has a direct effect on brand trust. Brand ethicality also enhances emotional attachment and perceived quality, which, in turn, lead to increased brand trust. Brand credibility, however, does not have a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Discussion Drawing on signalling theory, the findings provide causal evidence that brand ethicality builds brand trust through two parallel pathways: an affective pathway via emotional attachment and a cognitive pathway via perceived quality. Contrary to expectations, brand credibility did not act as a boundary condition, suggesting that brand ethicality and brand credibility may be better understood as sequential antecedents of brand trust rather than as interacting constructs. For practice, marketers ought to increase brand ethicality to increase brand trust, both directly and via emotional attachment and perceived quality.

latest.title: Strengthening Students’ Personal Financial Planning through Budgeting Education at SMAN 10 Pandeglang: A Community Service Report
latest.abstract: Financial literacy is an essential life skill that helps adolescents make informed decisions about limited resources. On 22 October 2026, Universitas Pamulang PSDKU Serang conducted a community-service activity at SMAN 10 Pandeglang to strengthen students’ personal financial planning skills through budgeting education. A total of 200 students participated. The activity addressed pocket-money management, distinguishing needs from wants, allocating expenses, prioritizing spending, and setting savings goals through explanations, guided budgeting exercises, and prioritization scenarios. This article presents a descriptive account based on program materials, event documentation, information from the organizing team, and contemporaneous media coverage. The percentage improvement in students’ financial-planning competence and the number and quality of completed budget worksheets and personal financial plans require further evaluation. Accordingly, the article reports the implementation and learning focus without making numerical claims about competency gains or student outputs.

latest.title: An Integrated Rule Based Robo Advisory, Goal-Planning and Compliance Aware Lending Framework for Boutique Financial Advisory Firms in India: A Design-Science Study
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose. Boutique financial advisory firms in India operate amid record retail participation in mutual funds and a large housing-credit market, yet often rely on manual, analyst-dependent processes and on a narrow revenue base, under tightening conduct regulation. This study asks how such a firm can standardise fund screening and goal-based planning with low-cost, transparent tools and extend responsibly into home-loan intermediation. Design/methodology. Using a design-science approach, the study documents two spreadsheet artefacts built during a two-month internship at an advisory firm in Pune, a rule-based Robo Mutual Fund Advisory model covering 200 funds and a Goal-Based Planner, together with a compliance-aware workflow for a proposed Direct Selling Agent (DSA) vertical. The artefacts are evaluated through sensitivity and scenario analysis, a qualitative capability comparison and a risk assessment, supported by secondary sector data. Findings. Required investment falls steeply with horizon (for a ₹1 crore goal at 10% p.a., about ₹1,28,070 a month over 5 years versus about ₹13,060 over 20 years); a two-point change in inflation moves a 15-year goal by about a third; and a 10% annual step-up roughly doubles the 20-year corpus of a flat SIP. Under illustrative assumptions, a DSA vertical breaks even at about two to four loans a month, with viability driven by lender payout and disbursal conversion. Data quality, conduct and privacy are the most consequential risks. Originality. The paper offers an integrated, auditable design that links investment advice, goal planning and loan sourcing within explicit compliance checkpoints. Limitations. No live client trial was conducted; payout and ticket values are assumptions. Keywords: robo-advisory; goal-based planning; mutual

latest.title: Understanding digital purchase intentions: trust, scarcity marketing, and fomo among generation z
latest.venue: ECOBIZTECH Journal of Economics Business and Technology
latest.abstract: Purpose: to analyze the effects of trust, scarcity marketing, and fear of missing out (fomo) on generation z's purchase intention toward tiktok live shopping in Kendal regency. Method: this study used a quantitative approach and a survey method involving 100 generation z respondents in Kendal regency who had watched tiktok live shopping within the previous three months. Respondents were selected through purposive and snowball sampling techniques. Primary data were collected using an online questionnaire with a five-point likert scale and analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS version 27. Data analysis included validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, and hypothesis testing (t-test, F-test, and adjusted R²). Findings: trust, scarcity marketing, and fomo have positive and significant effects on generation z's purchase intention toward tiktok live shopping. All three variables significantly influence purchase intention, with fomo and scarcity marketing showing stronger effects than trust. The findings highlight the importance of functional, conditional, and social values in shaping generation z's digital purchasing behavior. Implications: this study encourages businesses to build trust, apply transparent scarcity promotions, and strengthen social engagement to increase purchase intention. Originality: lies in integrating trust, scarcity marketing, and fomo within the consumption value theory framework to explain generation z's purchase intention toward tiktok live shopping in Kendal regency.

latest.title: Beyond the Dining Room: Integrating Digital Delivery Platforms, Customer Experience, and Omnichannel Growth in Contemporary Restaurant Management
latest.abstract: The restaurant industry is undergoing a structural transformation in which customer relationships increasingly extend beyond the physical dining room. Digital ordering applications, third-party delivery platforms, restaurant-owned websites, mobile applications, social media, loyalty programs, and in-person dining now operate as interconnected points within a broader customer journey. This transformation creates substantial growth opportunities, but it also introduces new managerial challenges involving platform dependence, channel conflict, customer ownership, service consistency, data integration, and profitability. This article develops a strategic framework for understanding how contemporary restaurants can integrate digital delivery platforms with physical and direct-to-consumer channels to create sustainable omnichannel growth. The analysis examines the evolution of restaurant distribution, the role of third-party delivery platforms, customer experience across digital and physical touchpoints, channel substitution and complementarity, digital reputation, menu adaptation, data-driven decision making, and direct-channel development. Particular attention is given to the distinction between merely offering multiple channels and achieving genuine omnichannel integration. The article argues that digital delivery should not be treated solely as an outsourced logistics function or an additional source of orders. Instead, it should be managed as part of a broader customer relationship and channel strategy. Recent empirical evidence indicates that delivery platforms can increase restaurant sales while also generating spillovers into dine-in activity, although these effects vary considerably by restaurant type and channel structure (Li & Wang, 2025). At the same time, service

latest.title: Developing Students’ Digital Marketing Skills through Creative Social Media Training at SMAN 10 Pandeglang: A Community Service Report
latest.abstract: Social media use is widespread among young people, but effective digital marketing requires more than posting content. It involves identifying an audience, communicating product value, selecting suitable platforms, planning content, and using digital media responsibly. On 22 October 2026, Universitas Pamulang PSDKU Serang conducted a community-service activity at SMAN 10 Pandeglang focused on creative social media marketing skills. A total of 200 students participated. The training addressed digital marketing concepts, product photography and video, promotional writing, branding, content planning, platform selection, and responsible social media use through interactive explanations, demonstrations, practical activities, and group discussion. This article presents a descriptive account based on activity materials, event photographs, information from the organizing team, and contemporaneous media coverage. The percentage improvement in students’ digital marketing competencies, the number and quality of student-created promotional content and marketing plans, and platform-performance indicators require further evaluation. The article therefore reports implementation and learning focus without claiming numerical competency gains or commercial outcomes.

latest.title: Digital marketing strategies and their relationship with customer loyalty in poultry companies in Northern Peru
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe accelerated adoption of digital communication channels has transformed customer relationship management in the poultry sector, particularly in emerging economies where companies face increasing competitive pressure and limited differentiation. In Peru’s poultry industry, many firms have incorporated digital tools into their commercial activities; however, empirical evidence regarding the relationship between digital marketing strategies and customer loyalty remains limited. This study aims to analyze the relationship between digital marketing strategies and customer loyalty in poultry companies located in the Northern Highlands of Peru. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional, and correlational research design was adopted. Data were collected through structured surveys administered to 150 customers who made recurring purchases via digital channels between January and March 2025. Given the non-normal distribution of the data, Spearman’s rho coefficient was used for statistical analysis. The results revealed a strong and statistically significant positive association between digital marketing strategies and customer loyalty (ρ = 0.898; p < 0.001). High correlations were also identified between customer loyalty and specific dimensions of digital marketing, including tangible digital aspects (ρ = 0.854), digital promotions (ρ = 0.826), and digital responsiveness (ρ = 0.831). A complementary multiple regression analysis showed that the three dimensions remained significantly associated with customer loyalty when considered simultaneously, explaining 82.2% of its variance (R2 = 0.822). In conclusion, the findings indicate that digital communication quality, promotional strategies, and rapid responsiveness may contribu

latest.title: The Role of Digital Marketing In Indonesia’s Energy Transition:Understanding Electric Motorcycle Purchase Decisions Through Influencer Marketing and Product Quality
latest.venue: International Journal of Science and Environment (IJSE)
latest.abstract: Indonesia’s energy transition is increasingly reflected in transport electrification, including the expanding electric-motorcycle market. Yet purchase decisions remain shaped by more than policy incentives and charging infrastructure. This study re-examines three market-facing determinants—digital marketing, influencer marketing, and product quality—and evaluates their relationship with consumers’ purchase decisions. A quantitative survey was administered to 85 consumers who had purchased electric motorcycles. The questionnaire contained indicators for the four constructs and was assessed using validity and reliability tests, followed by multiple linear regression, partial significance tests, and a simultaneous F-test in SPSS. All measurement items exceeded the reported validity threshold (r-table = 0.213), while Cronbach’s alpha values ranged from 0.614 to 0.655, indicating acceptable internal consistency under the criterion used in the study. The reported regression results show that digital marketing and influencer marketing carry negative coefficients, whereas product quality carries a positive coefficient. All three predictors are statistically significant individually, and the overall model is significant (F = 26.959; p < 0.001) with R = 0.703, R² = 0.494, and adjusted R² = 0.475. The findings suggest that product quality is the most straightforward positive lever for strengthening purchase decisions, while digital and influencer activities require strategic recalibration toward relevance, authenticity, and decision-stage usefulness rather than simple exposure. The study thus frames consumer adoption as a market-side dimension of Indonesia’s energy transition.

latest.title: Peran Mediasi Kinerja Keuangan: Faktor Determinan dalam Mempengaruhi Keberlanjutan Usaha
latest.venue: Jurnal Akuntansi Ekonomi dan Manajemen Bisnis
latest.abstract: MSMEs play an important role in regional economies, but their sustainability still faces challenges in financial management and technology use. This study examines the effect of entrepreneurship, mental accounting, and digital business strategy on MSME sustainability, with financial performance as a mediating variable. A quantitative approach was used with primary data from questionnaires completed by 125 MSME owners in Pontianak City who had operated for at least two years. Respondents were selected through purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 3.0. The instrument met validity and reliability requirements, with all loadings above 0.700, AVE above 0.500, and Composite Reliability above 0.700. Entrepreneurship (β = 0.317), mental accounting (β = 0.204), and digital business strategy (β = 0.233) have a positive and significant effect on financial performance. For business sustainability, only entrepreneurship has a significant direct effect (β = 0.312). Financial performance has a positive and significant effect on business sustainability (β = 0.408) and fully mediates the effect of mental accounting, but it does not mediate the effects of entrepreneurship or digital business strategy. The model explains 42.6% of the variance in financial performance and 52.0% in business sustainability. These findings indicate that MSME sustainability is largely determined by financial performance and entrepreneurial spirit; therefore, the government and related parties should provide training in entrepreneurship and financial management for MSME owners.

latest.title: How to Apply Environmental Accounting at Regional General Hospitals in Indonesia? (Paradigm of Bioregionalsm)
latest.venue: Journal of Accounting Business and Management (JABM)
latest.abstract: Applying environmental accounting (EA) is a form of the bioregionalism paradigm, which unites economics and ecology. This study aims to find out the application of EA in regional general hospitals (RSUD) in Indonesia today and the benefits of implementing the EA. This study uses a library research approach that integrates the findings of previous studies regarding the implementation of existing EA in RSUD. The results show that not all hospitals have a place to treat adequate waste due to the costs charged to the hospitals. Standards and policies governing EA for RSUD still need to be created, so the reference for implementing EA needs to be revised. RSUD still reports EA voluntarily and no EA has been specifically reported. EA needs to be explicitly implemented and correctly. For this reason, the government must actively monitor and create EA standards that can be used as a reference for hospitals to improve environmental and organizational performance. This study contributes to the development of the application of environmental accounting in hospitals in Indonesia.

latest.title: Pengaruh Penggunaan E-Wallet DANA terhadap Perilaku Konsumtif Mahasiswa (Studi Kasus pada Mahasiswa Universitas Mathla’ul Anwar Banten)
latest.venue: Jurnal Semesta Ilmu Manajemen dan Ekonomi
latest.abstract: Perkembangan teknologi pembayaran digital mendorong mahasiswa menggunakan dompet digital (e-wallet) untuk memenuhi berbagai kebutuhan transaksi secara praktis dan efisien. Namun, kemudahan transaksi serta berbagai promosi yang ditawarkan berpotensi meningkatkan perilaku konsumtif mahasiswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh penggunaan e-wallet DANA terhadap perilaku konsumtif mahasiswa Universitas Mathla’ul Anwar (UNMA) Banten serta mengetahui tingkat hubungan dan kontribusinya. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 81 mahasiswa aktif UNMA Banten yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner dan dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear sederhana, uji t, uji korelasi, serta koefisien determinasi dengan bantuan SPSS versi 31. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan e-wallet DANA berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap perilaku konsumtif mahasiswa, dengan koefisien regresi sebesar 0,731 dan nilai signifikansi kurang dari 0,001. Hasil uji korelasi menunjukkan hubungan positif yang kuat sebesar 0,774, sedangkan koefisien determinasi menunjukkan kontribusi sebesar 59,9%. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa semakin tinggi penggunaan e-wallet DANA, semakin tinggi pula kecenderungan perilaku konsumtif mahasiswa. Oleh karena itu, mahasiswa perlu meningkatkan literasi keuangan digital dan mengendalikan pengeluaran secara bijak.

latest.title: Product quality and price alongside physical evidence in Hanasui lipstick purchase intention
latest.abstract: This study examines associations of perceived product quality, price, and physical evidence with intention to purchase Hanasui lipstick at Toko Kawan Skincare, North Sumatra. The source study used a convenience sample of 96 repeat store customers, including 64 civil servants. Recruitment and eligibility verification were insufficiently documented. Reported OLS summaries gave F(3, 92) = 161.50, p < .001, and R² = .840. Product quality (B = 0.332, 95% CI [0.167, 0.497]), price perception (B = 0.187, 95% CI [0.012, 0.362]), and physical evidence (B = 0.417, 95% CI [0.169, 0.665]) had positive conditional associations. Their unique increments in R² were approximately .028, .008, and .019. VIFs of 4.433-6.856, overlapping and double-barreled items, and a Durbin-Watson statistic of .841 limit interpretation. The latter raises a concern about residual dependence in the recorded order but does not establish recruitment clustering. Conventional inference remains provisional because respondent-level data and recruitment metadata were unavailable for robustness checks. A regression sensitivity analysis gives an 80%-power benchmark of f² ≈ .0835 for one coefficient under independent errors. Physical evidence as trial infrastructure is proposed as a category-specific extension of servicescape reasoning, not an empirically tested mechanism: trial use, perceived risk, and need for touch were not measured. The findings do not establish a ranking of managerial priorities or justify prioritizing facilities over pricing.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan dan Harga terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen pada Nissin Café dan Emporium
authors: Aktama Rara Diva Lucky Pyllia Fitrah
latest.abstract: Persaingan usaha yang menggabungkan layanan kafe dan penjualan ritel mendorong pentingnya evaluasi kualitas pelayanan serta kewajaran harga dalam memahami keputusan pembelian konsumen. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan kualitas pelayanan dan persepsi harga dengan keputusan pembelian pada Nissin Café & Emporium. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif melalui survei potong lintang terhadap 200 responden yang dipilih secara purposif dan seluruhnya telah melakukan pembelian. Pengumpulan data menggunakan kuesioner berskala Likert lima poin. Analisis mengacu pada koefisien regresi dan tabel ANOVA dalam naskah awal, kemudian beberapa statistik dihitung kembali secara aritmetis karena terdapat ketidaksesuaian antarangka yang dilaporkan. Koefisien regresi tak terstandar yang tercantum menunjukkan arah positif untuk kualitas pelayanan (B = 0,438) dan persepsi harga (B = 0,251). Perhitungan dari jumlah kuadrat pada tabel ANOVA menghasilkan F sekitar 96,526, R² sekitar 0,495, dan adjusted R² sekitar 0,490. Hasil ini memberikan indikasi hubungan positif antara evaluasi pelayanan dan harga dengan keputusan pembelian yang dilaporkan responden, meskipun konsistensi statistiknya masih perlu diverifikasi dari keluaran pengolahan data asli. Implikasi sementara adalah pentingnya meningkatkan pengalaman pelayanan dan menjaga kesesuaian harga dengan nilai yang dirasakan konsumen. Keterbatasan penelitian mencakup desain potong lintang, teknik sampling nonprobabilitas, dan belum tersedianya bukti diagnostik regresi serta reliabilitas instrumen secara lengkap.

latest.title: Minat Mahasiswa Universitas Muhammadiyah Sumatera Utara terhadap Pengeluaran Menggunakan QRIS dan Tunai di Café Celesco Mukhtar Basri Medan
latest.abstract: Tujuan dari penelitian ini adalah untuk mengetahui minat mahasiswa Universitas Muhammadiyah Sumatera Utara terhadap penggunaan QRIS dan pembayaran tunai serta hubungannya dengan cara mereka membelanjakan uang di Café Celesco Mukhtar Basri Medan. Dalam penelitian ini, metode kualitatif deskriptif diterapkan pada subjek penelitian, yaitu mahasiswa yang pernah bertransaksi di kafe tersebut. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi langsung, dan informan dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa mahasiswa memiliki minat yang sama terhadap QRIS dan tunai, dan keduanya digunakan bersama dalam transaksi sehari-hari. Sejalan dengan Technology Acceptance Model, QRIS praktis, cepat, mudah digunakan, dan memudahkan pencatatan biaya melalui riwayat transaksi. Pembayaran tunai tetap menjadi pilihan utama siswa karena kemudahan, kebiasaan, kenyamanan, dan ketersediaan saldo digital dan uang tunai. Ini juga menjadi alternatif ketika saldo digital tidak cukup atau jaringan terganggu. Sementara QRIS dapat mengurangi kesadaran tentang jumlah uang yang dibelanjakan, terutama untuk transaksi kecil, tunai memberikan gambaran yang lebih langsung tentang pengeluaran. Namun, metode pembayaran tidak secara langsung mempengaruhi jumlah yang dihabiskan. Pengeluaran sehari-hari lebih bergantung pada kebiasaan dan kemampuan mengelola keuangan, seperti membuat anggaran, mengendalikan diri, dan memeriksa transaksi.

latest.title: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF BRAND IMAGE IN THE EFFECTS OF PRICE PERCEPTION AND PROMOTION ON REPURCHASE INTENTION(A Study of Fore Coffee Customers in Denpasar City)
authors: Ni Luh Ayu Yuliantari, Ni Nyoman Kerti Yasa, Ni Wayan Ekawati, Gede Bayu Rahanatha
latest.abstract: Fore Coffee continues to expand its number of outlets, but its brand strength in encouraging repeat purchases remains weaker than that of its main competitors, despite its products being among the most expensive compared to those offered by locally established coffee chains. This study aims to analyze the effects of price perception and promotion on repurchase intention, as well as the mediating role of brand image in these relationships. The study was conducted among Fore Coffee customers in Denpasar City, involving a sample of 150 respondents selected through judgment sampling. Data were collected using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The results show that price perception and promotion have positive and significant effects on both brand image and repurchase intention, while brand image has a positive and significant effect on repurchase intention. Brand image partially mediates the effects of price perception and promotion on repurchase intention, with mediation proportions of 39.47 percent for the price perception path and 52.73 percent for the promotion path. Brand image is the strongest predictor of repurchase intention, whereas the direct effect of promotion is the weakest. These findings indicate that price perception operates more strongly through a direct effect, while promotion works more extensively through brand image formation. Fore Coffee management is advised to prioritize strengthening the brand's distinctive identity and designing promotional activities as a means of building brand image, rather than using them solely as short-term transactional incentives.

latest.title: Consumer decision in online processed-food purchase: income, price, and digital quality perception
latest.venue: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies
latest.abstract: Purpose This study analyzes the association of consumer income with online processed-food demand through digital quality perception and perceived price on digital food platforms in Makassar, Indonesia. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a cross-sectional online survey of 162 female household food decision-makers. Data were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling in International Business Machines Statistical Package for the Social Sciences Analysis of Moment Structures, with bias-corrected bootstrapping used to assess the indirect association. Findings Consumer income was positively associated with perceived price, but not with digital quality perception or online processed-food demand. Digital quality perception was positively associated with perceived price and online processed-food demand, whereas perceived price was not directly associated with demand. The indirect association was positive but not statistically significant. The model explained 56% of the variance in online processed-food demand. Research limitations/implications The single-city purposive sample and cross-sectional design limit causal interpretation and statistical generalizability. Future studies should use longitudinal, multisource, or platform-based transaction data. Social implications Reliable digital product information can support informed consumer choice and strengthen trust in developing-economy e-commerce. Originality/value This study provides developing-market evidence that platform-based quality cues are the closest correlates of online processed-food demand, while price plays a limited direct role.

latest.title: Pengaruh Content Marketing dan ElePengaruh Content Marketing dan Electronic Word of Mouth (E-WOM) terhadap Repeat Order Produk Skincare di TikTok Shopctronic Word of Mouth (E-WOM) terhadap Repeat Order Produk Skincare di TikTok Shop
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of Content Marketing and Electronic Word of Mouth (E-WOM) on repeat orders of skincare products on TikTok Shop. A quantitative associative approach was applied. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale from 26 respondents selected through purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression, including t-test, F-test, and the coefficient of determination. The reported results show that Content Marketing has a positive but statistically insignificant partial effect on Repeat Order (p = 0.252). In contrast, E-WOM has a positive and significant partial effect (p = 0.008). Simultaneously, Content Marketing and E-WOM significantly affect Repeat Order (F-test significance = 0.000088). The coefficient of determination is 0.556, indicating that the two independent variables explain 55.6% of the variation in Repeat Order. The findings suggest that consumer reviews and shared experiences are important considerations in repeat purchasing, while content marketing should be supported by product quality and a satisfactory consumer experience.

latest.title: Transformasi Perilaku Konsumtif Menjadi Perilaku Produktif melalui Kebiasaan Menabung Saham
latest.abstract: Perkembangan teknologi finansial dan ekosistem belanja daring (e-commerce) telah mempercepat budaya konsumtif di kalangan masyarakat usia produktif, khususnya Generasi Milenial dan Generasi Z. Fenomena belanja impulsif akibat gaya hidup hedonis dan tekanan sosial di media digital mengancam ketahanan keuangan mereka dalam jangka panjang. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis bagaimana kebiasaan menabung saham di pasar modal dapat mengubah perilaku konsumtif menjadi perilaku produktif. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kualitatif melalui tinjauan pustaka sistematis (systematic literature review) terhadap 15 artikel jurnal terakreditasi nasional dan internasional yang terbit pada tahun 2024 hingga 2026. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa kebiasaan menabung saham berfungsi sebagai sarana intervensi perilaku yang menggeser tujuan penggunaan uang, dari sekadar memuaskan keinginan sesaat menjadi upaya mengumpulkan aset produktif. Proses perubahan ini terjadi melalui empat mekanisme utama, yaitu menata ulang pola pikir penganggaran (mental accounting), menerapkan prinsip membayar diri sendiri terlebih dahulu (pay yourself first), mengganti kesenangan belanja sesaat dengan kepuasan melihat pertumbuhan aset, serta memanfaatkan aplikasi keuangan sebagai pengunci komitmen. Keberhasilan perubahan perilaku ini didukung oleh empat faktor penentu, yakni pemahaman keuangan yang praktis, pengendalian diri dari rasa takut tertinggal tren (FoMO), konsistensi mengelola keuangan, serta dukungan lingkungan sosial dan lembaga edukasi. Kebiasaan menyisihkan dana secara rutin ke instrumen saham terbukti mampu menekan belanja impulsif sekaligus membangun kemandirian ekonomi.

latest.title: EKSPLORASI PERILAKU EKONOMI SISWA DALAM PENGGUNAAN E-WALLET SEBAGAI BENTUK LITERASI KEUANGAN DIGITAL DI SMA NEGERI 17 MEDAN
latest.abstract: This study aims to explore students' economic behavior in using e-wallets as a form of digital financial literacy at SMA Negeri 17 Medan. This study employed a qualitative method with an exploratory approach. The research informants consisted of 15 students as primary informants and 2 teachers as supporting informants. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, observation, and documentation. Data analysis used the Miles and Huberman interactive model, consisting of data collection, data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. Data validity was established through source and technique triangulation.The results showed that students' use of e-wallets was influenced by personal needs, convenience and practicality of transactions, social environment, technological development, as well as promotions and cashback. E-wallets were used for various purposes, including purchasing food and beverages, online shopping, internet quota payments, money transfers, transportation, and other needs. Students' economic behavior in managing their finances varied. Some students were able to set spending limits, monitor their balance, record transactions, save money, and prioritize their needs, while others had less control over their spending and were easily influenced by wants and promotional offers. The study also revealed a gap between students' ability to operate e-wallet features and their ability to manage finances wisely. Therefore, e-wallet use can become part of digital financial literacy when accompanied by the ability to manage, control, and evaluate financial use

latest.title: Price Perception and Promotional Effectiveness in Airport Food & Beverage Consumption: An Exploratory Survey with Implications for Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad
latest.abstract: Airport food and beverage (F&B) outlets operate in a distinctive retail environment in which passengers balance convenience, time constraints and reference prices shaped by alternatives outside the terminal. This study examines perceived airport F&B prices, reported price-related purchase deterrence, promotional visibility and preferred purchase triggers, drawing on an online questionnaire completed by 86 respondents and a qualitative secondary-research review undertaken as part of a Summer Internship Project (SIP). The secondary review covered airport commercial environments and F&B practices at Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (RGIA), Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru. In the survey, 60.0% of valid respondents rated airport F&B prices in the two highest categories on a five-point scale, and 91.8% reported that high prices had deterred a purchase at least sometimes. Promotional visibility was relatively high (87.1% noticed promotions always, often or sometimes), while 6.0% reported being frequently influenced by promotions. Combo offers were selected by 67.1% as an activity that could encourage trial, and 72.6% identified lower prices as a change that would encourage purchase. Overall experience averaged 3.07 (SD = 0.80; n = 84). The findings point to perceived value and offer design as important issues for further investigation. The survey questions refer to airport F&B generally rather than documenting transactions at RGIA specifically; therefore, the findings are interpreted as exploratory evidence with implications for RGIA, not as representative estimates of its passengers. The sample is non-probability-based and self-reported.

latest.title: PENGARUH CONTENT MARKETING DAN PERSEPSI HARGA TERHADAP KEPUTUSAN PEMBELIAN KONSUMEN DI OLLSHOPBYDINDA
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of digital business has encouraged business owners to implement effective marketing strategies to enhance consumers' purchasing decisions. Content Marketing and price perception are considered important factors that may influence consumers' purchasing decisions. This study aims to analyze the effects of Content Marketing and price perception, both simultaneously and partially, on consumers' purchasing decisions at Ollshopbydinda. This research employed a quantitative method with a causal approach. The sampling technique used was purposive sampling, resulting in a total of 100 respondents. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of SPSS version 26. The results indicate that Content Marketing and price perception simultaneously have a significant effect on consumers' purchasing decisions. Partially, Content Marketing has a positive and significant effect on consumers' purchasing decisions. Likewise, price perception also has a positive and significant effect on consumers' purchasing decisions

latest.title: MARKETPLEYSLARDA CHEGIRMA VA BEPUL YETKAZIB BERISHNING XARID QARORIGA TA’SIRI
latest.abstract: Ushbu maqolada marketpleyslarda qo‘llaniladigan chegirma va bepul yetkazib berish aksiyalarining iste’molchilarning xarid qaroriga ta’siri tahlil qilinadi. Elektron savdoning kengayishi natijasida xaridor mahsulotning faqat asosiy narxiga emas, balki chegirma miqdori, yetkazib berish xarajati, aksiya muddati, qulaylik va yakuniy to‘lov summasiga ham e’tibor bermoqda. Maqolada narxni idrok etish, iqtisodiy manfaatni his qilish, shoshilinch xarid, psixologik ta’sir va xarid niyatining shakllanishi kabi omillar yoritilgan. Mavzu bo‘yicha ilmiy tadqiqotlar tahliliga tayangan holda chegirma va bepul yetkazib berish alohidaalohida ham, birgalikda ham xarid ehtimolini oshirishi mumkinligi ko‘rsatildi. Shu bilan birga, aksiyaning shartlari murakkab bo‘lsa yoki mahsulotning dastlabki narxi sun’iy oshirilgan deb qabul qilinsa, uning ijobiy ta’siri pasayishi mumkin. Maqolada marketpleyslar uchun aksiyalarni samarali tashkil etish bo‘yicha amaliy takliflar ham berilgan.

latest.title: Pengaruh Mikrotransaksi Game Online terhadap Pengelolaan Keuangan Mahasiswa (Survei pada Mahasiswa Jurusan Akuntansi Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis Universitas Halu Oleo)
latest.venue: Jurnal Semesta Ilmu Manajemen dan Ekonomi
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh mikrotransaksi game online terhadap pengelolaan keuangan mahasiswa Jurusan Akuntansi Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis Universitas Halu Oleo. Populasi dalam penelitian ini adalah mahasiswa Jurusan Akuntansi Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis Universitas Halu Oleo angkatan 2022–2025. Teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan metode purposive sampling, sehingga diperoleh 90 responden. Jenis data yang digunakan adalah data kuantitatif dengan sumber data primer yang diperoleh melalui penyebaran kuesioner. Metode analisis data menggunakan regresi linear sederhana dengan bantuan software IBM SPSS versi 31. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa mikrotransaksi game online berpengaruh negatif terhadap pengelolaan keuangan mahasiswa. Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa semakin tinggi intensitas mahasiswa dalam melakukan mikrotransaksi, maka kemampuan mereka dalam mengelola keuangan cenderung menurun. Berdasarkan hasil penelitian dapat disimpulkan bahwa mikrotransaksi memiliki pengaruh negatif terhadap pengelolaan keuangan mahasiswa, sehingga mahasiswa disarankan untuk mampu meningkatkan pengendalian keuangan, khususnya dalam pengeluaran pada mikrotransaksi game online.

latest.title: Beyond Rational Choice: A Behavioral Game-Theoretic Frameworkfor Consumer Decision-Making
latest.venue: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
latest.abstract: Since Behavioral Economics explains decisions through bounded rationality and mental shortcuts, it is necessary to incorporate strategic interactions into such analyses. This study develops an integrated framework for analyzing irrational purchasing decisions, which includes elements of Behavioral Economics, non-cooperative Game Theory, econometric analysis, and an integrated model of consumer behavior, the Consumer Irrational Utility Model (CIUM). The study employs a quantitative survey of personal care products consumers in the FMCG market, modeling a consumer and a seller as two players in a 2 × 2 non-cooperative game. The game is analyzed using best-response strategies, followed by the derivation of a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium. The results of the game-theoretic model are then tested using Linear Probability Model (LPM) and Weighted Least Squares (WLS) for estimation purposes. The results of the behavioral determinants, validated in the LPM and WLS estimations, are then incorporated into CIUM, which explains how irrational behavior by a consumer deviates from the utility-maximizing behavior of a rational human being. The study reveals that in the Indian FMCG market, consumers mainly adopt the Relative Decision Paradox strategy, whereas sellers mainly adopt the Strategized Pricing strategy. The study further reveals that the behavioral variables identified in the study have a significant impact on consumers' purchasing decisions. Also, results from the CIUM indicate that the economic utility of a product and the utility influenced by various behavioral factors in strategic interactions in the market jointly determine the overall utility of a product for a consumer.

latest.title: CONSUMER EVALUATIONS OF RESTAURANTS IN BOLU ON DIGITAL PLATFORMS: THE TRIPADVISOR CASE
latest.abstract: This study examines user reviews of restaurants in Bolu on Tripadvisor. The research uses a qualitative approach and employs descriptive content analysis as the analytical method. A total of 274 user reviews from 10 restaurants that provided meaningful content and were posted between January and December 2025 were analyzed. The findings indicate that most reviews were positive, with taste being the most frequently emphasized dimension. Analyses of food and beverage offerings confirm the meat-based nature of Bolu cuisine, while local dishes such as mantı, gözleme, and soups strongly reflect the region’s gastronomic identity on digital platforms. Additionally, staff and service quality, atmosphere and ambiance, cleanliness and hygiene, and price–value perception were identified as key themes shaping the user experience. Overall, the results support the influence of digital user evaluations on restaurant image and consumer preference decisions, and demonstrate that both product quality and service performance in gastronomic destinations are perceived and evaluated through online platforms.

latest.title: Peran Pemasaran Media Sosial dan Atribut Produk dalam Keputusan Pembelian Paket Wisata One Day Lampung
latest.abstract: This research is motivated by the importance of social media marketing and product attributes in influencing consumer purchase decisions on tour packages. This study aims to determine the influence of social media marketing on purchase decisions, the influence of product attributes on purchase decisions, and the influence of social media marketing and product attributes simultaneously on the purchase decision of One Day Lampung tour packages at CV Wondery Agita Wisata. This study uses a quantitative method. Data was collected through the distribution of questionnaires to 150 respondents who had purchased One Day Lampung tour packages and viewed CV Wondery Agita Wisata social media marketing content using purposive sampling techniques. Data analysis was carried out using validity tests, reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, t-tests, and F tests with the help of the Statistical Package for Social Science (SPSS) program, The results of the study showed that social media marketing had a significant influence on the purchase decision of tour packages. Product attributes also have a significant influence on purchasing decisions. In addition, social media marketing and product attributes simultaneously have a significant influence on the purchase decision of One Day Lampung tour packages at CV Wondery Agita Wisata.

latest.title: PENERAPAN MENTAL ACCOUNTING DALAM PENGELOLAAN BISNIS GYM (STUDI KASUS ESHADE FITNESS CENTER)
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the application of mental accounting in the financial management of a gym business that faces recurring, seasonal fluctuations in membership numbers. It explores how the business owner manages funds to navigate off-peak seasons. Employing a qualitative approach with a case study design, the research focuses on Eshade Fitness Center. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with the owner-manager and analyzed via data reduction and conclusion drawing. The findings reveal that the owner-manager categorizes revenue from memberships, personal training services, and product sales into distinct types of funds: "entrusted funds" (held on behalf of others), "profit-sharing funds," and "trading funds." These funds are allocated to fixed operational costs, salaries, maintenance, and the owner’s profit, with varying rules for inter-fund borrowing; while funds allocated for salaries and fixed operational costs cannot be borrowed, the other categories may be accessed, provided they are repaid. The business undergoes regular evaluation. During peak periods, surplus revenue is set aside as a reserve for the off-peak season, whereas during quieter periods, a decline in revenue is viewed as expected, given the owner’s familiarity with the business’s seasonal calendar. The study concludes that the owner utilizes three components of mental accounting, a practice that helps cover expenses during off-peak periods without the need to incur debt.

latest.title: Pengaruh Ulasan Pelanggan Online dan Persepsi Harga terhadap Niat Beli Konsumen Sudut Kedai di Metland Transyogi
latest.abstract: A sharp increase in menu prices at Sudut Kedai, coupled with shifting customer engagement online, raises a fundamental question: do online reviews and price perception actually influence purchase intention? This study examines both factors among Sudut Kedai consumers in Metland Transyogi. Questionnaires were distributed to 120 respondents who had read online reviews of Sudut Kedai, selected through convenience sampling. Data analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3.0. Online customer reviews demonstrate a positive and significant effect on purchase intention (path coefficient 0.245; T-statistic 3.271; p 0.001), as does price perception (path coefficient 0.373; T-statistic 4.861; p 0.000), with an R-Square of 0.220. Credible and informative reviews build buyer trust; prices perceived as proportional to quality enhance purchase intention. Sudut Kedai needs to actively manage customer reviews and maintain fair pricing to strengthen purchase intention amid an increasingly competitive culinary market.

latest.title: The Influence Of Price Perception And Online Customer Reviews On Purcashing Decisions For House Of Smith Products On The Tiktok Application
latest.venue: Journal of Management Economic and Accounting
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of price perception and online customer reviews on purchasing decisions for House of Smith products through the TikTok application. The study employed a quantitative method with descriptive and causal approaches. The population consisted of House of Smith consumers on TikTok, whose total number was unknown, while a sample of 100 respondents was selected using non-probability sampling with a purposive sampling technique based on the Lemeshow formula. Primary data were collected through an online questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale, transformed using the Method of Successive Interval (MSI), and analyzed by multiple linear regression with SPSS version 25. The results show that price perception and online customer reviews simultaneously have a significant effect on purchasing decisions, with an F-value of 34.359 and p < 0.001. Partially, price perception has a positive and significant effect, with a regression coefficient of 0.152, a t-value of 2.170, and p = 0.032. Online customer reviews also have a positive and significant effect, with a regression coefficient of 0.400, a t-value of 4.683, and p < 0.001. The R Square value of 0.415 indicates that both variables explain 41.5% of the variation in purchasing decisions, while the remaining 58.5% is explained by other factors outside the study. These findings indicate that online customer reviews exert a more dominant influence than price perception in encouraging purchasing decisions for House of Smith products on TikTok

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan, Persepsi Harga, dan Word of Mouth terhadap Loyalitas Pelanggan Lily Laundry Express
latest.venue: Indonesian Journal of Innovation Multidisipliner Research
latest.abstract: Kedekatan antarpesaing di sekitar kampus dan pondok pesantren memberi pelanggan banyak pilihan jasa laundry. Penelitian ini menganalisis hubungan kualitas pelayanan, persepsi harga, dan word of mouth dengan loyalitas pelanggan Lily Laundry Express di Kalibeber, Wonosobo. Penelitian menggunakan survei potong lintang terhadap 100 pelanggan yang dipilih melalui purposive sampling. Analisis mencakup 14 butir pernyataan berskala Likert lima tingkat, statistik deskriptif, uji validitas butir dan reliabilitas, serta regresi linier berganda dengan galat baku robust HC3. Kualitas pelayanan berhubungan positif dan signifikan dengan loyalitas pelanggan (B = 0,295, p = 0,0199). Persepsi harga (p = 0,7051) dan word of mouth (p = 0,0957) tidak menunjukkan hubungan parsial yang signifikan. Model signifikan secara keseluruhan, F(3, 96) = 8,363 dengan p < 0,001, dan menjelaskan 43,2% variasi skor loyalitas pelanggan. Temuan ini mendukung penetapan kualitas pelayanan sebagai prioritas dalam mempertahankan pelanggan, terutama melalui konsistensi hasil cucian, ketepatan waktu penyelesaian, dan ketanggapan karyawan. Implikasi praktis dari studi ini menegaskan bahwa manajemen perlu merancang standar operasional prosedur yang terukur guna menjaga kebersihan dan kerapian pakaian secara berkelanjutan. Selain itu, pelatihan rutin bagi staf operasional serta penyediaan saluran komunikasi keluhan yang responsif sangat diperlukan untuk mencegah perpindahan pelanggan ke penyedia jasa kompetitor. Studi lanjutan disarankan mengkaji variabel kepuasan dan kepercayaan pelanggan.

latest.title: Principal Modern Trends in The International Hotel Industry
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
latest.abstract: Technological innovation is a primary driver of development in the global hotel sector, leading to significant shifts in human resource requirements, customer expectations, and environmental impact. Simultaneously, sustainability, the increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI), and the integration of local cultural identity have emerged as key strategic priorities. Hotels are increasingly adopting AI, digital booking systems, smart-room technologies, and optimized revenue management strategies to enhance both competitiveness and profitability. This article examines the most prominent contemporary trends shaping the global hotel industry, analyzes their implications for hotel management, and identifies the opportunities and challenges associated with their implementation. The study emphasizes that successful hotel development requires a synthesis of digital transformation, environmental responsibility, financial performance, and hospitality. It concludes that the future competitiveness of hotels will depend on their ability to strike a balance and align sustainable business practices with human interaction and the efficiency of the technology employed.

latest.title: When Halal Brand Trust Does Not Guarantee Brand Equity: Evidence from Hijab-Oriented Hair Care
latest.venue: International Journal of Humanity Advance Business & Sciences (IJHABS)
latest.abstract: Halal brand trust plays an important role in shaping consumer confidence, yet its contribution to customer-based brand equity remains inconclusive. This study examines the relationships among halal brand image, halal brand trust, and halal brand equity, emphasizing the mediating role of halal brand trust in Indonesia's hijab-oriented hair-care market. A quantitative approach employing a cross-sectional survey design and purposive sampling was specified, with data analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The analytical findings indicate that halal brand image is positively associated with both halal brand trust and halal brand equity. However, halal brand trust does not demonstrate a statistically significant relationship with halal brand equity, and its mediating effect is not supported. These findings suggest that favorable halal brand perceptions can strengthen consumer confidence without necessarily translating into additional brand value. The study highlights a distinction between trust formation and brand equity development, suggesting that confidence in halal compliance alone may be insufficient to create meaningful brand differentiation. The proposed framework contributes to halal branding research by examining the limitations of trust as a mechanism connecting halal brand image to brand equity within hijab-oriented personal care. From a managerial perspective, the analysis emphasizes the potential importance of complementing credible halal positioning with distinctive product benefits and consistent functional performance to strengthen customer-based brand equity.

latest.title: THE EFFECT OF SOCIAL MEDIA AND SERVICE QUALITY ON CUSTOMER LOYALTY AT BARBERSHOP ODE IN JAMBI CITY
latest.venue: Indonesian Journal of Social Sciences, Policy and Politics.
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of social media and service quality in shaping customer loyalty at Barbershop Ode in Jambi City. This study uses a descriptive qualitative approach through observation, documentation, and a literature review of seven relevant local journals. Documentation data indicate that the number of customers increased from 9,000 in 2021 to 10,800 in 2025, although a decline occurred in 2023. Meanwhile, Instagram followers increased from 379 to 691, while the engagement rate remained at approximately 1.5%. The percentage of repeat customers ranged from 35% to 45%, with approximately 80–100 regular customers remaining active each month.The findings indicate that social media plays an important role in increasing brand awareness, providing information, encouraging interaction, and maintaining relationships with customers. Furthermore, service quality, measured through five dimensions: tangibles, reliability, responsiveness, assurance, and empathy, contributes to creating positive customer experiences, satisfaction, and trust. These two aspects complement each other in building customer loyalty. Social media helps shape customer perceptions and expectations, while service quality determines the actual experiences customers receive when using the services. Positive experiences can encourage customers to revisit and recommend the barbershop to others.This study concludes that customer loyalty at Barbershop Ode can be strengthened through the integration of effective social media strategies and consistent improvements in service quality. Therefore, both aspects are essential in maintaining customer relationships, increasing repeat visits, and supporting the long-term sustainability of the business.

latest.title: THE ROLE OF PRODUCT QUALITY AND PROMOTION ON CONSUMER TRUST IN PRELOVED CLOTHING IN JAMBI
latest.venue: Indonesian Journal of Social Sciences, Policy and Politics.
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of product quality and promotional strategies in building consumer trust in preloved clothing purchases in Jambi City. This research employs a descriptive qualitative approach using observation and literature review. Observations focused on product characteristics, sorting and grading processes, information transparency, digital promotional activities on Instagram, TikTok, and WhatsApp, seller-consumer interactions, and social proof such as reviews and testimonials. The literature review examined seven verified national journal articles relevant to product quality, promotion, and consumer trust, complemented by three articles from the Indonesian Journal of Social Sciences, Policy and Politics (IJSSPP). Findings indicate that product quality is not only about physical condition but also consistency between actual product condition and information provided. Promotional strategy functions as uncertainty reduction. Transparent, informative, and testimonial-supported promotions strengthen trust, while excessive promotion without quality creates doubt. Consumer trust is formed through consistency between pre-transaction communication and post-transaction experience.

latest.title: Price, Promotion, and Consumer Reviews on Repurchase Intention through Customer Satisfaction among Marketplace Users
latest.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the effects of price, promotion, and consumer reviews on repurchase intention with customer satisfaction as a mediating variable among marketplace users. An explanatory quantitative approach was employed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Data were obtained through questionnaires from 152 university students in Probolinggo Regency who used marketplaces. The analysis showed that price, promotion, and consumer reviews had positive and significant effects on customer satisfaction. Customer satisfaction also had a positive and significant effect on repurchase intention. Directly, price, promotion, and consumer reviews had positive and significant effects on repurchase intention. The indirect-effect analysis showed that customer satisfaction mediated the relationships of price, promotion, and consumer reviews with repurchase intention. These findings indicate that fair pricing, relevant promotions, and credible consumer reviews can strengthen satisfaction and encourage repeat purchases in marketplaces

latest.title: Peran E-Review dalam Memediasi Influencer Marketing dan Price Diversity terhadap Purchase Decision Produk Fashion di Marketplace (Studi Kasus pada Remaja Putri di Kota Pontianak)
latest.venue: Jurnal Ekonomi Bisnis Manajemen dan Akuntansi
latest.abstract: This study aims to investigate the influence of e-reviews as a mediating variable between influencer marketing and price diversity on fashion product purchase decisions among young women in Pontianak City on marketplace platforms This study employs a quantitative method with an explanatory research approach. The sampling technique uses purposive sampling, with a sample size of 125 respondents. Data collection was conducted via a questionnaire and analyzed using SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that both influencer marketing and price diversity have a significant positive influence on e-reviews and purchasing decisions. In addition, e-reviews also have a significant positive effect on purchasing decisions. Furthermore, e-reviews were found to act as a partial mediator linking influencer marketing and price diversity to purchasing decisions. This study highlights the important role of integrated collaboration between influencer marketing, price diversity, and e-reviews in shaping purchasing decisions for fashion products on marketplaces

latest.title: The impact of tax compliance governance on the corporate financial performance during the COVID-19 crisis
latest.abstract: This study examines how tax compliance governance affects the financial performance of listed companies in Morocco during the challenging COVID-19 crisis period. Building on the recognition that tax compliance extends well beyond traditional control mechanisms and is shaped by broader institutional and behavioral factors (Alm, 2019), alongside evidence that responsible corporate practices can strengthen relationships with key stakeholders (Freeman et al., 2010), we approached the tax compliance seal as a governance mechanism with the potential to generate tangible financial benefits. Using panel data from 2013 to 2021, we conducted a linear regression analysis, completed with robustness tests to evaluate model specification and ensure estimate reliability. The results show a significant positive relationship between the tax compliance seal and firms’ financial performance, although its effects vary by performance indicator and time period. These results suggest that effective tax compliance governance can strengthen financial resilience and market capitalization during times of economic uncertainty.

latest.title: The Influence of Social Media Marketing and Brand Awareness on Purchase Decisions for Decoration Services at Catasa.id In South Tangerang
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of Social Media Marketing and Brand Awareness on purchase decisions for decoration services through Instagram @Catasa.id, both partially and simultaneously. The research used a quantitative associative approach. Data were collected through questionnaires from 106 respondents who knew or had interacted with @Catasa.id. The data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, simple and multiple linear regression, correlation, coefficient of determination, t-test, and F-test with IBM SPSS Statistics 27. The results show that Social Media Marketing has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (t = 8.361; p < 0.001), while Brand Awareness has a positive but insignificant effect (t = 0.925; p = 0.357). Simultaneously, Social Media Marketing and Brand Awareness have a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (F = 70.849; p < 0.001). The coefficient of determination is R² = 0.579, indicating that 57.9% of the variation in purchase decisions is explained jointly by the two independent variables.

hot.title: A Glance on Changing Workplace Dynamics Post Covid-19 in India: A Review of Psychological Employee Withdrawal Behavior
hot.abstract: Advances in Consumer Research (Abbreviated as Adv. Consum. Res.) is a distinguished journal based in the United States and published by Sheridan Books. The journal is highly regarded in the academic community, particularly within the fields of Business, Management, and Accounting, with a specific focus on Marketing.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The Impact of Visual Elements of Packaging Design on Purchase Intention: Brand Experience as a Mediator in the Tea Bag Product Category
hot.abstract: While packaging design plays a vital role in experience-oriented markets, how multiple visual elements influence purchase intention through brand experience remains unclear. This study addresses this gap by employing innovative orthogonal experiments to examine the complex relationship between the visual elements of packaging design and purchase intention for low-involvement products, integrating both design and marketing perspectives. Through orthogonal experimental design, we developed 14 packaging prototypes as stimuli by systematically manipulating five visual elements (Colour, Graphics, Logo, Typography, and Layout). The framework and prototypes were validated through expert evaluation. Data were collected via a cross-sectional survey from 490 tea bag consumers and analysed using SPSS (version 29.0) for preliminary data processing and Mplus (version 8.3) for structural equation modelling. Our results reveal the direct effects of visual packaging elements on consumer purchase intention. Notably, Colour, Graphics, Logo, and Layout significantly influence purchase intention through brand experience mediation. Importantly, our multi-level analysis of visual elements unveils distinct patterns in how different design levels (e.g., colour harmony, graphic types) affect consumer responses. This study provides novel theoretical insights into how consumers make purchase decisions based on packaging design visual elements, addressing a significant gap in existing research. Unlike previous studies focusing on isolated design elements, our systematic classification and multi-level analysis offer both theoretical insights into packaging design mechanisms and practical guidelines for designers and practitioners.

hot.title: Digital Tourism and Smart Development: State-of-the-Art Review
hot.abstract: The intersection between digital technologies and tourism emerges as a prominent area of research within the tourism industry. This is primarily driven by the immense complexity of digital tourism itself as a multifaceted social, economic, and cultural phenomenon. This paper reveals the future implications of tourism in the context of digital intelligence. To gain insights into the latest applications of digital tourism, this work reviews 278 studies spanning from 2012 to 2024. A systematic literature analysis method is proposed to identify the research hotspots and trends. Through value co-creation theory and Schumpeter’s innovation theory, five key trajectories are suggested, as follows: in-depth application of digital technologies in tourism, spawning new scenarios, new forms and new modes of digital tourism, and deep integration of digital economy and tourism real economy. This state-of-the-art review will help to reflect the efforts towards promoting the smart development of digital technologies in tourism.

hot.title: Factors influencing Generation Z’s intention to purchase sustainable clothing products in Vietnam
hot.abstract: The increasing awareness of environmental challenges has significantly influenced consumer behavior, with sustainable products, particularly sustainable clothing, becoming a top priority for Generation Z consumers. This study aims to investigate the factors influencing Generation Z's purchase intentions toward sustainable clothing in Vietnam, guided by the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model and Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) frameworks. Specifically, it examines the effects of green perceived value, green perceived quality, perceived price, social influence, product design, environmental concern, and environmental knowledge on purchase intentions. The study also explores the mediating roles of environmental attitude and product attitude in these relationships. The research employed a quantitative approach, using a Likert scale questionnaire to gather data from 641 Vietnamese Generation Z consumers. The study utilized exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM) to analyze the data. The results revealed that all proposed hypotheses were supported, indicating that all factors significantly impact environmental attitude and product attitude, which, in turn, influence purchase intention. The results emphasize the strong mediating role of environmental attitude and product attitude, suggesting that consumers with positive attitudes toward the environment and products are more likely to intend to purchase sustainable clothing. This research provides valuable insights into the psychological and contextual factors that influence Generation Z's sustainable consumption behavior. For marketers, these findings underscore the need to promote transparency in sustainable practices, emphasize high product quality an

hot.title: Perceived Value, Consumer Engagement, and Purchase Intention in Virtual Influencer Marketing: The Role of Source Credibility and Generational Cohort
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: As virtual influencers gain popularity, understanding the factors driving consumer responses is essential. However, limited research explores how perceived value (informativeness, entertainment, novelty, and incentives) and consumer engagement influence purchase intention. Perceived value is a key predictor of consumer behavior, while consumer engagement enhances perceived value and marketing effectiveness. Additionally, the moderating roles of source credibility and generational cohort remain underexplored. This study examines these relationships through a survey of 331 Chinese Generation Y and Z consumers, analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). The results show that informativeness, entertainment, and incentives positively influence purchase intention, while novelty has a negative effect. Consumer engagement drives purchase intention and enhances perceived value. Source credibility and generational cohort moderate these effects. When source credibility is low, novelty reduces purchase intention, while incentives increase it. High source credibility makes consumer engagement more influential. Informativeness enhances purchase intention among Generation Y, whereas Generation Z is more influenced by consumer engagement. This study extends research on advertising value and consumer engagement, offering insights for brands optimizing virtual influencer marketing strategies across different consumer segments.

hot.title: Do Consumers Perceive Impulsive Buying and Pain of Payment? E-Commerce Transactions Using Pay Later, E-Wallet, and Cash-On-Delivery
hot.venue: Gadjah Mada International Journal of Business
hot.abstract: This study investigates how modern payment options, pay-later, e-wallets, and COD affect online shopping behavior, specifically on impulsive purchases and the feeling of regret after spending, known as the pain of payment. While numerous studies have individually assessed the impact of these payment modalities, there was a paucity of research examining the combined effect of these three contemporary payment methods within experimental frameworks. This study also examines whether buying groceries or fashion items influences these behaviors. The research involved 162 consumers divided into 6 groups based on the type of payment method (pay-later, e-wallet, cash-on-delivery) and type of products (grocery and fashion). The study found that the chosen payment method has no significant impact on impulsive buying behavior. However, customers are more likely to purchase fashion items impulsively than groceries. The pay-later option, especially for fashion items, led to the most impulsive buying and the strongest feeling of payment regret. On the other hand, using COD for fashion items was the least popular, and e-wallets generally led to lower overall spending. The study also found that people spend more time shopping for groceries than fashion. Both thought processes and emotions influenced the decision to buy. Interestingly, paying with COD helped improve self-control and reduce negative feelings. Based on the control theory of self-regulation, this research provides insights into managing spending and achieving customer financial goals, highlighting the connection between payment options, impulsive buying, and consumer well-being.

hot.title: The role of robo-advisors in behavioural finance, shaping investment decisions
hot.abstract: This study focuses on using artificial intelligence-driven financial robo-advisors in the investment decision-making domain by retail investors. Based on heuristic and prospect theory, the researcher aims to examine how AI-powered financial robo-advisors (AIPFRA), through their perceived interactivity, personalisation, autonomy, algorithm interpretation and structural assurance, influence retail investors’ loss aversion and overconfidence biases, ultimately enhancing robo-advisor usage in investment decision-making. Using purposive sampling, data from 461 retail investors were collected and analysed through structural equation modelling using SmartPLS 4.0. The results indicate that, except for structural assurance, robo-advisors’ perceived personalisation, interactivity, autonomy and algorithm transparency substantially mitigated investors’ overconfidence and loss-aversion biases, enhancing robo-advisor usage for investment decision-making. The study highlights the significance of financial literacy in moderating the relationship between biases and the use of robo-advisors. The study contributed by extending Heuristic and Prospect Theories to the AI-driven robo-advisor investment ecosystem. The study comprehensively explains how AI-powered robo-advisor design features impact investor psychology and adoption by bridging behavioural biases such as loss aversion and overconfidence with technology mechanisms like interactivity, personalisation, autonomy, algorithm interpretability and structural assurance. The results can help financial institutions implement user-centric advisory tools and help fintech developers create more bias-aware robo-advisors.

hot.title: From Asymmetry to Satisfaction: The Dynamic Role of Perceived Value and Trust to Boost Customer Satisfaction in the Tourism Industry
hot.abstract: The study investigates how information asymmetry affects customer satisfaction in the tourism industry by examining trust and perceived value as mediating factors. The research implements an integrated model to test and prove information asymmetry’s direct and mediating effects on customer satisfaction by examining the literature gap. The research used a quantitative approach based on opinion polls distributed to 408 customers of hotels, tourism companies, and travel agencies who were in Egypt. SmartPLS 3 software implemented the data analysis process using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Previous studies have developed scales to measure information asymmetry and its related constructs, including customer trust, perceived value, and customer satisfaction. Multiple tests showed that the measurement tools possess both reliability and validity. Results strongly support all hypotheses: information asymmetry demonstrated significant direct negative effects on customer satisfaction (β = −0.187), trust (β = −0.520), and perceived value (β = −0.453). Conversely, customer satisfaction received significant positive direct effects from both trust (β = 0.273) and perceived value (β = 0.263). Importantly, trust (indirect effect β = −0.142) and perceived value (indirect effect β = −0.119) acted as powerful mediators, confirming that information asymmetry diminishes satisfaction largely by eroding these crucial factors. Crucially, the results demonstrate that the negative impact of information asymmetry on customer satisfaction is significantly mediated jointly through two parallel pathways: the erosion of customer trust and the impairment of perceived value. The research adds theoretical support to information asymmetry theory with its findings while als

hot.title: Investigating the factors influencing customer loyalty and the mediating effect of customer satisfaction in online food delivery services: empirical evidence from an emerging market
hot.abstract: This study investigates the factors affecting customer loyalty and the mediating role of customer satisfaction in online food delivery services (OFDS) in Bangladesh. An analysis of 300 responses via structural equation modeling (SEM) revealed that perceived food and service quality alone did not significantly impact customer loyalty. While these qualities are essential, they must enhance customer satisfaction in order to boost loyalty. Significant relationships exist among perceived price, ease of payment, time efficiency, and customer loyalty, with customer satisfaction acting as a crucial mediator. Strategies focusing on pricing, payment convenience, and timely delivery are the most effective for building loyalty. The interplay between perceived quality, pricing, payment, and delivery efficiency enhances the overall customer experience. This study contributes to the literature by applying Attribution Theory and the Technological Acceptance Model (TAM), emphasizing external factors such as pricing, delivery, and payment ease as key loyalty drivers. The findings suggest that OFDS businesses should prioritize reasonable pricing, efficient payment systems, and timely delivery to foster loyalty. Combined with high-quality food and services, these strategies can enhance customer satisfaction, promote business growth, and increase revenue.

hot.title: Impulse buying in live streaming commerce: A literature review and research agenda
hot.abstract: Impulse buying in live streaming commerce (LSC) is an emerging phenomenon characterized by spontaneous, unplanned purchases driven by real-time social interactions. Despite increasing scholarly attention, the existing literature remains fragmented, lacking consensus on antecedents, theoretical perspectives, and outcomes. This fragmentation hinders theoretical development and accumulation of knowledge of this research stream. To address these issues, this study provides a systematic review of impulse buying in LSC, synthesizing key research trends, theoretical foundations, and methodological approaches. Drawing on the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework, we propose an integrative framework that consolidates antecedents, psychological mechanisms, and outcomes of impulse buying within LSC.
